name: African Union
summary: Continental organisation succeeding the OAU, with a Peace and Security Council and free-trade area.

name: Alaouite Sultanate of Morocco
summary: Sharifian dynasty that has ruled Morocco since the 17th century, surviving colonial protectorate.

name: French and Spanish Protectorates in Morocco
summary: Treaty of Fez protectorate with a Spanish zone, resisted in the Rif War and ended in 1956.

name: Green March
summary: Mass Moroccan civilian march into Spanish Sahara that secured Moroccan control.

name: Kingdom of Morocco
summary: Independent monarchy since 1956 under Mohammed V, Hassan II and Mohammed VI.

name: Rif War
summary: Abd el-Krim's republic defeated Spanish armies before falling to a Franco-Spanish offensive.

name: Belgian Colonial Africa
summary: Belgian Congo plus Ruanda-Urundi, decolonised abruptly in 1960-62.

name: British Colonial Africa
summary: British colonies and protectorates from the Cape to Egypt, decolonised mainly between 1956 and 1980.

name: Burkina Faso
summary: Independent as Upper Volta in 1960, renamed by Thomas Sankara in 1984, now facing jihadist war and coups.

name: Rule of Thomas Sankara
summary: Revolutionary leader of literacy, vaccination and anti-imperial rhetoric, assassinated in 1987.

name: Republic of Cabo Verde
summary: Atlantic island republic independent from Portugal in 1975, a stable multiparty democracy.

name: Central African Republic
summary: Independent in 1960, ruled briefly as an empire by Bokassa and repeatedly at civil war.

name: Belgian Congo
summary: Belgian state colony exploited for copper, rubber and uranium, decolonised abruptly in 1960.

name: Congo Crisis
summary: Post-independence collapse: Katangese secession, Lumumba's murder, UN intervention and Mobutu's rise.

name: Congo Free State
summary: Leopold II's personal colony whose rubber regime caused mass death and international scandal.

name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
summary: Vast mineral-rich state renamed in 1997, still troubled by conflict in its eastern provinces.

name: Republic of Equatorial Guinea
summary: Only Spanish-speaking African state, independent in 1968, oil-rich and highly repressive.

name: First Congo War
summary: Rwandan- and Ugandan-backed rebellion that overthrew Mobutu.

name: Kingdom of Kongo
summary: Christianised Central African kingdom that traded with Portugal and declined under the slave trade.

name: Rule of Mobutu Sese Seko
summary: Thirty-two years of kleptocratic rule over the country he renamed Zaire.

name: Republic of Zaire
summary: Mobutu's renamed state, ended by Kabila's rebellion in the First Congo War.

name: Ruanda-Urundi
summary: Belgian mandate then trust territory that hardened Hutu-Tutsi categories through identity cards.

name: Second Congo War
summary: Africa's world war, involving nine countries and causing millions of deaths, mostly from disease and hunger.

name: Union of the Comoros
summary: Indian Ocean state independent in 1975, with numerous coups and Mayotte remaining French.

name: Decolonisation of Africa
summary: Independence of more than fifty states, from Libya in 1951 to South Africa's democratic transition in 1994.

name: Republic of Djibouti
summary: Former French Somaliland independent in 1977, now host to multiple foreign military bases.

name: Eritrean-Ethiopian War
summary: Border war over Badme that killed tens of thousands and froze relations until 2018.

name: German East Africa
summary: German colony covering Tanganyika, Rwanda and Burundi, site of the Maji Maji rebellion.

name: Republic of Seychelles
summary: Indian Ocean archipelago independent from Britain in 1976.

name: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
summary: Ethnic-federal republic established after the Derg's fall, later shaken by the Tigray war.

name: Battle of Adwa
summary: Ethiopian defeat of an Italian army, the only decisive African victory over a European colonial power.

name: Derg
summary: Marxist military junta under Mengistu: Red Terror, famine and war with Eritrea and Somalia.

name: Ethiopian Empire
summary: Christian Solomonic empire that survived European conquest and was abolished by the Derg.

name: Ethiopian Famine of 1983-85
summary: Drought and war famine that killed several hundred thousand and prompted global relief campaigns.

name: Italian Occupation of Ethiopia
summary: Five years of Italian East Africa rule with poison gas and reprisals, ended by British and Ethiopian forces.

name: Tigray War
summary: Federal and Eritrean campaign against Tigray's regional government, with mass atrocities and famine conditions.

name: Federal Republic of Nigeria
summary: Africa's most populous state, independent in 1960, oil-rich and shaped by civil war and military rule.

name: Boko Haram Insurgency
summary: Jihadist conflict in the northeast with mass abductions and millions displaced across the Lake Chad basin.

name: Colonial Nigeria
summary: British protectorates amalgamated in 1914 and ruled through indirect rule over emirs and chiefs.

name: Kingdom of Benin (late)
summary: Powerful Edo kingdom famed for its bronzes, sacked and looted by a British punitive expedition in 1897.

name: Nigerian Civil War
summary: Biafra's secession and blockade, which killed one to two million people, mostly by starvation.

name: Nigerian Fourth Republic
summary: Civilian democracy since 1999, contending with Boko Haram, oil-delta conflict and rapid population growth.

name: Nigerian Military Rule
summary: Nearly three decades of coups and juntas, including Abacha's dictatorship, ending with the Fourth Republic.

name: Oyo Empire
summary: Yoruba cavalry empire that dominated the slave-trading coast before collapsing into civil wars.

name: French Colonial Africa
summary: French West and Equatorial Africa plus the Maghreb, mostly independent in 1960 and Algeria in 1962.

name: Gabonese Republic
summary: Oil-exporting republic independent in 1960, ruled by the Bongo family from 1967 until a 2023 coup.

name: German Colonial Africa
summary: Togo, Kamerun, South West Africa and East Africa, lost as mandates after the First World War.

name: Italian Colonial Africa
summary: Eritrea, Somalia, Libya and briefly Ethiopia, lost during the Second World War.

name: Kingdom of Eswatini
summary: Absolute monarchy independent in 1968, renamed from Swaziland in 2018.

name: Kingdom of Lesotho
summary: Mountain kingdom founded by Moshoeshoe I, a British protectorate then independent in 1966.

name: Reign of Haile Selassie
summary: Last emperor: exile under Italian occupation, postwar modernisation, OAU founding and deposition by famine and revolt.

name: Reign of Menelik II
summary: Expanded the empire southward, founded Addis Ababa and defeated Italy at Adwa.

name: Reign of Tewodros II
summary: Reunified Ethiopia after the era of princes; died resisting a British expedition at Magdala.

name: Rule of Muammar Gaddafi
summary: Forty-two years of idiosyncratic rule under the Jamahiriya, ended by uprising and NATO intervention.

name: Italian Libya
summary: Italian colony whose pacification killed a large share of the Cyrenaican population.

name: Kingdom of Libya
summary: Senussi monarchy under Idris I, independent by UN resolution and transformed by oil.

name: Libyan Civil Wars
summary: Uprising and NATO campaign that killed Gaddafi, followed by a decade of rival governments and militias.

name: Ottoman Tripolitania
summary: Ottoman and Karamanli rule over the Libyan coast, ended by the Italian invasion.

name: Organisation of African Unity
summary: Pan-African body founded in Addis Ababa that upheld colonial borders and backed liberation movements.

name: Pan-Africanism
summary: Movement for African unity and diaspora solidarity from the early congresses to Nkrumah and the AU.

name: Portuguese Colonial Africa
summary: Angola, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau, Cape Verde and Sao Tome, held until the Carnation Revolution.

name: People's Democratic Republic of Algeria
summary: Independent from France in 1962, hydrocarbon-dependent and shaped by FLN rule and the 1990s civil war.

name: Algerian Civil War
summary: War between the state and Islamist insurgents after cancelled elections, with about 150,000 to 200,000 dead.

name: Algerian War of Independence
summary: Eight-year FLN insurgency and French counterinsurgency that killed hundreds of thousands and toppled the Fourth Republic.

name: Battle of Algiers
summary: Urban campaign of bombings and systematic French torture that became emblematic of the war.

name: French Algeria
summary: Departments of France with a large settler population, ended by the war of independence.

name: French Conquest of Algeria
summary: Long, violent conquest and settlement, resisted by Abd al-Qadir and Kabyle revolts.

name: Regency of Algiers
summary: Ottoman-aligned corsair state on the Barbary coast, conquered by France in 1830.

name: Republic of Angola
summary: Oil-rich state independent from Portugal in 1975, at civil war for most of its first three decades.

name: Angolan Civil War
summary: Cold War proxy war among the MPLA, UNITA and FNLA with Cuban and South African intervention.

name: Republic of Botswana
summary: Diamond-rich republic independent in 1966, one of Africa's most durable democracies.

name: Republic of Burundi
summary: Independent in 1962, marked by mass killings in 1972 and 1993 and a long civil war.

name: Republic of Cameroon
summary: Former German then French and British territory, independent in 1960-61 and ruled by Paul Biya since 1982.

name: Republic of Chad
summary: Sahelian republic independent in 1960, with long civil wars and Libyan intervention.

name: Republic of the Congo
summary: Former French Congo independent in 1960, oil-exporting and long ruled by Denis Sassou Nguesso.

name: Arab Republic of Egypt
summary: Republic since 1953: Nasserism, wars with Israel, Sadat's peace, Mubarak's rule and the 2011 revolution.

name: Aswan High Dam
summary: Soviet-aided dam that controlled the Nile flood, created Lake Nasser and displaced Nubian communities.

name: British Occupation of Egypt
summary: Occupation after the Urabi revolt, formalised as a protectorate in 1914 and ended by the 1956 evacuation.

name: Egyptian Revolution of 1952
summary: Free Officers' coup that deposed Farouk and brought Nasser to power.

name: Egyptian Revolution of 2011
summary: Eighteen days of protest centred on Tahrir Square that forced Mubarak's resignation.

name: French Invasion of Egypt
summary: Napoleon's campaign that shattered Mamluk power, produced the Description de l'Egypte and ended in British-Ottoman victory.

name: Khedivate of Egypt
summary: Autonomous Ottoman khedivate that built the Suez Canal, went bankrupt and fell under British control.

name: Kingdom of Egypt
summary: Nominally independent monarchy under Fuad I and Farouk, dominated by Britain and ended by revolution.

name: Presidency of Hosni Mubarak
summary: Thirty years of authoritarian stability, ended by the Tahrir Square uprising.

name: Rule of Muhammad Ali of Egypt
summary: Albanian-Ottoman officer who massacred the Mamluks and built a modern army, industry and cotton economy.

name: Rule of Gamal Abdel Nasser
summary: Pan-Arab leader who nationalised the canal, built the Aswan High Dam and lost the 1967 war.

name: Ottoman Egypt
summary: Ottoman province governed by Mamluk-Ottoman elites, briefly occupied by Napoleon in 1798.

name: Presidency of Anwar Sadat
summary: Launched the 1973 war, expelled Soviet advisers, made peace with Israel and was assassinated in 1981.

name: Presidency of Abdel Fattah el-Sisi
summary: Army chief who led the 2013 coup and has ruled since 2014 with severe restrictions on dissent.

name: Opening of the Suez Canal
summary: Waterway linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea, transforming global trade and Egypt's strategic value.

name: Suez Crisis
summary: British, French and Israeli attack on Egypt after Nasser nationalised the canal, reversed by US and Soviet pressure.

name: United Arab Republic
summary: Short-lived union of Egypt and Syria under Nasser, dissolved by a Syrian coup.

name: Republic of Ghana
summary: First sub-Saharan colony to gain independence, on 6 March 1957, under Kwame Nkrumah.

name: Asante Empire
summary: Akan gold and trading empire centred on Kumasi, annexed by Britain after five wars.

name: Gold Coast
summary: British colony built on gold, cocoa and the conquest of Asante, first in sub-Saharan Africa to independence.

name: Rule of Kwame Nkrumah
summary: Pan-Africanist founding leader who built the Akosombo Dam and was overthrown by a coup in 1966.

name: Republic of Guinea
summary: Only French African colony to reject the 1958 community, independent under Sekou Toure.

name: Republic of Kenya
summary: Independent in 1963 under Jomo Kenyatta, later multiparty and shaped by the 2007-08 election violence.

name: East Africa Protectorate and Kenya Colony
summary: British colony of settler highlands, the Uganda railway and land alienation from the Kikuyu and Maasai.

name: Rule of Jomo Kenyatta
summary: Founding leader who pursued capitalist development and centralised power in KANU.

name: Mau Mau Uprising
summary: Kikuyu-led rebellion met by mass detention camps and emergency rule, hastening independence.

name: Rule of Daniel arap Moi
summary: Twenty-four-year one-party then multiparty presidency marked by patronage and repression.

name: Republic of Liberia
summary: Founded by freed American slaves and independent from 1847, later devastated by two civil wars.

name: Liberian Civil Wars
summary: Two wars involving Charles Taylor that killed about 250,000 and destabilised the region.

name: Republic of Madagascar
summary: Indian Ocean island republic independent from France in 1960.

name: Kingdom of Madagascar
summary: Merina kingdom that unified most of the island before French conquest.

name: Republic of Malawi
summary: Independent in 1964, ruled for three decades by Hastings Banda before multiparty elections.

name: Republic of Mali
summary: Sahelian republic independent in 1960, since 2012 facing jihadist insurgency and coups.

name: Mali War
summary: Tuareg and jihadist rebellion, French intervention and successive military coups.

name: Republic of Mauritius
summary: Independent in 1968 and a republic since 1992, with a diversified economy and stable democracy.

name: Republic of Mozambique
summary: Independent from Portugal in 1975 under FRELIMO, then torn by a long civil war.

name: Mozambican Civil War
summary: War between FRELIMO and RENAMO, backed by Rhodesia and South Africa, with about a million deaths.

name: Republic of Namibia
summary: Independent in 1990 after a UN-supervised transition following SWAPO's long struggle.

name: German South West Africa
summary: German colony where the Herero and Nama genocide of 1904-08 killed the majority of both peoples.

name: Herero and Nama Genocide
summary: German extermination campaign widely regarded as the twentieth century's first genocide.

name: South West Africa under South African Rule
summary: South African administration that extended apartheid and fought SWAPO's liberation war.

name: Republic of Niger
summary: Sahelian uranium-producing republic independent in 1960, with a 2023 coup ending civilian rule.

name: Republic of Rwanda
summary: Independent in 1962, site of the 1994 genocide and since then of state-led reconstruction under Paul Kagame.

name: Rule of Paul Kagame
summary: RPF leader, president since 2000, credited with development and criticised for authoritarianism.

name: Kingdom of Rwanda
summary: Tutsi-led monarchy that colonial rule reinforced before the 1959 Hutu revolution abolished it.

name: Rwandan Civil War
summary: RPF invasion and war that led to the Arusha Accords and then to genocide.

name: Rwandan Genocide
summary: Roughly 800,000 to one million Tutsi and moderate Hutu killed in about a hundred days.

name: Republic of Senegal
summary: West African republic independent in 1960, notable for stable civilian rule and Leopold Senghor's presidency.

name: Republic of South Africa
summary: Constitutional democracy since 1994, with a rights-based constitution and continuing inequality.

name: Founding of the African National Congress
summary: Formation of the movement that led the struggle against segregation and apartheid.

name: Anglo-Zulu War
summary: British invasion of Zululand, defeated at Isandlwana before winning at Ulundi.

name: Apartheid
summary: National Party system of racial classification, pass laws, bantustans and forced removals.

name: British Cape Colony
summary: British colony that abolished slavery, fought frontier wars and expanded north with diamonds and gold.

name: Dutch Cape Colony
summary: VOC settlement at the Cape whose expansion dispossessed Khoikhoi and San and imported slaves.

name: Great Trek
summary: Boer migration inland from the Cape that founded the Transvaal and Orange Free State republics.

name: Presidency of Nelson Mandela
summary: First democratically elected president, who pursued reconciliation and a new constitution.

name: Presidency of Thabo Mbeki
summary: Growth, African Renaissance diplomacy and controversy over HIV/AIDS policy.

name: South African Mineral Revolution
summary: Diamond and Witwatersrand gold discoveries that industrialised the region and created migrant labour systems.

name: Natives Land Act
summary: Law restricting African land ownership to about 7 percent of the country, the basis of later dispossession.

name: Presidency of Cyril Ramaphosa
summary: President since 2018, facing energy shortages, corruption inquiries and coalition politics after 2024.

name: Republic of South Africa (apartheid era)
summary: Republic that left the Commonwealth in 1961 and faced sanctions, township revolt and regional wars.

name: Rivonia Trial
summary: Trial that sentenced Nelson Mandela and co-accused to life imprisonment.

name: Second Anglo-Boer War
summary: British conquest of the Boer republics using scorched earth and concentration camps.

name: Sharpeville Massacre
summary: Police killing of 69 anti-pass protesters, after which the ANC and PAC were banned and turned to armed struggle.

name: South African Election of 1994
summary: First universal-franchise election, won by the ANC, making Nelson Mandela president.

name: South African Negotiated Transition
summary: Mandela's release, unbanning of the ANC and CODESA talks that produced non-racial elections.

name: South African Republic and Orange Free State
summary: Boer republics of the Transvaal and Free State, annexed by Britain after the Second Anglo-Boer War.

name: South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission
summary: Tutu-chaired hearings on apartheid-era crimes, offering amnesty for full disclosure.

name: Soweto Uprising
summary: Student protest against Afrikaans instruction met with police fire, igniting a new phase of resistance.

name: Union of South Africa
summary: Self-governing dominion uniting four colonies with a whites-only franchise, forerunner of apartheid.

name: Presidency of Jacob Zuma
summary: Presidency marked by state capture scandals and economic stagnation, ended by ANC pressure.

name: Republic of the Sudan
summary: Independent in 1956, marked by two civil wars, Darfur, Bashir's rule and renewed war from 2023.

name: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan
summary: Condominium administered largely by Britain, which governed the south separately.

name: Rule of Omar al-Bashir
summary: Islamist military ruler indicted by the ICC, overthrown by protests and the army in 2019.

name: Darfur Conflict
summary: Government and Janjaweed campaign against Darfuri rebels and civilians, described as genocide.

name: First Sudanese Civil War
summary: North-south conflict ended by the Addis Ababa Agreement's autonomy for the south.

name: Mahdist State
summary: Islamic state founded after the fall of Khartoum, destroyed by Kitchener at Omdurman.

name: Second Sudanese Civil War
summary: Twenty-two-year war with the SPLA that killed some two million and ended in a peace deal.

name: Sudanese Civil War of 2023
summary: War between the army and the Rapid Support Forces that produced the world's largest displacement crisis.

name: Republic of Tunisia
summary: Independent republic under Bourguiba then Ben Ali, birthplace of the Arab Spring.

name: Rule of Habib Bourguiba
summary: Founding president who secularised law and advanced women's rights before being deposed for senility.

name: French Protectorate of Tunisia
summary: Protectorate established by the Treaty of Bardo, ended by Neo Destour's independence campaign.

name: Husainid Beylik of Tunis
summary: Dynasty that ruled Tunisia under Ottoman then French suzerainty until the republic.

name: Tunisian Revolution
summary: Protests after Mohamed Bouazizi's self-immolation that ousted Ben Ali and began the Arab Spring.

name: Republic of Uganda
summary: Independent in 1962, ravaged under Amin and Obote, ruled by Yoweri Museveni since 1986.

name: Rule of Idi Amin
summary: Brutal dictatorship that expelled Uganda's Asians and killed hundreds of thousands, ended by Tanzanian invasion.

name: Kingdom of Buganda
summary: Powerful lacustrine kingdom, the core of the Uganda Protectorate, abolished in 1966 and restored in 1993.

name: Uganda Protectorate
summary: British protectorate ruled indirectly through Buganda's institutions.

name: Republic of Zambia
summary: Copper-exporting republic independent in 1964 under Kenneth Kaunda.

name: Republic of Zimbabwe
summary: Independent in 1980 under Robert Mugabe, later hit by land seizures and hyperinflation.

name: Rule of Robert Mugabe
summary: Thirty-seven years in power: Gukurahundi massacres, land reform and economic collapse, ended by a coup.

name: Rhodesian Bush War
summary: Liberation war by ZANLA and ZIPRA that forced the Lancaster House settlement.

name: Rhodesian Unilateral Declaration of Independence
summary: Ian Smith's white minority government declared independence, triggering sanctions and guerrilla war.

name: Southern Rhodesia
summary: Self-governing British settler colony named for Cecil Rhodes, based on land alienation and white minority rule.

name: Sao Tome and Principe
summary: Atlantic island republic independent from Portugal in 1975.

name: Somali Republic
summary: Union of British and Italian Somaliland in 1960, collapsed into statelessness after 1991.

name: Rule of Siad Barre
summary: Military socialist regime that fought the Ogaden War and fell to clan-based rebellion.

name: Somali Civil War
summary: State collapse, famine, US and UN interventions, Islamist insurgency and al-Shabaab.

name: Republic of Somaliland
summary: Self-declared unrecognised state in the northwest with relative stability and its own institutions.

name: Republic of South Sudan
summary: World's newest widely recognised state, independent by referendum in 2011 and soon at civil war.

name: Mfecane
summary: Period of upheaval, migration and state formation across southern Africa associated with Zulu expansion.

name: State of Eritrea
summary: Independent by referendum in 1993, ruled since by Isaias Afwerki without elections.

name: Eritrean War of Independence
summary: Thirty-year struggle against Ethiopian rule won by the EPLF in 1991.

name: Togolese Republic
summary: Former German then French territory independent in 1960, ruled by the Gnassingbe family since 1967.

name: Indian Ocean and Trans-Saharan Slave Trades
summary: Long-running slave trades across the Sahara and Indian Ocean, ended by gradual abolition and colonial rule.

name: United Republic of Tanzania
summary: Union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, shaped by Nyerere's ujamaa socialism and later liberalisation.

name: Maji Maji Rebellion
summary: Mass revolt against German rule crushed by famine tactics with perhaps 250,000 deaths.

name: Rule of Julius Nyerere
summary: Founding president whose ujamaa villagisation failed economically but built national unity and literacy.

name: Tanganyika
summary: British mandate then trust territory, independent in 1961 and united with Zanzibar in 1964.

name: Republic of Guinea-Bissau
summary: Independent after Amilcar Cabral's PAIGC war against Portugal.

name: Mali Federation
summary: Short-lived union of Senegal and French Sudan that split within months of independence.

name: Islamic Republic of Mauritania
summary: Saharan republic independent in 1960, which formally abolished slavery only in 1981.

name: Republic of Benin
summary: Independent as Dahomey in 1960, Marxist from 1975 to 1990 and a pioneer of African democratic transition.

name: Republic of Cote d'Ivoire
summary: Cocoa-exporting republic independent in 1960 under Houphouet-Boigny, later split by civil war.

name: Republic of Sierra Leone
summary: Founded as a settlement for freed slaves, independent in 1961 and scarred by a diamond-fuelled civil war.

name: Sierra Leone Civil War
summary: Brutal war involving the RUF and blood diamonds, ended by British and UN intervention.

name: Fall of the Songhai Empire
summary: Moroccan musketeers defeated Songhai at Tondibi, ending the last great Sahelian empire.

name: Republic of The Gambia
summary: Small riverine state independent in 1965, ruled by Yahya Jammeh from 1994 to 2017.

name: Western Sahara Conflict
summary: Moroccan annexation after Spanish withdrawal, contested by the Polisario Front and a stalled UN referendum.

name: Year of Africa
summary: Seventeen African countries became independent in 1960, transforming the United Nations.

name: Argentine Republic
summary: Federal republic constituted in 1853, transformed by mass European immigration and the grain and beef export boom.

name: Argentine Economic Crisis of 2001
summary: Default, corralito bank freeze and five presidents in two weeks.

name: Conquest of the Desert
summary: Military campaigns that seized Indigenous Patagonian lands and opened them to settlement.

name: Argentine Dirty War
summary: Military junta's campaign of disappearances that killed up to 30,000 people.

name: Argentine Declaration of Independence
summary: Congress of Tucuman declared independence from Spain on 9 July 1816.

name: Falklands War
summary: Argentine invasion of the Falklands defeated by Britain, precipitating the junta's collapse.

name: May Revolution
summary: Buenos Aires cabildo abierto deposed the viceroy, beginning Argentine self-government.

name: Peronism
summary: Mass movement founded by Juan and Eva Peron combining labour rights, nationalism and personalist leadership.

name: Rule of Juan Manuel de Rosas
summary: Federalist caudillo who dominated the Argentine Confederation until defeat at Caseros.

name: United Provinces of the Rio de la Plata
summary: Post-revolutionary confederation that declared independence at Tucuman in 1816 amid unitarian-federalist civil war.

name: Commonwealth of The Bahamas
summary: Archipelagic state independent from Britain in 1973.

name: Barbados
summary: Independent since 1966 and a republic since 2021, once a model English sugar colony.

name: Belize
summary: Former British Honduras, independent in 1981, the only English-speaking state in Central America.

name: Bourbon Reforms
summary: Administrative, fiscal and military reforms that increased extraction and provoked creole resentment and revolt.

name: Federative Republic of Brazil
summary: Democratic Brazil under the 1988 constitution, with the Real Plan, commodity boom and impeachment crises.

name: Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro
summary: Right-wing populist presidency marked by Amazon deforestation, COVID-19 denial and the 2023 Brasilia riot.

name: First Brazilian Republic
summary: Oligarchic 'coffee with milk' republic of Sao Paulo and Minas elites, ended by Vargas's revolution.

name: Minas Gerais Gold Rush
summary: Gold and diamond boom that shifted Brazil's centre south and funded Portuguese and British commerce.

name: Golden Law
summary: Abolition of slavery in Brazil, the last country in the Americas to end it.

name: Brazilian Independence
summary: Pedro I's Grito do Ipiranga on 7 September 1822 declared independence, achieved with little bloodshed.

name: Brazilian Military Dictatorship
summary: Twenty-one years of army rule with censorship, torture and the 'economic miracle', ending in a gradual opening.

name: Brazilian Second Republic
summary: Democratic period of developmentalism, the building of Brasilia and mounting political crisis.

name: Portuguese Landing in Brazil
summary: Pedro Alvares Cabral reached the Brazilian coast in April 1500, claiming it for Portugal.

name: Colonial Brazil
summary: Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold and enslaved African labour, with its capital at Salvador then Rio.

name: Dutch Brazil
summary: Dutch West India Company colony in Pernambuco under Johan Maurits, expelled by Luso-Brazilian forces.

name: Empire of Brazil
summary: Constitutional monarchy of the Americas under Pedro I and Pedro II, which abolished slavery and fell to a coup.

name: Reign of Pedro I of Brazil
summary: Founder of the empire who granted the 1824 constitution and abdicated to claim the Portuguese throne.

name: Reign of Pedro II of Brazil
summary: Long, stable reign of a scholar-emperor: the Paraguayan War, coffee expansion, abolition and deposition.

name: Estado Novo (Brazil)
summary: Vargas's corporatist dictatorship, which nonetheless joined the Allies in 1942.

name: Founding of Brasilia
summary: Kubitschek's modernist capital inaugurated in the interior, designed by Costa and Niemeyer.

name: Presidencies of Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
summary: Trade-unionist president 2003-2010 and again from 2023: Bolsa Familia, poverty reduction and diplomatic prominence.

name: Plano Real
summary: Currency stabilisation plan that ended hyperinflation and introduced the real.

name: Quilombo dos Palmares
summary: Large maroon polity of escaped enslaved people in Alagoas, destroyed after decades of resistance under Zumbi.

name: Impeachment of Dilma Rousseff
summary: Brazil's first woman president removed amid recession and the Lava Jato corruption investigation.

name: Transfer of the Portuguese Court to Brazil
summary: The royal family fled Napoleon to Rio, opening Brazilian ports and elevating the colony.

name: United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves
summary: Transatlantic kingdom in which Brazil was legally equal to Portugal.

name: Vargas Era
summary: Getulio Vargas ruled by revolution then dictatorship, creating labour laws, industry and the Estado Novo.

name: Abolition of Slavery in the Caribbean
summary: Successive emancipations from Haiti and the British colonies to Cuba, ending Atlantic plantation slavery.

name: Caribbean Community
summary: Regional integration organisation founded by the Treaty of Chaguaramas.

name: Chaco War
summary: Bolivia-Paraguay war over the Gran Chaco, won largely by Paraguay at great cost to both.

name: Congress of Panama
summary: Bolivar's attempt at a league of American republics, an ancestor of Pan-Americanism.

name: Dominican Republic
summary: Independent from Haiti in 1844, later occupied by the United States and ruled by Trujillo for three decades.

name: Trujillo Dictatorship
summary: Rafael Trujillo's cult-of-personality regime, responsible for the 1937 Parsley Massacre of Haitians.

name: Canada
summary: Federal dominion of 1867 that grew to ten provinces and three territories and became fully sovereign by stages.

name: Expulsion of the Acadians
summary: British deportation of some 10,000 French-speaking Acadians from the Maritimes.

name: Creation of Alberta and Saskatchewan
summary: Two new prairie provinces carved from the North-West Territories.

name: British Columbia Joins Canada
summary: BC entered Confederation on the promise of a transcontinental railway.

name: Canada in the First World War
summary: More than 600,000 served; Vimy Ridge and the conscription crisis shaped national identity.

name: Completion of the Canadian Pacific Railway
summary: Last spike at Craigellachie linked Canada by rail, built largely by Chinese labourers.

name: Canadian Indian Residential School System
summary: Church-run, state-funded schools that forcibly assimilated Indigenous children, with thousands of deaths.

name: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada
summary: Inquiry into residential schools that documented cultural genocide against Indigenous peoples.

name: Jacques Cartier's Voyages
summary: Three French voyages that claimed the St Lawrence for France and named Canada.

name: Constitution Act, 1982
summary: Patriation of the constitution with the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, without Quebec's consent.

name: Hudson's Bay Company
summary: Royal-chartered fur-trade company that governed Rupert's Land until selling it to Canada in 1870.

name: Manitoba Joins Canada
summary: Manitoba entered Confederation as the fifth province after the Red River Resistance.

name: Newfoundland Joins Canada
summary: Newfoundland became Canada's tenth province after two close referendums.

name: North-West Rebellion
summary: Metis and Cree resistance led by Riel and Big Bear, defeated and followed by Riel's execution.

name: Creation of Nunavut
summary: New Inuit-majority territory established from the eastern Northwest Territories.

name: October Crisis
summary: FLQ kidnappings and the murder of Pierre Laporte led Trudeau to invoke the War Measures Act.

name: Prince Edward Island Joins Canada
summary: PEI entered Confederation in 1873, burdened by railway debt.

name: Premiership of Alexander Mackenzie
summary: Liberal prime minister who created the Supreme Court and the secret ballot.

name: Premiership of Arthur Meighen
summary: Conservative prime minister in 1920-21 and briefly in 1926 during the King-Byng affair.

name: Premiership of Brian Mulroney
summary: Free trade with the United States, the GST, failed Meech Lake and Charlottetown accords, and anti-apartheid diplomacy.

name: Premiership of Charles Tupper
summary: Shortest-serving Canadian prime minister, in office 69 days.

name: Premiership of Jean Chretien
summary: Deficit elimination, the 1995 referendum and the Clarity Act, and refusal to join the Iraq war.

name: Premiership of Joe Clark
summary: Nine-month Progressive Conservative minority government defeated on its budget.

name: Premiership of John A. Macdonald
summary: First prime minister (1867-73, 1878-91): Confederation, the CPR, the National Policy and the Riel executions.

name: Premiership of John Abbott
summary: Conservative caretaker prime minister after Macdonald's death.

name: Premiership of John Diefenbaker
summary: Prairie Conservative: the Bill of Rights, Indigenous voting rights and the Avro Arrow cancellation.

name: Premiership of John Thompson
summary: Prime minister who codified the Criminal Code and died in office at Windsor Castle.

name: Premiership of John Turner
summary: Liberal prime minister for 79 days before a landslide defeat.

name: Premiership of Justin Trudeau
summary: Liberal prime minister: cannabis legalisation, carbon pricing, USMCA and the COVID-19 response.

name: Premiership of Kim Campbell
summary: Canada's first woman prime minister, in office for about four months.

name: Premiership of Lester Pearson
summary: Nobel peace laureate whose minority governments created medicare, the maple leaf flag and the Canada Pension Plan.

name: Premiership of Louis St-Laurent
summary: 'Uncle Louis' oversaw NATO membership, Newfoundland's entry and the St Lawrence Seaway.

name: Premiership of Mackenzie Bowell
summary: Prime minister brought down by cabinet revolt over the Manitoba schools question.

name: Premiership of William Lyon Mackenzie King
summary: Longest-serving prime minister in the Commonwealth: Depression, wartime leadership and the welfare state's start.

name: Premiership of Mark Carney
summary: Former central banker who became Liberal leader and prime minister in 2025.

name: Premiership of Paul Martin
summary: Prime minister who legalised same-sex marriage nationally and faced the sponsorship scandal.

name: Premiership of Pierre Trudeau
summary: Prime minister 1968-79 and 1980-84: bilingualism, multiculturalism, the October Crisis and patriation with the Charter.

name: Premiership of R. B. Bennett
summary: Depression-era Conservative prime minister who created the Bank of Canada and the CBC's predecessor.

name: Premiership of Robert Borden
summary: Wartime prime minister: conscription crisis, Union government and a separate Canadian seat at Versailles.

name: Premiership of Stephen Harper
summary: Conservative prime minister through the 2008 crisis, the residential schools apology and Afghan combat operations.

name: Premiership of Wilfrid Laurier
summary: First francophone prime minister: immigration boom, two new provinces and compromise on imperial questions.

name: Province of Canada
summary: United colony of Canada East and West that won responsible government in 1848.

name: Province of Quebec (British)
summary: British colony where the Quebec Act of 1774 guaranteed French civil law and Catholic rights.

name: Quebec Referendum of 1980
summary: Sovereignty-association rejected by 60 percent of Quebec voters.

name: Quebec Referendum of 1995
summary: Sovereignty narrowly defeated by 50.6 to 49.4 percent.

name: Rebellions of 1837-38
summary: Patriote and Upper Canadian revolts for responsible government, suppressed but leading to the Durham Report.

name: Red River Resistance
summary: Louis Riel's Metis provisional government, which led to Manitoba's creation as a province.

name: Statute of Westminster
summary: British act recognising the legislative independence of the dominions.

name: Upper and Lower Canada
summary: Two colonies created by the Constitutional Act, each with an elected assembly, joined after the 1837 rebellions.

name: War of 1812 in Canada
summary: American invasions repelled by British regulars, Canadian militia and Indigenous allies under Tecumseh and Brock.

name: French Guiana
summary: French territory and now overseas department, once a penal colony and now home to the Kourou spaceport.

name: Gran Colombia
summary: Bolivar's union of Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama, dissolved by regional rivalries.

name: Jamaica
summary: Former Spanish then British sugar colony, independent within the Commonwealth since 1962.

name: British Jamaica
summary: English conquest of 1655 created a plantation colony with maroon wars and the 1865 Morant Bay rebellion.

name: Presidency of Lazaro Cardenas
summary: Land redistribution, support for Spanish republicans and the 1938 nationalisation of oil as Pemex.

name: Cristero War
summary: Catholic rural rebellion against anticlerical enforcement, settled by negotiated modus vivendi.

name: First Mexican Empire
summary: Agustin de Iturbide's brief empire, which included Central America.

name: First Mexican Republic
summary: Federal republic under the 1824 constitution, riven by centralist-federalist conflict.

name: Presidency of Benito Juarez
summary: Zapotec liberal who led resistance to the French intervention and restored the republic.

name: La Reforma
summary: Liberal reforms under Juarez that curbed church and army privilege and produced the 1857 constitution.

name: Mexican Constitution of 1917
summary: Landmark constitution establishing land reform, labour rights and state ownership of subsoil resources.

name: Mexican Democratic Transition
summary: Vicente Fox's victory ended 71 years of PRI presidential rule.

name: Mexican Drug War
summary: Militarised campaign against cartels launched by Felipe Calderon, with well over 300,000 dead.

name: Mexican Oil Expropriation
summary: Cardenas nationalised foreign oil companies and created Pemex, a founding act of economic sovereignty.

name: Mexican Peso Crisis
summary: Currency collapse and US-led bailout known as the Tequila Crisis.

name: Mexican Revolution
summary: Decade of civil war involving Madero, Villa, Zapata, Carranza and Obregon, costing perhaps a million lives.

name: Mexican War of Independence
summary: Eleven-year struggle begun by Hidalgo's Grito de Dolores and completed by Iturbide's Plan of Iguala.

name: Porfiriato
summary: Porfirio Diaz's 35-year rule: railways, foreign investment and repression, ended by the Revolution.

name: Presidency of Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador
summary: Leftist president who built Morena's dominance and expanded social programmes and military infrastructure roles.

name: Presidency of Claudia Sheinbaum
summary: Mexico's first woman president, elected in 2024 as AMLO's successor.

name: Rule of the Institutional Revolutionary Party
summary: Single dominant party governed Mexico for 71 years under a rotating presidential system.

name: War of the Reform
summary: Civil war between liberals and conservatives won by Juarez's liberals.

name: Era of Santa Anna
summary: Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna held the presidency eleven times amid the loss of Texas and the war with the United States.

name: Second Mexican Empire
summary: French-imposed empire of Maximilian of Habsburg, which collapsed when France withdrew; he was executed at Queretaro.

name: Spanish Conquest of the Aztec Empire
summary: Cortes and Indigenous allies destroyed Tenochtitlan, beginning Spanish rule in Mesoamerica.

name: Tlatelolco Massacre
summary: Army killing of student protesters in Mexico City days before the Olympics.

name: United Mexican States
summary: Federal republic of 31 states and a capital, Latin America's second-largest economy.

name: Zapatista Uprising
summary: EZLN indigenous rebellion in Chiapas launched as NAFTA took effect.

name: Federal Republic of Central America
summary: Union of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica that fragmented into five states.

name: Abenaki
summary: Algonquian nation of northern New England and Quebec, part of the Wabanaki Confederacy.

name: Adena Culture
summary: Ohio Valley mound-building culture known for conical burial mounds and elaborate grave goods.

name: Unangax (Aleut)
summary: Peoples of the Aleutian Islands, enslaved and decimated under Russian fur-trade rule and interned by the US during World War II.

name: Apache Nations
summary: Southern Athabaskan peoples including Chiricahua, Mescalero, Jicarilla and Western Apache of the Southwest.

name: Chiricahua Apache
summary: Apache band led at various times by Cochise, Victorio and Geronimo, whose resistance ended with imprisonment in Florida and Oklahoma.

name: Arapaho
summary: Algonquian Plains nation allied with the Cheyenne and Lakota, now the Northern Arapaho of Wyoming and Southern Arapaho of Oklahoma.

name: Archaic Period
summary: Long era of diversified foraging, regional adaptation and early plant domestication before widespread pottery and farming.

name: Blackfoot Confederacy
summary: Alliance of Piikani, Kainai and Siksika nations on the northern Plains, with the Blackfeet Nation in Montana today.

name: California Mission System
summary: Chain of twenty-one Franciscan missions that coerced Indigenous labour and conversion in Alta California until Mexican secularisation.

name: California Republic
summary: Brief settler rebellion republic proclaimed at Sonoma during the Bear Flag Revolt, absorbed into US forces within weeks.

name: Cherokee Nation
summary: Iroquoian-speaking southeastern nation that adopted a written constitution and Sequoyah's syllabary, was forcibly removed on the Trail of Tears, and today is the largest US tribal nation.

name: Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians
summary: Federally recognised Cherokee community in western North Carolina descended from those who avoided removal.

name: Cheyenne
summary: Algonquian Plains nation of the Northern and Southern divisions, central to the Plains wars and the Sand Creek and Washita attacks.

name: Chickasaw Nation
summary: Muskogean nation of northern Mississippi and western Tennessee, removed to Indian Territory and sovereign today.

name: Chinook
summary: Lower Columbia River peoples who dominated Northwest trade and gave their name to the Chinook Jargon trade language.

name: Choctaw Nation
summary: Muskogean nation of Mississippi, first removed under the 1830 Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek; sovereign today in southeastern Oklahoma.

name: Chumash
summary: Maritime people of the southern California coast and Channel Islands, known for tomol plank canoes and shell-bead money.

name: Clovis Culture
summary: Widespread early Paleo-Indian tradition identified by distinctive fluted spear points found across North America.

name: Bacon's Rebellion
summary: Backcountry uprising in Virginia against Governor Berkeley and Indigenous neighbours, which hastened the shift to racialised slavery.

name: British North America
summary: English and later British colonial holdings in North America, from Jamestown to the Treaty of Paris that recognised American independence.

name: Colony of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations
summary: Colony founded by Roger Williams on religious liberty and separation of church and state.

name: Colony of Virginia
summary: Oldest of the thirteen colonies, built on tobacco, enslaved labour and the House of Burgesses.

name: Connecticut Colony
summary: Puritan colony governed under the Fundamental Orders, one of the earliest written constitutions in the colonies.

name: Delaware Colony
summary: Lower counties on the Delaware, held under Penn's proprietorship with a separate assembly from 1704.

name: Dominion of New England
summary: Short-lived consolidation of the northern colonies under Governor Andros, overthrown after England's Glorious Revolution.

name: Arrival of the First Africans in Virginia
summary: About twenty captive Africans were sold at Point Comfort, beginning African bondage in English North America.

name: First Great Awakening
summary: Wave of evangelical revival led by Whitefield, Edwards and Tennent that reshaped colonial religion and undermined established churches.

name: French and Indian War
summary: North American theatre of the Seven Years' War in which Britain and its colonists conquered New France, ended by the Treaty of Paris.

name: House of Burgesses
summary: First elected legislative assembly in English America, meeting in Virginia.

name: Jamestown
summary: First permanent English settlement in North America, on the James River in Virginia; survived starvation to become the tobacco colony's capital.

name: King George's War
summary: North American theatre of the War of the Austrian Succession, including the capture and return of Louisbourg.

name: King Philip's War
summary: Devastating war between New England colonists and Wampanoag, Narragansett and Nipmuc forces under Metacom.

name: King William's War
summary: First of the intercolonial wars between English and French colonists and their Indigenous allies.

name: Massachusetts Bay Colony
summary: Puritan colony centred on Boston founded during the Great Migration, notable for congregational churches and Harvard College.

name: Mayflower Compact
summary: Self-government agreement signed by Mayflower passengers before landing, an early instance of consent-based colonial rule.

name: New Haven Colony
summary: Strict Puritan colony on Long Island Sound, absorbed into Connecticut in 1665.

name: New Netherland
summary: Dutch colony on the Hudson and Delaware rivers centred on New Amsterdam, conquered by England in 1664 and ceded in 1667.

name: New Sweden
summary: Small Swedish colony on the lower Delaware River, absorbed by New Netherland in 1655.

name: Pequot War
summary: War in Connecticut in which English colonists and allies destroyed the Pequot, including the Mystic massacre.

name: Plymouth Colony
summary: Separatist Pilgrim colony founded after the Mayflower voyage and governed by the Mayflower Compact; merged into Massachusetts in 1691.

name: Pontiac's War
summary: Pan-Indigenous uprising in the Great Lakes against British rule after the French defeat, prompting the Proclamation of 1763.

name: Royal Proclamation of 1763
summary: British order barring colonial settlement west of the Appalachians, a grievance for land-hungry colonists.

name: Province of Carolina
summary: Original proprietary grant covering the later Carolinas, governed under the Fundamental Constitutions.

name: Province of Georgia
summary: Last of the thirteen colonies, founded by Oglethorpe as a debtors' refuge and military buffer against Spanish Florida.

name: Province of Maryland
summary: Proprietary colony granted to the Calverts as a Catholic refuge, home of the 1649 Act of Toleration.

name: Province of Massachusetts Bay
summary: Royal province combining Massachusetts Bay, Plymouth and Maine; the epicentre of revolutionary resistance.

name: Province of New Hampshire
summary: Northern New England colony of fishing, timber and shipbuilding, long entangled with Massachusetts.

name: Province of New Jersey
summary: Colony divided into East and West Jersey before reuniting as a royal province in 1702.

name: Province of New York
summary: Former New Netherland granted to the Duke of York, a diverse commercial colony centred on New York City.

name: Province of North Carolina
summary: Southern colony of small farms, naval stores and backcountry settlement, split from Carolina in 1712.

name: Province of Pennsylvania
summary: Quaker colony founded by William Penn on religious tolerance and fair dealing with the Lenape; Philadelphia became the largest colonial city.

name: Province of South Carolina
summary: Rice and indigo colony with a Black majority population, centred on Charles Town.

name: Queen Anne's War
summary: North American theatre of the War of the Spanish Succession, ending with British gains at Utrecht.

name: Roanoke Colony
summary: Failed English settlement off North Carolina whose second group of colonists vanished, remembered as the Lost Colony.

name: Salem Witch Trials
summary: Mass witchcraft panic in Essex County, Massachusetts, that executed twenty people and imprisoned scores more.

name: Stono Rebellion
summary: Largest slave revolt in the British mainland colonies, in South Carolina, followed by a harsh Negro Act.

name: Thirteen Colonies
summary: The British colonies on the Atlantic seaboard from New Hampshire to Georgia that united to form the United States.

name: Voyages of Columbus
summary: Four Spanish-sponsored crossings that initiated sustained European contact with the Americas.

name: Comanche Nation
summary: Equestrian power that dominated the southern Plains from the 18th century, checking Spanish, Mexican and Texan expansion until the 1870s.

name: Confederate States of America
summary: Breakaway slaveholding republic of eleven southern states, defeated by the Union in the Civil War and dissolved in 1865.

name: Coronado Expedition
summary: Spanish expedition across the Southwest and Plains in search of Cibola, the first European contact for many Indigenous nations.

name: Crow Nation
summary: Plains nation of Montana, frequent US allies against the Lakota, sovereign on the Crow Reservation today.

name: De Soto Expedition
summary: Spanish march through the Southeast that described late Mississippian societies and spread devastating disease.

name: Five Tribes of Indian Territory
summary: Cherokee, Choctaw, Chickasaw, Muscogee and Seminole nations relocated to Indian Territory, later reorganised as sovereign governments in Oklahoma.

name: Folsom Culture
summary: Paleo-Indian bison-hunting tradition of the Great Plains known for thin fluted points.

name: North American Fur Trade
summary: Continental commerce in beaver and other pelts that structured Indigenous-European relations and drove exploration.

name: Ghost Dance Movement
summary: Revitalisation religion spread by the Paiute prophet Wovoka, whose growth among the Lakota preceded the Wounded Knee massacre.

name: Great Sioux Nation
summary: Oceti Sakowin, the Seven Council Fires uniting Lakota, Dakota and Nakota peoples across the northern Plains.

name: Dakota
summary: Eastern Sioux peoples of Minnesota and the Dakotas, forced from Minnesota after the 1862 war.

name: Haida
summary: Northwest Coast nation of Haida Gwaii and southern Alaska, celebrated for monumental cedar carving and canoes.

name: Beaver Wars
summary: Prolonged Iroquois campaigns for control of the fur trade that shattered Huron, Erie and other nations in the Great Lakes.

name: Cayuga Nation
summary: Haudenosaunee nation of the Finger Lakes region of New York.

name: Mohawk Nation
summary: Easternmost Haudenosaunee nation, 'keepers of the eastern door', in the Mohawk Valley and later Quebec and Ontario.

name: Oneida Nation
summary: Haudenosaunee nation of central New York that largely sided with the Americans in the Revolution.

name: Onondaga Nation
summary: Haudenosaunee nation that hosts the Grand Council fire as the confederacy's capital.

name: Seneca Nation
summary: Largest Haudenosaunee nation, 'keepers of the western door', in western New York.

name: Tuscarora Nation
summary: Iroquoian nation originally of North Carolina that migrated north and became the sixth nation of the confederacy in 1722.

name: Ho-Chunk
summary: Siouan-speaking nation of Wisconsin, repeatedly removed but returned to their homeland.

name: Hohokam
summary: Southwestern culture of the Sonoran Desert notable for extensive irrigation canals, ballcourts and platform mounds.

name: Hopewell Tradition
summary: Woodland culture of the Ohio and Mississippi valleys famed for geometric earthworks and a continental exchange network.

name: Wendat Confederacy
summary: Iroquoian confederacy of the Great Lakes, dispersed by Iroquois attacks and epidemics in 1649-50.

name: Inupiat and Yupik Peoples
summary: Arctic and subarctic peoples of Alaska descended from the Thule tradition, sustained by marine hunting.

name: Kingdom of Hawaii
summary: Unified Hawaiian monarchy founded by Kamehameha I, overthrown in 1893 and annexed by the United States in 1898.

name: Kiowa
summary: Southern Plains nation allied with the Comanche, confined to a reservation after the Red River War.

name: Lakota
summary: Westernmost Sioux division of seven bands, dominant horse-and-bison power of the northern Plains and victors at Little Bighorn.

name: Lenape
summary: Algonquian nation of the Delaware valley whose lands became New Jersey, Pennsylvania and New York, later removed to Oklahoma and Ontario.

name: Miami Tribe
summary: Algonquian nation of the Wabash valley led by Little Turtle in the Northwest Indian War.

name: Cahokia
summary: Largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico, near modern St. Louis, with Monks Mound and perhaps 15,000-20,000 residents at its height.

name: Moundville
summary: Major Mississippian centre on the Black Warrior River in Alabama with twenty-nine mounds around a plaza.

name: Mogollon Culture
summary: Southwestern culture of southern New Mexico and Arizona, including the Mimbres tradition's painted pottery.

name: Mohegan
summary: Connecticut Algonquian nation that split from the Pequot under Uncas and is federally recognised today.

name: Muscogee (Creek) Nation
summary: Southeastern confederacy of towns in Georgia and Alabama, removed to Indian Territory and now a large sovereign nation in Oklahoma.

name: Narragansett
summary: Algonquian nation of Rhode Island, devastated in King Philip's War and federally recognised in 1983.

name: Natchez
summary: Last major Mississippian-descended chiefdom, ruled by the Great Sun on the lower Mississippi, dispersed by the French after 1729.

name: Navajo Nation
summary: Largest Native American reservation and one of the largest tribal nations, spanning Arizona, New Mexico and Utah; endured the 1864 Long Walk.

name: Long Walk of the Navajo
summary: Forced march of thousands of Navajo to Bosque Redondo internment, where many died before the 1868 treaty allowed return.

name: New France
summary: French colonial empire in North America including Canada, Acadia and Louisiana, ceded to Britain and Spain in 1763.

name: Founding of Quebec City
summary: Samuel de Champlain established the habitation at Quebec, the permanent base of New France.

name: Nez Perce
summary: Plateau nation of Idaho, Oregon and Washington, renowned horse breeders led in 1877 by Chief Joseph.

name: Norse Settlement of Vinland
summary: Short-lived Norse presence in northeastern North America, archaeologically confirmed at L'Anse aux Meadows.

name: Ohlone
summary: Peoples of the San Francisco and Monterey bay areas, devastated by the Spanish mission system.

name: Ojibwe
summary: Large Algonquian nation of the western Great Lakes with many US and Canadian communities, known for wild rice harvesting and birchbark scrolls.

name: Osage Nation
summary: Dhegihan Siouan nation that dominated the Ozarks and later grew wealthy and was preyed upon during the Oklahoma oil boom.

name: Paiute
summary: Numic peoples of the Great Basin, divided into Northern, Southern and Owens Valley groups, origin of the Ghost Dance prophet Wovoka.

name: Paleo-Indian Period
summary: Earliest human occupation of the Americas, associated with big-game hunting and fluted-point traditions.

name: Pawnee Nation
summary: Caddoan farming and hunting nation of the Platte valley in Nebraska, later removed to Oklahoma.

name: Pequot
summary: Algonquian nation of southeastern Connecticut nearly destroyed in the Pequot War; the Mashantucket Pequot survive today.

name: Potawatomi
summary: Algonquian nation of the Great Lakes, part of the Council of Three Fires, removed in the 1838 Trail of Death.

name: Poverty Point Culture
summary: Late Archaic culture in Louisiana that built massive earthen ridges and mounds and traded exotic stone widely.

name: Powhatan Confederacy
summary: Paramount chiefdom of about thirty Algonquian-speaking groups in Tidewater Virginia under Wahunsenacawh, which fought and then fell to the Jamestown colony.

name: Anglo-Powhatan Wars
summary: Three wars between Virginia colonists and the Powhatan that ended Powhatan independence and confined survivors to reservations.

name: Pueblo Peoples
summary: Southwestern agricultural nations of New Mexico and Arizona, including Hopi, Zuni, Acoma, Taos and the Rio Grande pueblos, continuing today.

name: Acoma Pueblo
summary: Mesa-top Pueblo community in New Mexico, among the oldest continuously inhabited places in the United States.

name: Hopi
summary: Pueblo nation of northern Arizona with continuously inhabited villages including Oraibi, one of the oldest settlements in North America.

name: Pueblo Revolt
summary: Coordinated uprising led by Pope that expelled the Spanish from New Mexico for twelve years.

name: Zuni
summary: Pueblo nation of western New Mexico with a distinct language, targeted by Coronado's 1540 expedition.

name: Quiet Revolution
summary: Rapid secularisation and state-building in Quebec that transformed its politics and fuelled sovereigntism.

name: Republic of Hawaii
summary: Short-lived settler-led republic in Hawaii between the overthrow of the monarchy and US annexation.

name: Republic of Texas
summary: Independent republic that broke from Mexico in 1836 and was annexed by the United States in 1845.

name: Russian America
summary: Russian colonial possession in Alaska administered by the Russian-American Company, sold to the United States in 1867.

name: Founding of Santa Fe
summary: Spanish colonial capital of New Mexico, the oldest state capital in the United States.

name: Seminole Nation
summary: Nation formed in Florida from Creek migrants, free and fugitive Black allies and remnant groups; fought three wars and survives in Oklahoma and Florida.

name: Shawnee
summary: Algonquian nation of the Ohio Valley, home of Tecumseh and Tenskwatawa, later removed to Kansas and Oklahoma.

name: Shoshone
summary: Numic peoples of the Great Basin and Snake River, including Sacagawea's Lemhi band and Chief Washakie's Eastern Shoshone.

name: Spanish Florida
summary: Spanish colonial province in the southeast, centred on St. Augustine, transferred to the United States under the Adams-Onis Treaty.

name: Spanish New Mexico
summary: Spanish colonial province in the upper Rio Grande valley, later a Mexican territory and then a US territory.

name: Founding of St. Augustine
summary: Spanish settlement in Florida, the oldest continuously occupied European city in the continental United States.

name: State of Franklin
summary: Unrecognised breakaway state in what is now eastern Tennessee, reabsorbed by North Carolina.

name: Tecumseh's Confederacy
summary: Pan-Indigenous alliance built by Tecumseh and Tenskwatawa to resist US expansion, allied with Britain and broken at the Thames.

name: Texas Revolution
summary: Anglo-Texan and Tejano revolt against Mexico, marked by the Alamo and Goliad and won at San Jacinto.

name: Battle of the Alamo
summary: Thirteen-day siege in San Antonio in which Santa Anna's army killed the entire Texian garrison, creating a rallying cry.

name: Tlingit
summary: Northwest Coast nation of southeastern Alaska known for clan houses, totemic art and resistance to Russian colonisation.

name: Abolitionist Movement
summary: Campaign to end American slavery led by figures such as Garrison, Douglass, Tubman and the Grimke sisters.

name: Adams-Onis Treaty
summary: Treaty by which Spain ceded Florida to the United States and fixed the boundary of the Louisiana Purchase.

name: Affordable Care Act
summary: Health reform law expanding insurance coverage through exchanges, subsidies, Medicaid expansion and pre-existing condition protections.

name: AIDS Crisis in the United States
summary: Epidemic that killed hundreds of thousands of Americans and produced militant activism by groups such as ACT UP.

name: Alaska Purchase
summary: US purchase of Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million, derided at the time as 'Seward's Folly'.

name: Alaska Territory
summary: Organised US territory in the far northwest, admitted as the 49th state in 1959.

name: Alien and Sedition Acts
summary: Federalist laws restricting immigration and criminalising criticism of the government, provoking the Virginia and Kentucky Resolutions.

name: American Civil War
summary: War between the Union and eleven seceding slave states, the deadliest in US history, ending slavery and preserving the Union.

name: Surrender at Appomattox
summary: Lee's surrender to Grant at Appomattox Court House, effectively ending the Civil War.

name: Battle of Antietam
summary: Bloodiest single day in American history; the strategic Union result let Lincoln issue the Emancipation Proclamation.

name: Battle of Gettysburg
summary: Three-day Union victory in Pennsylvania that turned back Lee's second invasion of the North.

name: Battle of Shiloh
summary: Bloody two-day Union victory in Tennessee that revealed the war's likely cost.

name: First Battle of Bull Run
summary: First major land battle of the Civil War, a Confederate victory that shattered hopes of a quick Union win.

name: Sherman's March to the Sea
summary: Union campaign of destruction from Atlanta to Savannah intended to break southern will to fight.

name: Siege of Vicksburg
summary: Grant's siege that captured the last Confederate stronghold on the Mississippi, splitting the Confederacy.

name: American Imperialism
summary: Period of overseas expansion producing colonies and protectorates in the Caribbean and Pacific, including Puerto Rico and the Philippines.

name: American Indian Wars
summary: Four centuries of warfare between Euro-American colonists and later the United States and Indigenous nations across the continent.

name: American Revolutionary War
summary: War of independence in which the thirteen colonies, aided by France, defeated Britain; ended by the Treaty of Paris recognising US sovereignty.

name: Battle of Bunker Hill
summary: Costly British victory on the Charlestown heights outside Boston that showed colonial militia could stand against regulars.

name: Battles of Lexington and Concord
summary: First shots of the Revolutionary War, as Massachusetts militia turned back British regulars sent to seize colonial arms.

name: Battles of Saratoga
summary: Decisive American victory that destroyed Burgoyne's army and brought France into the war as an ally.

name: Siege of Yorktown
summary: Franco-American siege that forced Cornwallis's surrender and effectively ended the Revolutionary War.

name: Valley Forge Encampment
summary: Winter camp where Washington's army endured privation and was retrained under von Steuben.

name: Americans with Disabilities Act
summary: Law barring discrimination against disabled people and mandating accessibility in employment and public life.

name: Angel Island Immigration Station
summary: West Coast immigration station in San Francisco Bay where Asian arrivals, especially Chinese, faced prolonged detention.

name: Antebellum Period
summary: Decades before the Civil War marked by market revolution, westward expansion, slavery's growth and intensifying sectional crisis.

name: Apache Wars
summary: Decades of conflict in the Southwest with Chiricahua and other Apache bands, ending with Geronimo's surrender.

name: Nuclear Arms Race
summary: US-Soviet buildup of nuclear arsenals and delivery systems, shaped by deterrence doctrine and arms control treaties.

name: Articles of Confederation
summary: First US constitution, ratified in 1781, creating a weak central Confederation government without power to tax; replaced by the Constitution in 1789.

name: Assassination of John F. Kennedy
summary: Kennedy was shot in Dallas; Lee Harvey Oswald was charged and the Warren Commission investigated.

name: Assassination of Abraham Lincoln
summary: John Wilkes Booth shot Lincoln at Ford's Theatre days after Appomattox, elevating Andrew Johnson.

name: Banana Wars
summary: Series of US military interventions and occupations in Central America and the Caribbean protecting commercial and strategic interests.

name: Bay of Pigs Invasion
summary: Failed CIA-sponsored landing of Cuban exiles intended to topple Fidel Castro.

name: Berlin Airlift
summary: US and British air supply of West Berlin during the Soviet blockade, a defining early Cold War operation.

name: Bill of Rights
summary: First ten amendments to the Constitution, guaranteeing speech, religion, arms, due process and other individual and state protections.

name: Black Hawk War
summary: Brief war in Illinois and Wisconsin against Sauk and Meskwaki led by Black Hawk, ending at Bad Axe.

name: Black Lives Matter Movement
summary: Movement against police violence and racial injustice that produced the largest protests in US history in 2020.

name: Black Power Movement
summary: Militant turn in Black politics stressing self-determination, community control and racial pride, associated with SNCC's later phase and the Black Panther Party.

name: Bleeding Kansas
summary: Guerrilla warfare between proslavery and free-state settlers over Kansas's status, a prelude to civil war.

name: Bonus Army March
summary: Veterans' encampment in Washington demanding early bonus payment, dispersed by the Army under MacArthur.

name: Boston Massacre
summary: British soldiers fired into a Boston crowd, killing five and giving Patriots a propaganda cause.

name: Boston Tea Party
summary: Sons of Liberty dumped East India Company tea into Boston Harbor, provoking the Coercive Acts.

name: Boxer Rebellion Intervention
summary: US participation in the eight-nation expedition that relieved the Beijing legations during the Boxer uprising.

name: Massive Resistance
summary: Southern campaign of school closures, private academies and interposition laws to defy Brown v. Board of Education.

name: Brown v. Board of Education
summary: Unanimously held racially segregated public schools unconstitutional, overturning Plessy and catalysing the civil rights movement.

name: Bush v. Gore
summary: Halted the Florida recount, effectively deciding the 2000 presidential election for George W. Bush.

name: California Gold Rush
summary: Discovery at Sutter's Mill drew some 300,000 migrants to California, accelerating statehood and devastating Native communities.

name: Camp David Accords
summary: Carter-brokered framework leading to the Egypt-Israel peace treaty.

name: Cherokee Nation v. Georgia
summary: Held the Cherokee were a 'domestic dependent nation' lacking standing to sue Georgia in the Supreme Court.
aliases: Cherokee Nation v. State of Georgia

name: Chinese Exclusion Act
summary: First US law barring immigration by an entire nationality, prohibiting Chinese labourers for ten years and later extended.

name: Citizens United v. FEC
summary: Held that corporate and union independent political spending is protected speech, reshaping campaign finance.

name: Civil Rights Act of 1875
summary: Reconstruction law barring discrimination in public accommodations, struck down by the Supreme Court in 1883.

name: Civil Rights Act of 1964
summary: Landmark law banning discrimination in public accommodations, employment and federally funded programmes.

name: Civil Rights Cases
summary: Struck down the Civil Rights Act of 1875, holding the Fourteenth Amendment did not reach private discrimination.

name: Civil Rights Movement
summary: Mass campaign against segregation and disenfranchisement, from Brown v. Board and the Montgomery bus boycott to the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts.

name: Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
summary: King's murder in Memphis triggered unrest in over a hundred cities and hastened the Fair Housing Act.

name: Freedom Summer
summary: Mississippi voter registration campaign marked by the murders of three activists and the challenge of the MFDP.

name: Little Rock Integration Crisis
summary: Eisenhower sent federal troops to escort nine Black students into Central High School after the governor blocked desegregation.

name: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
summary: Mass rally of about 250,000 people where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered the 'I Have a Dream' speech.

name: Montgomery Bus Boycott
summary: Year-long boycott sparked by Rosa Parks's arrest that desegregated Montgomery buses and elevated Martin Luther King Jr.

name: Selma to Montgomery Marches
summary: Voting rights marches including 'Bloody Sunday' at the Edmund Pettus Bridge, which spurred the Voting Rights Act.

name: Closing of the American Frontier
summary: Census finding that no continuous frontier line remained, framed by Frederick Jackson Turner as the end of an era.

name: Slavery in Colonial and Antebellum America
summary: Institution of chattel slavery in what became the United States, from the first Africans in Virginia to the Thirteenth Amendment.

name: Compromise of 1850
summary: Package of laws admitting California free, organising Utah and New Mexico by popular sovereignty and toughening the Fugitive Slave Act.

name: Compromise of 1877
summary: Bargain resolving the disputed 1876 election by seating Hayes in exchange for ending federal Reconstruction.

name: Constitutional Convention
summary: Philadelphia convention that drafted the US Constitution, resolving representation through the Great Compromise.

name: Continental Congress
summary: Governing assembly of the rebelling colonies and then of the United States, spanning the First and Second Congresses and the Confederation Congress.

name: 1960s Counterculture
summary: Youth rebellion against mainstream norms featuring antiwar protest, rock music, communal living and drug experimentation.

name: Court-Packing Plan
summary: Roosevelt's failed proposal to add Supreme Court justices after the Court struck down New Deal laws.

name: Creek War
summary: War against the Red Stick Creeks in Alabama, won by Andrew Jackson at Horseshoe Bend and ending in massive land cessions.

name: American Culture Wars
summary: Ongoing political conflict over abortion, religion, sexuality, race, guns, education and national identity.

name: Dakota War of 1862
summary: Uprising of Dakota Sioux in Minnesota, followed by the largest mass execution in US history at Mankato.

name: Dawes Act
summary: Allotment policy dividing tribal lands into individual parcels, costing Indigenous nations about ninety million acres.

name: Declaration of Independence
summary: Continental Congress declared the thirteen colonies free of British rule in a document drafted chiefly by Thomas Jefferson.

name: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
summary: Overruled Roe v. Wade, returning abortion regulation to the states.

name: Dominican Republic Intervention
summary: US military intervention in the Dominican civil war, sending over 20,000 troops to prevent a feared communist takeover.

name: Dot-Com Boom and Bust
summary: Internet-driven stock bubble and subsequent crash that reshaped the American technology economy.

name: Dred Scott v. Sandford
summary: Held Black Americans could not be citizens and that Congress could not bar slavery in the territories, inflaming the sectional crisis.

name: Dust Bowl
summary: Severe drought and soil erosion on the southern Plains that displaced hundreds of thousands of farm families.

name: Early Republic
summary: Formative decades of the constitutional United States, from Washington's inauguration through the War of 1812.

name: Eighteenth Amendment
summary: Amendment prohibiting the manufacture, sale and transport of intoxicating liquors, implemented by the Volstead Act.

name: Election of 1800
summary: Contested election resolved by the House that produced the first peaceful transfer of power between parties.

name: Election of 1860
summary: Four-way contest won by Lincoln with under 40 percent of the vote, prompting southern secession.

name: Election of 1876
summary: Disputed election between Hayes and Tilden resolved by an electoral commission and the Compromise of 1877.

name: Election of 1932
summary: Roosevelt's landslide over Hoover that created the New Deal coalition and realigned American politics.

name: Election of 2000
summary: Election decided by 537 Florida votes after a recount halted by the Supreme Court.

name: Ellis Island Immigration Station
summary: Principal US immigrant inspection station in New York Harbor, through which about twelve million people passed.

name: Emancipation Proclamation
summary: Lincoln's executive order declaring enslaved people in rebel territory free and authorising Black enlistment in the Union army.

name: Embargo Act of 1807
summary: Jefferson's ban on American exports intended to coerce Britain and France, which devastated US commerce instead.

name: American Environmental Movement
summary: Wave of ecological activism sparked by Silent Spring, producing Earth Day, the EPA, the Clean Air Act and the Endangered Species Act.

name: Equal Rights Amendment Campaign
summary: Congressional passage and ultimately failed state ratification drive for a constitutional guarantee of sex equality.

name: Era of Good Feelings
summary: Period of one-party nationalism after the War of 1812, associated with James Monroe's presidency and the Monroe Doctrine.

name: Erie Canal
summary: 363-mile canal linking the Hudson to Lake Erie, slashing freight costs and making New York the nation's leading port.

name: Ex parte Milligan
summary: Held that military tribunals cannot try civilians where civil courts are open, limiting wartime executive power.

name: Fair Housing Act
summary: Law prohibiting discrimination in the sale, rental and financing of housing, passed days after Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination.

name: Fall of Saigon
summary: North Vietnamese capture of Saigon and the chaotic US evacuation, ending the Vietnam War.

name: Federal Reserve Act
summary: Law creating the Federal Reserve System as the nation's central bank.

name: Federal Writers' Project Slave Narratives
summary: WPA programme that recorded more than 2,300 interviews with formerly enslaved people.

name: Federalist Era
summary: Period of Federalist Party dominance under Washington and John Adams, marked by Hamilton's financial system and partisan conflict.

name: The Federalist Papers
summary: Eighty-five essays by Hamilton, Madison and Jay arguing for ratification of the Constitution.

name: Fifteenth Amendment
summary: Amendment barring denial of the vote on grounds of race, colour or previous condition of servitude.

name: First Barbary War
summary: US naval campaign against Tripoli and other Barbary states over tribute demands and captured sailors.

name: First Continental Congress
summary: Twelve colonies met in Philadelphia to coordinate resistance to the Intolerable Acts through boycott and petition.

name: First Seminole War
summary: Jackson's invasion of Spanish Florida against Seminoles and maroons, which precipitated the US acquisition of Florida.

name: Fourteenth Amendment
summary: Amendment granting birthright citizenship and guaranteeing due process and equal protection against state action.

name: Gadsden Purchase
summary: Purchase of southern Arizona and New Mexico land from Mexico for a southern railroad route.

name: Gettysburg Address
summary: Lincoln's brief speech dedicating the Soldiers' National Cemetery, redefining the war as a struggle for democratic equality.

name: GI Bill
summary: Law providing veterans with college tuition, job training, unemployment pay and subsidised home loans, expanding the middle class.

name: Gibbons v. Ogden
summary: Established broad federal authority over interstate commerce, striking down a New York steamboat monopoly.

name: Gideon v. Wainwright
summary: Guaranteed appointed counsel to indigent defendants in state felony cases.

name: Gilded Age
summary: Era of rapid industrialisation, railroads, immigration, urban growth, machine politics and extreme inequality named after a Twain novel.

name: Age of Mass Immigration
summary: Arrival of over twenty million immigrants, mostly from southern and eastern Europe, processed largely at Ellis Island.

name: Great Depression
summary: Worst economic collapse in US history, beginning with the 1929 crash and producing mass unemployment, bank failures and the New Deal.

name: Great Migration
summary: Movement of about six million African Americans from the rural South to northern, midwestern and western cities.

name: Great Sioux War of 1876
summary: War over the Black Hills including the Lakota-Cheyenne victory at Little Bighorn and subsequent US reconquest.

name: Battle of the Little Bighorn
summary: Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors annihilated Custer's detachment of the 7th Cavalry in Montana.

name: Great Society
summary: Lyndon Johnson's sweeping domestic programme creating Medicare, Medicaid, federal education aid, immigration reform and civil rights enforcement.

name: Gulf War
summary: US-led coalition war that expelled Iraqi forces from Kuwait through Operations Desert Shield and Desert Storm.

name: Harlem Renaissance
summary: Flowering of African American literature, music and art centred in Harlem, with figures such as Hughes, Hurston and Ellington.

name: Territory of Hawaii
summary: US territory from annexation until statehood as the 50th state in 1959.

name: Haymarket Affair
summary: Chicago rally bombing and mass trial that set back the eight-hour movement and became a global labour symbol.

name: World War II Home Front
summary: Wartime mobilisation of the US economy and society, with rationing, war bonds, women in industry and Japanese American incarceration.

name: Homestead Act
summary: Law granting 160 acres of public land to settlers who improved it for five years, accelerating western settlement.

name: Hurricane Katrina
summary: Storm that flooded New Orleans, killed over 1,800 people and exposed failures in federal and local emergency response.

name: Immigration Act of 1924
