summary: Law imposing national-origin quotas that sharply cut southern and eastern European immigration and barred most Asians.

name: Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965
summary: Law abolishing national-origin quotas and reshaping the sources of American immigration.

name: Impeachment of Andrew Johnson
summary: First presidential impeachment, over violation of the Tenure of Office Act; Johnson survived by one Senate vote.

name: Impeachment of Bill Clinton
summary: House impeachment for perjury and obstruction arising from the Lewinsky investigation; the Senate acquitted him.

name: Impeachments of Donald Trump
summary: Two House impeachments, over Ukraine aid in 2019 and incitement of the January 6 attack in 2021; the Senate acquitted both times.

name: Indian Citizenship Act
summary: Law conferring US citizenship on all Native Americans born within the country's territory.

name: Indian Removal Act
summary: Law authorising treaties to relocate eastern Indigenous nations west of the Mississippi, leading to forced removals.

name: Indian Reorganization Act
summary: New Deal law ending allotment and restoring tribal self-government and land bases.

name: Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act
summary: Law allowing tribes to contract and administer federal programmes themselves, ending the termination era.

name: Indian Termination Policy
summary: Federal effort to dissolve tribal status and relocate Native people to cities, later reversed by self-determination policy.

name: Indian Territory
summary: Federal territory in present-day Oklahoma set aside for removed Indigenous nations, dissolved at Oklahoma statehood.

name: American Industrial Revolution
summary: Shift from agrarian craft production to mechanised factory industry, from Slater's mill to steel and electricity.

name: Interstate Commerce Act
summary: First major federal regulation of private industry, creating the Interstate Commerce Commission to oversee railroads.

name: Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956
summary: Law funding the 41,000-mile Interstate Highway System, transforming American mobility and suburban growth.

name: Sunbelt Migration
summary: Long shift of population, industry and political power from the Northeast and Midwest to the South and Southwest.

name: Intolerable Acts
summary: Punitive British laws closing Boston's port and altering Massachusetts government, which united the colonies in resistance.

name: Invasion of Grenada
summary: US-led invasion that removed the revolutionary government of Grenada after a coup.

name: Invasion of Panama
summary: US invasion that ousted and captured Manuel Noriega.

name: Iran-Contra Affair
summary: Scandal over secret US arms sales to Iran with proceeds diverted to Nicaraguan Contras in defiance of a congressional ban.

name: Iran Hostage Crisis
summary: Seizure of the US embassy in Tehran and 444-day detention of 52 Americans, which crippled Carter's presidency.

name: Iraq War
summary: US-led invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein, followed by insurgency, sectarian civil war and the 2007 surge.

name: Jacksonian Era
summary: Age of mass democracy, spoils politics, Indian removal and the Second Party System, named for Andrew Jackson.

name: January 6 Capitol Attack
summary: Mob storming of the Capitol seeking to block certification of the 2020 election results.

name: Japanese American Incarceration
summary: Forced removal and confinement of about 120,000 people of Japanese descent under Executive Order 9066.

name: Jazz Age
summary: Prosperous, culturally exuberant 1920s of jazz, flappers, radio, automobiles and Prohibition-era nightlife.

name: Jeffersonian Era
summary: Period of Democratic-Republican ascendancy featuring the Louisiana Purchase, the War of 1812 and the Era of Good Feelings.

name: Jim Crow Era
summary: Long period of legally enforced racial segregation and Black disenfranchisement in the South, ended by civil rights legislation.

name: John Brown's Raid on Harpers Ferry
summary: Abolitionist John Brown's failed attempt to spark a slave insurrection by seizing a federal armoury; his execution deepened sectional fear.

name: Judiciary Act of 1789
summary: Statute establishing the federal court system and the office of Attorney General.

name: Kansas-Nebraska Act
summary: Law repealing the Missouri Compromise line in favour of popular sovereignty, igniting Bleeding Kansas and creating the Republican Party.

name: Korematsu v. United States
summary: Upheld the wartime exclusion of Japanese Americans from the West Coast; repudiated by the Court in 2018.

name: Kosovo Intervention
summary: NATO air campaign led by the United States against Yugoslavia over the expulsion of Kosovar Albanians.

name: First Ku Klux Klan
summary: Postwar white terrorist organisation that attacked Black voters and Republicans until suppressed by the Enforcement Acts.

name: Second Ku Klux Klan
summary: Revived mass Klan of the 1920s, nativist and anti-Catholic as well as racist, with millions of members before collapsing in scandal.

name: American Labor Movement
summary: Long struggle for union recognition, shorter hours and workplace safety, from the National Labor Union through the AFL-CIO.

name: Lend-Lease
summary: Programme supplying about $50 billion in war material to Britain, the Soviet Union and other Allies before and during US belligerency.

name: Lewis and Clark Expedition
summary: Corps of Discovery's overland journey to the Pacific and back, mapping the Louisiana Purchase and beyond.

name: Lincoln-Douglas Debates
summary: Seven Illinois Senate debates over slavery in the territories that made Lincoln a national figure.

name: Lochner v. New York
summary: Struck down maximum-hours legislation on freedom-of-contract grounds, defining an era of judicial resistance to regulation.

name: Lost Generation
summary: Cohort of American writers and expatriates disillusioned by World War I, including Hemingway and Fitzgerald.

name: Louisiana Purchase
summary: Acquisition of 828,000 square miles from France for about $15 million, doubling the size of the United States.

name: Loving v. Virginia
summary: Struck down state bans on interracial marriage as violations of equal protection and due process.

name: Manifest Destiny
summary: Ideology holding that the United States was destined to expand across North America, used to justify Texas annexation, Oregon and the Mexican-American War.

name: Mapp v. Ohio
summary: Applied the exclusionary rule for illegally seized evidence to state criminal prosecutions.

name: Marbury v. Madison
summary: Chief Justice Marshall's ruling establishing judicial review, the Court's power to strike down unconstitutional laws.

name: Market Revolution
summary: Transformation of the American economy by canals, railroads, textile mills and wage labour.

name: McCarthyism
summary: Senator Joseph McCarthy's aggressive and largely unsubstantiated hunt for communists in government, discredited after the 1954 Army-McCarthy hearings.

name: McCulloch v. Maryland
summary: Upheld the constitutionality of the national bank and broad implied federal powers while barring state taxation of federal institutions.

name: McGirt v. Oklahoma
summary: Supreme Court ruling that much of eastern Oklahoma remains Indian country for criminal jurisdiction purposes.

name: MeToo Movement
summary: Mass reckoning with sexual harassment and assault that toppled prominent figures across industries.

name: Creation of Medicare and Medicaid
summary: Great Society amendments to Social Security establishing federal health insurance for the elderly and poor.

name: Mexican-American War
summary: War with Mexico that ended in the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, transferring California and the Southwest to the United States.

name: Miranda v. Arizona
summary: Required police to warn suspects of their rights to silence and counsel before custodial interrogation.

name: Missouri Compromise
summary: Congressional bargain admitting Missouri as a slave state and Maine as free, and barring slavery north of 36 degrees 30 minutes in the Louisiana Territory.

name: Monroe Doctrine
summary: Declaration that the Americas were closed to further European colonisation, becoming a pillar of US foreign policy.

name: North American Free Trade Agreement
summary: Trade pact eliminating most tariffs among the United States, Canada and Mexico; replaced by the USMCA in 2020.

name: Nat Turner's Rebellion
summary: Slave uprising in Southampton County, Virginia, that killed about sixty whites and triggered severe repression.

name: Founding of NATO
summary: US-led creation of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization as a collective defence alliance against the Soviet Union.

name: American Isolationism
summary: Interwar retreat from European commitments, expressed in Senate rejection of the League and the Neutrality Acts.

name: New Deal
summary: Franklin Roosevelt's programme of relief, recovery and reform, creating Social Security, the SEC, the TVA and federal work relief agencies.

name: Agricultural Adjustment Administration
summary: New Deal agency that paid farmers to cut production in order to raise crop prices.

name: Civilian Conservation Corps
summary: New Deal work relief agency that employed three million young men on forestry, parks and erosion projects.

name: National Recovery Administration
summary: New Deal agency setting industrial codes on prices and wages, struck down by the Supreme Court in 1935.

name: Tennessee Valley Authority
summary: New Deal public corporation that built dams, generated power and modernised the Tennessee Valley.

name: Works Progress Administration
summary: Largest New Deal agency, employing 8.5 million people on public works, arts and writing projects.

name: New Left
summary: Radical student and intellectual movement centred on SDS, participatory democracy and opposition to the Vietnam War.

name: Nez Perce War
summary: Fighting retreat of Chief Joseph's band across 1,170 miles toward Canada before surrender in the Bear Paw Mountains.

name: Nineteenth Amendment
summary: Amendment guaranteeing women the right to vote after a seventy-year suffrage campaign.

name: Nixon's Visit to China
summary: Nixon's week in Beijing that reopened US-Chinese relations after twenty-two years of estrangement.

name: Resignation of Richard Nixon
summary: First resignation of a US president, following the Supreme Court tapes ruling and imminent impeachment.

name: Northwest Indian War
summary: Conflict between the United States and a confederacy of Ohio Country nations, ended by Fallen Timbers and the Treaty of Greenville.

name: Northwest Ordinance
summary: Confederation Congress law organising the Northwest Territory, banning slavery there and setting the process for admitting new states.

name: Nullification Crisis
summary: South Carolina's attempt to void federal tariffs, defused by Jackson's Force Bill and a compromise tariff.

name: Obergefell v. Hodges
summary: Held that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry nationwide.

name: US Occupation of Haiti
summary: Nineteen-year Marine occupation of Haiti that reorganised its finances and provoked the Caco rebellion.

name: Oklahoma Land Rush
summary: Series of land runs opening former Indian Territory to non-Native settlement.

name: Oregon Treaty
summary: Anglo-American agreement dividing the Oregon Country at the 49th parallel.

name: Pacific Railway Acts
summary: Laws chartering and subsidising the first transcontinental railroad, completed at Promontory Summit in 1869.

name: Construction of the Panama Canal
summary: US engineering project that cut a shipping route across the isthmus after acquiring rights from newly independent Panama.

name: Pancho Villa Expedition
summary: Punitive expedition led by John J. Pershing into Mexico after Villa's raid on Columbus, New Mexico.

name: Panic of 1837
summary: Financial crisis and prolonged depression following speculation, the Specie Circular and British credit contraction.

name: Panic of 1873
summary: Railroad and banking collapse that began the Long Depression and undermined Reconstruction.

name: Panic of 1893
summary: Severe depression with mass unemployment, railroad bankruptcies and violent labour conflict.

name: Philippine-American War
summary: Brutal counterinsurgency against the Philippine Republic following US annexation of the islands.

name: US Rule in the Philippines
summary: American colonial administration of the Philippines from the Spanish cession to independence in 1946.

name: Plessy v. Ferguson
summary: Upheld 'separate but equal' racial segregation, constitutional cover for Jim Crow for fifty-eight years.

name: Populist Movement
summary: Agrarian revolt against railroads, banks and the gold standard that produced the People's Party and Bryan's 1896 campaign.

name: Postwar Boom
summary: Era of sustained prosperity, suburbanisation, the baby boom, the GI Bill and mass consumer culture.

name: Presidency of Abraham Lincoln
summary: Sixteenth president; led the Union through the Civil War, issued the Emancipation Proclamation and was assassinated days after Confederate surrender.

name: Presidency of Andrew Jackson
summary: Seventh president; destroyed the Second Bank, faced down South Carolina's nullification and forced Indian removal along the Trail of Tears.

name: Presidency of Andrew Johnson
summary: Seventeenth president; clashed bitterly with Radical Republicans over Reconstruction and was impeached and acquitted by one vote.

name: Presidency of Barack Obama
summary: Forty-fourth president and first African American president; enacted the Affordable Care Act and stimulus recovery and normalised relations with Cuba.

name: Presidency of Benjamin Harrison
summary: Twenty-third president; signed the Sherman Antitrust Act and the high McKinley Tariff and admitted six western states.

name: Presidency of Bill Clinton
summary: Forty-second president; presided over budget surpluses, NAFTA and welfare reform, and was impeached and acquitted in 1998-99.

name: Presidency of Calvin Coolidge
summary: Thirtieth president; presided over 1920s prosperity with tax cuts and minimal government activism.

name: Presidency of Chester A. Arthur
summary: Twenty-first president; a former spoilsman who surprised critics by signing the Pendleton Civil Service Act.

name: First Presidency of Donald Trump
summary: Forty-fifth president; cut taxes, reshaped the judiciary, was impeached twice and managed the initial COVID-19 response.

name: Second Presidency of Donald Trump
summary: Forty-seventh president; returned to office in 2025 after a non-consecutive gap, pursuing tariffs, immigration enforcement and federal restructuring.

name: Presidency of Dwight D. Eisenhower
summary: Thirty-fourth president; ended the Korean War, built the Interstate Highway System and sent troops to enforce desegregation at Little Rock.

name: Presidency of Franklin D. Roosevelt
summary: Thirty-second president and only four-term president; enacted the New Deal and led the Allied war effort until his death in April 1945.

name: Presidency of Franklin Pierce
summary: Fourteenth president; his support for the Kansas-Nebraska Act ignited Bleeding Kansas and shattered the Democratic coalition.

name: Presidency of George H. W. Bush
summary: Forty-first president; managed the end of the Cold War and German reunification and led the coalition that won the Gulf War.

name: Presidency of George W. Bush
summary: Forty-third president; responded to the September 11 attacks with the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, and left office amid the financial crisis.

name: Presidency of George Washington
summary: First president; set precedents for the office, established the cabinet and federal finance, suppressed the Whiskey Rebellion and urged neutrality in his Farewell Address.

name: Presidency of Gerald Ford
summary: Thirty-eighth president and the only one never elected to either national office; pardoned Nixon and battled inflation and recession.

name: First Presidency of Grover Cleveland
summary: Twenty-second president; fiscally conservative Democrat who vetoed pension bills and fought tariffs before losing the 1888 electoral vote.

name: Second Presidency of Grover Cleveland
summary: Twenty-fourth president; the only non-consecutive second term, dominated by the Panic of 1893 and the Pullman Strike.

name: Presidency of Harry S. Truman
summary: Thirty-third president; authorised the atomic bombings, launched the Marshall Plan, NATO and containment, and committed forces to Korea.

name: Presidency of Herbert Hoover
summary: Thirty-first president; the 1929 crash and Great Depression overwhelmed his limited relief efforts, and he lost in a 1932 landslide.

name: Presidency of James A. Garfield
summary: Twentieth president; shot by Charles Guiteau four months into his term and died in September 1881.

name: Presidency of James Buchanan
summary: Fifteenth president; failed to halt sectional collapse or secession, widely ranked among the least successful presidents.

name: Presidency of James K. Polk
summary: Eleventh president; expansionist who settled the Oregon boundary and won the Mexican-American War, adding the Southwest and California.

name: Presidency of James Madison
summary: Fourth president; led the nation through the War of 1812 and the burning of Washington, then presided over postwar nationalism.

name: Presidency of James Monroe
summary: Fifth president; oversaw the Era of Good Feelings, the acquisition of Florida, the Missouri Compromise and the Monroe Doctrine.

name: Presidency of Jimmy Carter
summary: Thirty-ninth president; brokered the Camp David Accords but was hampered by stagflation, the energy crisis and the Iran hostage crisis.

name: Presidency of Joe Biden
summary: Forty-sixth president; passed infrastructure and climate legislation, withdrew from Afghanistan and backed Ukraine against Russia.

name: Presidency of John Adams
summary: Federalist second president; navigated the Quasi-War with France, signed the Alien and Sedition Acts and lost re-election in 1800.

name: Presidency of John F. Kennedy
summary: Thirty-fifth president; faced the Bay of Pigs and Cuban Missile Crisis, launched the Moon programme and was assassinated in Dallas.

name: Presidency of John Quincy Adams
summary: Sixth president, elected by the House in the disputed 1824 contest; promoted internal improvements but was blocked by Jacksonian opposition.

name: Presidency of John Tyler
summary: Tenth president and first to succeed on a death; expelled from the Whig Party, he secured the annexation of Texas.

name: Presidency of Lyndon B. Johnson
summary: Thirty-sixth president; passed the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts and the Great Society, but was undone by the Vietnam War.

name: Presidency of Martin Van Buren
summary: Eighth president; his term was consumed by the Panic of 1837 depression and the continuing Second Seminole War.

name: Presidency of Millard Fillmore
summary: Thirteenth president; signed the Compromise of 1850 including the Fugitive Slave Act, and opened Japan via the Perry expedition.

name: Presidency of Richard Nixon
summary: Thirty-seventh president; opened relations with China, pursued detente and withdrew from Vietnam before resigning over Watergate.

name: Presidency of Ronald Reagan
summary: Fortieth president; cut taxes, expanded the military, weathered the Iran-Contra affair and negotiated arms reductions with Gorbachev.

name: Presidency of Rutherford B. Hayes
summary: Nineteenth president; took office via the Compromise of 1877, withdrew federal troops from the South and pursued civil service reform.

name: Presidency of Theodore Roosevelt
summary: Twenty-sixth president; trust-busting Progressive who championed conservation, the Pure Food and Drug Act and the Panama Canal.

name: Presidency of Thomas Jefferson
summary: Third president; completed the Louisiana Purchase, sent Lewis and Clark west, fought the Barbary pirates and imposed the Embargo Act.

name: Presidency of Ulysses S. Grant
summary: Eighteenth president; enforced Reconstruction and prosecuted the Klan while his administration was marred by financial scandals and the Panic of 1873.

name: Presidency of Warren G. Harding
summary: Twenty-ninth president; promised a 'return to normalcy' and died in office in 1923 as the Teapot Dome scandal emerged.

name: Presidency of William Henry Harrison
summary: Ninth president; died of illness thirty-one days after inauguration, the shortest presidency in US history.

name: Presidency of William Howard Taft
summary: Twenty-seventh president; pursued more antitrust suits than Roosevelt but split the Republican Party and lost the 1912 election.

name: Presidency of William McKinley
summary: Twenty-fifth president; won the Spanish-American War, annexed Hawaii and the Philippines and was assassinated in Buffalo in 1901.

name: Presidency of Woodrow Wilson
summary: Twenty-eighth president; created the Federal Reserve, led the US into World War I and championed the League of Nations.

name: Presidency of Zachary Taylor
summary: Twelfth president; Mexican War hero who died of illness sixteen months into his term amid the crisis over slavery in the new territories.

name: Presidential Reconstruction
summary: Andrew Johnson's lenient restoration policy for the ex-Confederate states, which produced Black Codes and provoked congressional backlash.

name: Progressive Era Amendments
summary: Cluster of four amendments creating the income tax, direct senatorial election, Prohibition and women's suffrage.

name: Progressive Era
summary: Reform period targeting trusts, corruption, unsafe food and labour conditions, producing antitrust action, direct election of senators and suffrage momentum.

name: Prohibition
summary: Nationwide ban on alcoholic beverages under the Eighteenth Amendment and Volstead Act, repealed by the Twenty-first Amendment.

name: Puerto Rico under US Rule
summary: Caribbean island ceded by Spain in 1898, an unincorporated US territory whose residents are citizens without presidential votes.

name: Pullman Strike
summary: National railway boycott broken by federal troops and injunction, making Eugene Debs a socialist leader.

name: Quasi-War
summary: Undeclared naval war with revolutionary France in the Caribbean, ended by the Convention of 1800.

name: Reagan Revolution
summary: Conservative realignment of tax cuts, deregulation, military buildup and confrontation with the Soviet Union.

name: Reconstruction
summary: Postwar rebuilding of the South, with federal military occupation, Black political participation and the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments; ended by the Compromise of 1877.

name: Black Codes
summary: Southern state laws restricting freedpeople's labour, movement and rights, which provoked congressional Reconstruction.

name: Freedmen's Bureau
summary: Federal agency providing relief, labour contracts, courts and schools to freedpeople and refugees in the postwar South.
aliases: Bureau of Refugees, Freedmen, and Abandoned Lands

name: Red Cloud's War
summary: Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho campaign against forts on the Bozeman Trail, won at the Treaty of Fort Laramie.

name: Red Power Movement
summary: Native activist movement including the Alcatraz occupation, AIM and Wounded Knee 1973, which won self-determination reforms.

name: Red River War
summary: Army campaign that broke Comanche, Kiowa and Southern Cheyenne resistance on the southern Plains.

name: First Red Scare
summary: Postwar panic over anarchism and Bolshevism, marked by the Palmer Raids, mass deportations and suppression of radical labour.

name: Second Red Scare
summary: Cold War anticommunist campaign of loyalty oaths, blacklists and congressional investigations into alleged subversion.

name: Redemption
summary: Campaign by white Democratic 'Redeemers' to overthrow Reconstruction governments in the South, often by paramilitary violence.

name: Regents of the University of California v. Bakke
summary: Barred racial quotas in university admissions while permitting race as one factor in pursuing diversity.

name: Roe v. Wade
summary: Recognised a constitutional right to abortion; overruled in 2022 by Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization.

name: Schenck v. United States
summary: Upheld Espionage Act convictions and introduced the 'clear and present danger' test for speech.

name: Secession Winter
summary: Departure of eleven southern states from the Union following Lincoln's election, culminating in the firing on Fort Sumter.

name: Second Barbary War
summary: Short US naval expedition under Decatur that ended Algerine attacks on American shipping.

name: Second Great Awakening
summary: Protestant revival movement of camp meetings and reform societies that fuelled abolition, temperance and women's activism.

name: Second Seminole War
summary: Longest and costliest of the Indian removal wars, fought in Florida swamps against Seminoles under Osceola.

name: Second-Wave Feminism
summary: Women's movement for legal and economic equality, producing NOW, Title IX, Roe v. Wade and the failed Equal Rights Amendment campaign.

name: Sectional Crisis
summary: Escalating North-South conflict over slavery's extension, from the Wilmot Proviso to secession.

name: Seneca Falls Convention
summary: First US women's rights convention, which issued the Declaration of Sentiments demanding equality including the vote.

name: Seventeenth Amendment
summary: Amendment providing for direct popular election of United States senators.

name: Shays' Rebellion
summary: Debtor farmers' armed revolt in western Massachusetts that exposed the weakness of the Articles of Confederation.

name: Sherman Antitrust Act
summary: Landmark law outlawing monopolistic combinations and restraints of trade.

name: Sixteenth Amendment
summary: Amendment authorising a federal income tax without apportionment among the states.

name: Social Security Act
summary: New Deal law creating old-age pensions, unemployment insurance and aid to dependent children.

name: Somalia Intervention
summary: US humanitarian and military mission in Somalia that ended after the Battle of Mogadishu.

name: Space Race
summary: US-Soviet competition in spaceflight, from Sputnik through the Apollo Moon landings and Apollo-Soyuz.

name: First Human Spaceflight
summary: Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth on 12 April 1961 aboard Vostok 1.

name: Launch of Sputnik 1
summary: First artificial satellite, launched by the USSR on 4 October 1957, opening the space age.

name: Spanish-American War
summary: Brief war that expelled Spain from Cuba and gave the United States Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.

name: Stagflation Era
summary: Decade of simultaneous high inflation and unemployment triggered by oil shocks and ended by Volcker's tight money policy.

name: Stamp Act Crisis
summary: Colonial resistance to Parliament's direct tax on printed materials, producing the Stamp Act Congress and repeal.

name: Admission of the States
summary: Process by which fifty states joined the Union, from Delaware's ratification to Alaska and Hawaii in 1959.

name: Stonewall Riots
summary: Uprising against a police raid on a Greenwich Village gay bar, conventionally the start of the modern LGBT rights movement.

name: Temperance Movement
summary: Long campaign against alcohol led by the WCTU and Anti-Saloon League, culminating in national Prohibition.

name: Tet Offensive
summary: Coordinated communist attacks across South Vietnam that were militarily repulsed but shattered US public confidence.

name: Third Seminole War
summary: Final campaign to expel remaining Seminoles from Florida.

name: Thirteenth Amendment
summary: Constitutional amendment abolishing slavery and involuntary servitude except as criminal punishment.

name: Trail of Tears
summary: Forced removals of Cherokee, Choctaw, Chickasaw, Creek and Seminole nations to Indian Territory, killing thousands en route.

name: Transatlantic Slave Trade to North America
summary: Forced transport of enslaved Africans to the mainland colonies and the United States, banned by federal law in 1808.

name: Completion of the Transcontinental Railroad
summary: Union Pacific and Central Pacific rails met at Promontory Summit, joining the coasts by rail.

name: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
summary: Treaty ending the Mexican-American War, ceding California, Nevada, Utah and more to the United States for $15 million.

name: Treaty of Paris (1783)
summary: Anglo-American peace treaty recognising US independence and setting borders to the Mississippi River.

name: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
summary: Fire that killed 146 garment workers in New York and spurred landmark workplace safety laws.

name: Truman Doctrine
summary: Pledge to support free peoples resisting subjugation, beginning the containment policy with aid to Greece and Turkey.

name: Twenty-first Amendment
summary: Amendment repealing Prohibition, the only amendment to nullify a previous one.

name: Twenty-fourth Amendment
summary: Amendment abolishing poll taxes in federal elections.

name: Twenty-second Amendment
summary: Amendment limiting presidents to two elected terms, a response to Franklin Roosevelt's four victories.

name: Twenty-sixth Amendment
summary: Amendment lowering the voting age to eighteen amid the Vietnam War draft.

name: Publication of Uncle Tom's Cabin
summary: Harriet Beecher Stowe's antislavery novel sold hundreds of thousands of copies and hardened sectional opinion.

name: Underground Railroad
summary: Clandestine network of routes and safe houses helping enslaved people escape to free states and Canada.

name: United States v. Nixon
summary: Held that executive privilege does not shield evidence in a criminal case, forcing release of the Watergate tapes.

name: United States Constitution
summary: Supreme law of the United States, ratified in 1788 and effective in 1789, creating a federal government of three branches.

name: USA PATRIOT Act
summary: Post-9/11 law greatly expanding federal surveillance, detention and financial-tracking powers.

name: Utah War
summary: Largely bloodless confrontation between the federal government and Mormon settlers in Utah Territory.

name: Voting Rights Act of 1965
summary: Law banning literacy tests and imposing federal oversight of elections in jurisdictions with histories of discrimination.

name: National Labor Relations Act
summary: Law guaranteeing private-sector collective bargaining and creating the National Labor Relations Board.

name: Wall Street Crash of 1929
summary: October stock market collapse that wiped out fortunes and signalled the onset of the Great Depression.

name: Intervention against ISIS
summary: US-led coalition campaign of airstrikes and advisers that destroyed the Islamic State's territorial caliphate in Iraq and Syria.

name: War in Afghanistan
summary: America's longest war, begun to destroy al-Qaeda and topple the Taliban and ended by the 2021 withdrawal and Taliban return.

name: War of 1812
summary: War with Britain over impressment, trade restrictions and western expansion; included the burning of Washington and Jackson's victory at New Orleans.

name: Battle of New Orleans
summary: Jackson's lopsided victory over British regulars, fought after the peace treaty was signed, made him a national hero.

name: Battle of Tippecanoe
summary: Harrison's attack on Prophetstown that broke Tenskwatawa's confederacy and helped precipitate the War of 1812.

name: Burning of Washington
summary: British forces captured the capital and burned the Capitol and White House in retaliation for raids in Canada.

name: War on Poverty
summary: Johnson administration antipoverty campaign launched by the Economic Opportunity Act, creating Head Start, Job Corps, VISTA and community action agencies.

name: Watergate Scandal
summary: Break-in at Democratic headquarters and the Nixon administration cover-up that led to the president's resignation in August 1974.

name: Westward Expansion
summary: Century of US territorial and settler expansion from the Louisiana Purchase to the closing of the frontier.

name: Whiskey Rebellion
summary: Armed tax revolt by western Pennsylvania distillers, suppressed by a federalised militia led personally by President Washington.

name: Women's Suffrage Movement
summary: Campaign from Seneca Falls to the Nineteenth Amendment for women's voting rights, led by Stanton, Anthony, Catt and Paul.

name: Worcester v. Georgia
summary: Ruled Georgia law had no force in Cherokee territory, a decision the Jackson administration declined to enforce.

name: World War I (United States)
summary: US entry into the Great War, sending two million troops of the AEF to France and turning the Western Front against Germany.

name: Western Front of the First World War
summary: Four years of trench stalemate in France and Belgium, with battles such as Verdun, the Somme and Passchendaele.

name: World War II (United States)
summary: US involvement from Pearl Harbor to the surrender of Japan, fighting in Europe, North Africa and the Pacific and developing the atomic bomb.

name: Atomic Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
summary: US atomic attacks that killed well over 100,000 people and preceded Japan's surrender.

name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
summary: Japanese surprise attack on the Pacific Fleet in Hawaii that brought the United States into World War II.

name: Battle of Iwo Jima
summary: Costly Marine assault on a fortified Japanese island, immortalised by the flag-raising on Mount Suribachi.

name: Battle of Midway
summary: Decisive US naval victory that destroyed four Japanese carriers and turned the Pacific war.

name: Battle of Stalingrad
summary: Soviet encirclement and destruction of a German army, the turning point on the Eastern Front.

name: Normandy Landings
summary: Allied invasion of northwest Europe on 6 June 1944 that opened the western front against Germany.

name: Manhattan Project
summary: Secret Allied programme led by the United States that built the first nuclear weapons at Los Alamos, Oak Ridge and Hanford.

name: Operation Barbarossa
summary: German invasion of the Soviet Union, the largest land offensive in history and the war's decisive theatre.

name: Wounded Knee Massacre
summary: US cavalry killed roughly 250-300 Lakota, mostly noncombatants, at Wounded Knee Creek, conventionally closing the Indian Wars.

name: Ute
summary: Numic nation of Colorado and Utah, among the first Plains-adjacent peoples to acquire horses from the Spanish.

name: Vermont Republic
summary: Self-declared independent republic between New York and New Hampshire that joined the Union as the fourteenth state in 1791.

name: Wampanoag
summary: Algonquian nation of southeastern Massachusetts and Rhode Island who met the Pilgrims and later fought King Philip's War; federally recognised today.

name: Oriental Republic of Uruguay
summary: Buffer republic created by British mediation between Brazil and Argentina, later a pioneering welfare democracy.

name: Uruguayan Military Dictatorship
summary: Civil-military regime that imprisoned and tortured on a mass scale after the Tupamaro insurgency.

name: Paraguayan War
summary: Triple Alliance of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay devastated Paraguay, killing a large share of its population.

name: Plurinational State of Bolivia
summary: Andean republic named for Bolivar, which lost its coast and Chaco lands and elected its first Indigenous president in 2005.

name: Bolivian National Revolution
summary: MNR revolution that nationalised tin, enfranchised Indigenous people and redistributed land.

name: Presidency of Evo Morales
summary: First Indigenous president: gas nationalisation, a plurinational constitution, and resignation amid disputed re-election.

name: Potosi Silver Complex
summary: Cerro Rico mines worked under the mita labour draft supplied much of the world's silver and financed Spain.

name: Republic of Chile
summary: South American republic stabilised by Portales's 1833 constitution, later shaped by nitrates, copper and the Pinochet era.

name: Presidency of Salvador Allende
summary: First elected Marxist president, who nationalised copper and was overthrown in the 11 September 1973 coup.

name: Captaincy General of Chile
summary: Spanish colony hemmed in by Mapuche resistance beyond the Bio-Bio river.

name: Chilean War of Independence
summary: Patria Vieja, reconquest and final liberation by San Martin and O'Higgins at Chacabuco and Maipu.

name: Occupation of Araucania
summary: Chilean military conquest of Mapuche territory south of the Bio-Bio.

name: Pinochet Dictatorship
summary: Military regime with over 3,000 killed and tens of thousands tortured, alongside radical free-market reform.

name: Republic of Colombia
summary: Andean-Caribbean republic, successor to New Granada, marked by two-party civil wars and a long internal conflict.

name: Colombian Armed Conflict
summary: Long war among FARC, ELN, paramilitaries, cartels and the state, partly ended by the 2016 peace accord.

name: Colombian Peace Agreement
summary: Havana accord that demobilised the FARC and won Santos the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: La Violencia
summary: Partisan civil conflict triggered by Gaitan's assassination and the Bogotazo, killing about 200,000.

name: Thousand Days' War
summary: Liberal-Conservative civil war that killed some 100,000 and preceded Panama's secession.

name: Republic of Costa Rica
summary: Central American republic that abolished its army in 1949 and became the region's most stable democracy.

name: Republic of Cuba
summary: Cuban republic from 1902, under the Platt Amendment, then Batista, then communist rule since 1959.

name: Batista Regime
summary: Fulgencio Batista's corrupt dictatorship, overthrown by the 26th of July Movement.

name: Cuban Revolution
summary: Castro and Guevara's guerrilla campaign that took Havana on 1 January 1959.

name: Special Period
summary: Severe economic crisis after Soviet subsidies ended, forcing rationing and limited market openings.

name: Ten Years' War
summary: First Cuban war of independence, ending in the Pact of Zanjon without independence.

name: Cuban War of Independence
summary: Marti- and Maceo-led revolt that drew in the United States and ended Spanish rule.

name: Rule of Fidel Castro
summary: Nearly half a century leading communist Cuba through nationalisation, Soviet alliance and US embargo.

name: Presidency of Raul Castro
summary: Cautious economic liberalisation and the 2015 restoration of relations with the United States.

name: Spanish Cuba
summary: Spain's sugar and tobacco colony and last major American possession, lost in 1898.

name: Republic of Ecuador
summary: Andean-Pacific republic that left Gran Colombia in 1830; oil-exporting and dollarised since 2000.

name: Republic of El Salvador
summary: Central American republic marked by the 1932 Matanza, a brutal civil war and postwar gang violence.

name: Salvadoran Civil War
summary: Twelve-year war between the US-backed government and the FMLN that killed some 75,000 people.

name: Republic of Guatemala
summary: Central American republic of the 1944 October Revolution, the 1954 coup and a genocidal civil war.

name: Guatemalan Civil War
summary: Thirty-six-year conflict with about 200,000 dead, including genocide against Maya communities.

name: Guatemalan Coup of 1954
summary: CIA-organised overthrow of Jacobo Arbenz after his land reform threatened United Fruit.

name: Republic of Guyana
summary: Former British Guiana, independent in 1966 and transformed by offshore oil since 2019.

name: Republic of Haiti
summary: Independent since 1804, burdened by the French indemnity, US occupation, dictatorship and repeated state collapse.

name: Duvalier Regime
summary: Francois 'Papa Doc' and Jean-Claude 'Baby Doc' Duvalier ruled with the Tontons Macoutes for 29 years.

name: 2010 Haiti Earthquake
summary: Magnitude 7.0 quake near Port-au-Prince that killed well over 100,000 people.

name: Haitian Declaration of Independence
summary: Dessalines proclaimed independence on 1 January 1804, the first Black republic and second American republic.

name: Haitian Revolution
summary: Only successful large-scale slave revolt, which defeated French, Spanish and British forces and created Haiti.

name: Saint-Domingue
summary: France's richest colony, producing sugar and coffee with enslaved labour on a vast scale, destroyed by revolution.

name: Leadership of Toussaint Louverture
summary: Former slave who became governor of Saint-Domingue, abolished slavery and died in French captivity.

name: United States Occupation of Haiti
summary: Nineteen-year American military rule that rewrote Haitian law and finances.

name: Republic of Honduras
summary: Central American republic long dominated by banana companies and by military politics.

name: Republic of Nicaragua
summary: Central American republic shaped by US intervention, the Somoza dynasty and Sandinista rule.

name: Contra War
summary: US-backed counter-revolutionary insurgency against the Sandinista government, tied to the Iran-Contra affair.

name: Sandinista Revolution
summary: FSLN insurrection that toppled Somoza and led to a decade of revolution and Contra war.

name: Somoza Dynasty
summary: Family dictatorship backed by the National Guard and the United States, overthrown by the Sandinistas.

name: Republic of Panama
summary: Seceded from Colombia with US backing in 1903; the canal returned to Panamanian control in 1999.

name: United States Invasion of Panama
summary: Operation Just Cause removed Manuel Noriega from power.

name: Republic of Paraguay
summary: Landlocked republic independent from 1811, devastated in the Triple Alliance war and ruled by Stroessner for 35 years.

name: Stroessner Dictatorship
summary: Alfredo Stroessner's anticommunist regime, the longest in 20th-century South America.

name: Republic of Peru
summary: Andean republic independent from 1821, shaped by guano and nitrate booms, military rule and the Shining Path conflict.

name: Battle of Ayacucho
summary: Sucre's victory that destroyed the last royalist army and sealed South American independence.

name: Fujimori Government
summary: Alberto Fujimori defeated hyperinflation and Sendero but ruled by self-coup and corruption.

name: Shining Path Insurgency
summary: Maoist insurgency and state counterinsurgency that killed about 70,000 people.

name: Rebellion of Tupac Amaru II
summary: Largest Andean uprising against Spanish rule, brutally suppressed after threatening Cusco.

name: Republic of Suriname
summary: Former Dutch Guiana, independent in 1975, with large emigration to the Netherlands.

name: Republic of Venezuela
summary: Caribbean-Andean republic that left Gran Colombia in 1830, later transformed by oil and by Chavismo.

name: Presidency of Hugo Chavez
summary: Bolivarian Revolution: new constitution, oil-funded social missions and confrontation with the United States.

name: Dictatorship of Juan Vicente Gomez
summary: Long personal rule during which oil made Venezuela a major exporter.

name: Presidency of Nicolas Maduro
summary: Rule marked by economic collapse, hyperinflation, disputed elections and the emigration of millions.

name: Venezuelan Declaration of Independence
summary: First Venezuelan republic declared independence on 5 July 1811; it soon fell, beginning years of war.

name: Punto Fijo Democracy
summary: Forty years of two-party democracy funded by oil, collapsing after the 1989 Caracazo riots.

name: Campaigns of Jose de San Martin
summary: Crossing of the Andes, liberation of Chile at Chacabuco and Maipu, and the proclamation of Peru's independence.

name: Campaigns of Simon Bolivar
summary: The Liberator's campaigns from Venezuela over the Andes to Boyaca, Carabobo, Junin and Ayacucho.

name: Spanish American Wars of Independence
summary: Continental struggle that ended Spanish rule in the mainland Americas and created some fifteen republics.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
summary: Oil- and gas-rich Caribbean state independent in 1962 and a republic since 1976.

name: Viceroyalty of New Granada
summary: Spanish viceroyalty covering Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama, based at Bogota.

name: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata
summary: Late Spanish viceroyalty based in Buenos Aires covering Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia.

name: War of the Pacific
summary: Chile defeated Peru and Bolivia, taking nitrate provinces and leaving Bolivia landlocked.

name: Desiccation of the Aral Sea
summary: Soviet irrigation of cotton lands shrank the Aral Sea by most of its volume, a landmark ecological disaster.

name: Basmachi Revolt
summary: Muslim resistance to Russian and Soviet rule across Turkestan, suppressed by the Red Army.

name: Dzungar Khanate
summary: Last great steppe empire, destroyed by the Qing in a campaign of near-annihilation.

name: Emirate of Bukhara
summary: Manghit emirate, a Russian protectorate from 1868, overthrown by the Red Army in 1920.

name: The Great Game
summary: Anglo-Russian strategic rivalry over Afghanistan, Persia and Turkestan, settled by the 1907 convention.

name: Russian Conquest of Central Asia
summary: Tsarist campaigns that absorbed Turkestan and the steppe, part of the Great Game with Britain.

name: Kyrgyz Republic
summary: Central Asian republic independent in 1991, with revolutions in 2005, 2010 and 2020.

name: Republic of Kazakhstan
summary: Largest Central Asian state, independent in 1991, oil-rich and ruled by Nazarbayev until 2019.

name: Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic
summary: Soviet Kazakhstan: famine under collectivisation, Virgin Lands campaign, Semipalatinsk nuclear tests and Baikonur.

name: Republic of Tajikistan
summary: Independent in 1991 and scarred by a civil war from 1992 to 1997; ruled by Emomali Rahmon.

name: Tajik Civil War
summary: Post-Soviet conflict between government and Islamist-democratic opposition that killed tens of thousands.

name: Republic of Uzbekistan
summary: Most populous Central Asian state, independent in 1991, ruled by Karimov until 2016.

name: Turkmenistan
summary: Gas-rich neutral state independent in 1991 under Niyazov's personality cult and his successors.

name: Asian Financial Crisis
summary: Currency and banking collapse from Thailand to Korea and Indonesia, with IMF programmes and political upheaval.

name: Boxer Rebellion
summary: Anti-foreign uprising crushed by an eight-nation force, followed by a crippling indemnity.

name: Canton System
summary: Restriction of Western trade to Guangzhou through licensed hong merchants, ended by the Opium War.

name: Rule of Chiang Kai-shek
summary: Nationalist leader who unified China in 1928, lost the civil war and governed Taiwan until his death.

name: Chinese Annexation of Tibet
summary: PLA entry into Tibet and the Seventeen Point Agreement, followed by the Dalai Lama's flight in 1959.

name: Chinese Civil War
summary: Intermittent war between Nationalists and Communists, won by the CCP in 1949.

name: Chinese Accession to the WTO
summary: Entry into the World Trade Organization that accelerated China's export-led growth.

name: First Opium War
summary: British victory forcing the Treaty of Nanking, ceding Hong Kong and opening treaty ports.

name: Founding of the Chinese Communist Party
summary: First congress in Shanghai established the CCP with Comintern support.

name: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
summary: Autonomous Chinese territory whose freedoms narrowed after the 2019 protests and 2020 national security law.

name: British Hong Kong
summary: Crown colony ceded in 1842 and leased in 1898 that became a global financial centre.

name: Handover of Hong Kong
summary: Transfer of sovereignty to China on 1 July 1997 under 'one country, two systems'.

name: Hong Kong Protests of 2019
summary: Mass movement against an extradition bill, answered by Beijing's national security law.

name: Hundred Days' Reform
summary: Guangxu Emperor's rapid reform programme, ended by Cixi's coup.

name: Late Ming Dynasty
summary: Silver-fuelled commerce, population growth and crisis ending in rebellion, famine and Manchu conquest.

name: Long March
summary: Communist retreat of some 9,000 kilometres during which Mao secured party leadership.

name: Macau Special Administrative Region
summary: Chinese special administrative region and the world's largest gambling centre.

name: Manchu Conquest of China
summary: Qing conquest from Beijing's fall in 1644 to the taking of Taiwan in 1683.

name: May Fourth Movement
summary: Student protests against the Versailles settlement that catalysed Chinese nationalism and the New Culture Movement.

name: Nanjing Massacre
summary: Mass killing and rape of Chinese civilians and prisoners after the fall of Nanjing.

name: Nixon's Visit to China
summary: Opening of relations that realigned Cold War diplomacy; the PRC took China's UN seat in 1971.

name: Northern Expedition
summary: Chiang Kai-shek's campaign that nominally unified China under the Kuomintang.

name: Portuguese Macau
summary: Oldest European settlement in East Asia, returned to China in 1999.

name: Belt and Road Initiative
summary: Global infrastructure and lending programme announced by Xi Jinping in 2013.

name: Reform and Opening Up
summary: Market reforms that lifted hundreds of millions from poverty and made China a manufacturing superpower.

name: Cultural Revolution
summary: Mao's mass campaign against 'revisionists' that closed schools, destroyed heritage and killed over a million.

name: Deng Xiaoping Era
summary: Reform and opening: household farming, special economic zones, and the Tiananmen crackdown.

name: Great Leap Forward
summary: Forced collectivisation and industrial campaign that caused a famine killing tens of millions.

name: Hu Jintao Era
summary: Rapid growth, the 2008 Beijing Olympics and stimulus after the global financial crisis.

name: Jiang Zemin Era
summary: Consolidation after Tiananmen, WTO accession and the Hong Kong and Macau handovers.

name: Mao Era
summary: Land reform, Korean War, Great Leap Forward famine and Cultural Revolution under Mao Zedong.

name: One-Child Policy
summary: Coercive birth-limitation programme that reshaped China's demography.

name: Tiananmen Square Protests and Massacre
summary: Seven weeks of pro-democracy protests ended by military force on 3-4 June 1989.

name: Xi Jinping Era
summary: Anti-corruption campaign, Belt and Road, term-limit abolition, Xinjiang repression and zero-COVID.

name: February 28 Incident
summary: Nationalist suppression of a Taiwanese uprising, followed by the White Terror.

name: Japanese Taiwan
summary: Fifty years of Japanese colonial rule that industrialised the island.

name: Nanjing Decade
summary: Decade of Nationalist state-building interrupted by communist insurgency and Japanese encroachment.

name: Republic of China on Taiwan
summary: Nationalist government relocated to Taipei in 1949; now a democracy claimed by the PRC.

name: Taiwanese Martial Law Period
summary: Thirty-eight years of one-party Kuomintang rule under martial law and the White Terror.

name: Taiwanese Democratisation
summary: Lifting of martial law, party competition and the first direct presidential election in 1996.

name: Rule of Yuan Shikai
summary: First president who dissolved parliament and briefly proclaimed himself emperor in 1916.

name: Second Opium War
summary: Anglo-French campaign that burned the Summer Palace and opened more of China to foreign trade and missions.

name: Self-Strengthening Movement
summary: Reform effort to adopt Western arms and industry while preserving Confucian institutions.

name: Sino-Soviet Split
summary: Ideological and strategic rupture between the communist giants, including border clashes in 1969.

name: Taiping Rebellion
summary: Millenarian civil war under Hong Xiuquan that killed perhaps 20-30 million people.

name: Unequal Treaties
summary: Century of imposed treaties granting extraterritoriality, indemnities and concessions to foreign powers.

name: Warlord Era
summary: Fragmentation of China among regional militarists after Yuan Shikai's death.

name: Xinhai Revolution
summary: Wuchang uprising and provincial secessions that ended two millennia of imperial rule.

name: First Sino-Japanese War
summary: Japanese victory that took Taiwan and ended Chinese suzerainty over Korea.

name: Premierships of Shinzo Abe
summary: Japan's longest-serving prime minister (2006-07, 2012-20): Abenomics, security reinterpretation, assassinated in 2022.

name: Atomic Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
summary: First use of nuclear weapons in war, killing well over 100,000 and hastening Japan's surrender.

name: Battle of Okinawa
summary: Eighty-two-day battle that killed perhaps a quarter of Okinawan civilians; US administration lasted to 1972.

name: Battle of Sekigahara
summary: Tokugawa Ieyasu's decisive victory that opened the way to the shogunate.

name: Boshin War
summary: Civil war in which imperial loyalists defeated the shogunate and restored direct rule to the emperor.

name: Sakoku
summary: Policy of closed borders permitting only limited Dutch, Chinese, Korean and Ryukyuan contact.

name: Shimabara Rebellion
summary: Christian and peasant revolt in Kyushu whose suppression sealed the proscription of Christianity.

name: Empire of Japan
summary: Constitutional empire that industrialised, defeated China and Russia, built a colonial empire and lost the Pacific War.

name: Meiji Constitution
summary: Prussian-inspired constitution granting a Diet while vesting sovereignty in the emperor.

name: Meiji Era
summary: Reign of Emperor Meiji: abolition of the samurai class, conscription, industry, constitution and imperial expansion.

name: Taisho Era
summary: Reign of Emperor Taisho: party cabinets, universal male suffrage, rice riots and the 1923 Kanto earthquake.

name: February 26 Incident
summary: Failed young-officers' coup in Tokyo after which the army dominated the government.

name: Great Kanto Earthquake
summary: Quake and firestorm that destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama and killed over 100,000.

name: Heisei Era
summary: Reign of Emperor Akihito: bubble collapse, Kobe earthquake, Aum attack and the 2011 triple disaster.

name: Japanese Asset Price Bubble and Lost Decades
summary: Stock and land bubble whose collapse produced prolonged stagnation and deflation.

name: Constitution of Japan
summary: Postwar constitution establishing popular sovereignty, a symbolic emperor and Article 9's renunciation of war.

name: Japanese Economic Miracle
summary: Two decades of double-digit growth that made Japan an industrial giant, symbolised by the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

name: Great Hanshin Earthquake
summary: Kobe earthquake that killed over 6,000 and exposed weaknesses in disaster response.

name: Manchurian Incident
summary: Staged railway explosion used to justify the Japanese conquest of Manchuria.

name: Meiji Restoration
summary: Restoration of imperial rule and the start of rapid, state-led modernisation on Western models.

name: Abolition of the Han
summary: Domains replaced by prefectures, ending feudal decentralisation.

name: Satsuma Rebellion
summary: Last samurai revolt, led by Saigo Takamori and crushed by the conscript army.

name: Allied Occupation of Japan
summary: MacArthur's SCAP administration demilitarised Japan, wrote a new constitution and reformed land and industry.

name: Rule of Oda Nobunaga
summary: Warlord who seized Kyoto, broke the Buddhist militant orders and began unifying Japan before being betrayed at Honno-ji.

name: Reversion of Okinawa
summary: Return of Okinawa to Japanese sovereignty, with US bases remaining.

name: Perry Expedition
summary: American gunboat diplomacy that forced Japan open with the Convention of Kanagawa.

name: Reiwa Era
summary: Reign of Emperor Naruhito, beginning with his father's abdication in 2019.

name: Kingdom of Ryukyu (late)
summary: Okinawan maritime kingdom, a Satsuma vassal from 1609, annexed as Okinawa Prefecture in 1879.

name: Late Sengoku Period
summary: Century of warring daimyo, firearms and castle towns, unified in stages by Nobunaga, Hideyoshi and Ieyasu.

name: Showa Era
summary: Reign of Emperor Hirohito: militarism, war, defeat, occupation and the postwar economic miracle.

name: Japan
summary: Postwar parliamentary state under the 1947 constitution, long the world's second-largest economy.

name: Taisho Democracy
summary: Era of party government, mass politics and liberal culture, ended by militarist assassinations.

name: Tohoku Earthquake and Fukushima Disaster
summary: Magnitude 9 quake, tsunami killing about 18,000, and the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear meltdowns.

name: Rule of Toyotomi Hideyoshi
summary: Completed unification, froze the social order by sword hunts and land surveys, and invaded Korea twice.

name: Treaty of San Francisco
summary: Peace treaty restoring Japanese sovereignty, accompanied by the US-Japan security treaty.

name: Gwangju Uprising
summary: Pro-democracy revolt crushed by paratroopers under Chun Doo-hwan with hundreds killed.

name: Rule of Kim Il-sung
summary: Founding leader who built the juche system and a hereditary personality cult.

name: Rule of Kim Jong-il
summary: Ruled through the 1990s famine and the first nuclear test, under 'military first' policy.

name: Rule of Kim Jong-un
summary: Third-generation leader who expanded the nuclear and missile programmes and met US and South Korean leaders.

name: June Democratic Struggle
summary: Mass protests that forced direct presidential elections and the end of military rule.

name: Miracle on the Han River
summary: Transformation from postwar poverty to an advanced industrial economy led by chaebol conglomerates.

name: North Korean Famine
summary: Famine after Soviet aid ended that killed hundreds of thousands.

name: Rule of Park Chung-hee
summary: Military strongman who drove export-led industrialisation under the repressive Yushin system; assassinated in 1979.

name: Presidency of Syngman Rhee
summary: Authoritarian founding president, ousted by the April Revolution.

name: Division of Korea
summary: American and Soviet occupation zones split at the 38th parallel, hardening into two states.

name: Imjin War
summary: Hideyoshi's two invasions of Korea, repelled with Ming aid and Admiral Yi Sun-sin's naval victories.

name: Japanese Annexation of Korea
summary: Treaty imposed after the 1905 protectorate made Korea a Japanese colony until 1945.

name: Japanese Colonial Rule in Korea
summary: Thirty-five years of colonial rule with land expropriation, assimilation policy and wartime forced labour.

name: Late Joseon Dynasty
summary: Neo-Confucian kingdom that survived the Imjin and Manchu invasions and pursued isolation until forced open.

name: March First Movement
summary: Nationwide independence demonstrations suppressed with thousands killed.

name: Manchukuo
summary: Japanese puppet state in Manchuria nominally headed by the last Qing emperor Puyi.

name: Mongolia
summary: Democratic parliamentary republic since 1992 with a mining-based economy.

name: Bogd Khanate of Mongolia
summary: Theocratic Mongolian state under the Jebtsundamba Khutughtu after the Qing collapse.

name: Mongolian People's Republic
summary: Second communist state in the world, a Soviet satellite with purges of the Buddhist clergy.

name: Qing Mongolia
summary: Outer and Inner Mongolia under Qing administration through the Manchu-Mongol aristocratic system.

name: Pacific War
summary: War between Japan and the Allies from Pearl Harbor to the surrender aboard USS Missouri.

name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
summary: Japanese carrier strike on 7 December 1941 that brought the United States into the Second World War.

name: Russo-Japanese War
summary: Japan's victory over Russia at Port Arthur, Mukden and Tsushima, the first modern Asian defeat of a European power.

name: Second Sino-Japanese War
summary: Full-scale Japanese invasion of China, part of the Second World War, with 15-20 million Chinese deaths.

name: Taiwan Strait Crises
summary: Series of military confrontations between the PRC and Taiwan involving American intervention.

name: Principality of Andorra
summary: Pyrenean co-principality under the Spanish bishop of Urgell and the French head of state; parliamentary since 1993.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
summary: Independent state since 1992, governed since Dayton as a federation of two entities with international oversight.

name: Bosnian War
summary: Three-way war with the siege of Sarajevo and genocide at Srebrenica, ended by the Dayton Agreement.

name: Dayton Agreement
summary: US-brokered peace ending the Bosnian War and creating a federal state of two entities.

name: Srebrenica Genocide
summary: Massacre of over 8,000 Bosniak men and boys by Bosnian Serb forces in a UN safe area.

name: Austro-Hungarian Empire
summary: Multinational dual monarchy of eleven major nationalities that dissolved in defeat in 1918.

name: Battle of Vienna
summary: Polish, Imperial and German relief army under Jan III Sobieski broke the Ottoman siege of Vienna.

name: Battle of White Mountain
summary: Catholic victory outside Prague that ended Bohemian independence and began forced re-Catholicisation.

name: Czech Republic
summary: Central European republic since 1993, in NATO from 1999 and the EU from 2004.

name: Czechoslovakia
summary: State of Czechs and Slovaks founded in 1918, dismembered in 1938-39, communist from 1948, split in 1993.

name: Czechoslovak Coup of 1948
summary: Communist seizure of power in February 1948 that ended postwar pluralism.

name: Presidency of Tomas Masaryk
summary: Founding president who made interwar Czechoslovakia central Europe's most durable democracy.

name: Prague Spring
summary: Dubcek's 'socialism with a human face', crushed by a Warsaw Pact invasion in August 1968.

name: Sudeten Crisis and Annexation
summary: German-speaking borderlands ceded under the Munich Agreement, followed by occupation in March 1939.

name: Velvet Divorce
summary: Peaceful split of Czechoslovakia into the Czech Republic and Slovakia on 1 January 1993.

name: Velvet Revolution
summary: Non-violent mass protests that ended communist rule and made Vaclav Havel president.

name: Defenestration of Prague
summary: Bohemian Protestants threw imperial regents from a castle window, triggering the Thirty Years' War.

name: Bismarck's Chancellorship
summary: Otto von Bismarck governed the new empire, building alliances abroad and social insurance and anti-socialist laws at home.

name: Reign of Wilhelm I
summary: First German emperor, whose reign under Bismarck saw unification, the Kulturkampf and the first welfare state.

name: Reign of Wilhelm II
summary: Last German emperor: naval race, Weltpolitik, the First World War and abdication in November 1918.

name: Year of the Three Emperors
summary: Wilhelm I, Friedrich III and Wilhelm II all reigned in 1888; Friedrich III ruled only 99 days.

name: Allied Occupation of Germany
summary: Four-power division of Germany, denazification, the Nuremberg trials and the Berlin airlift, ending with two German states.

name: Anschluss
summary: German annexation of Austria in March 1938, endorsed by a rigged plebiscite.

name: Austro-Prussian War
summary: Seven Weeks' War in which Prussia's victory at Koniggratz excluded Austria from Germany.

name: Berlin Blockade and Airlift
summary: Soviet closure of land routes to West Berlin, defeated by an eleven-month Western airlift.

name: Berlin Wall
summary: Fortified barrier sealing West Berlin from 1961, the Cold War's central symbol, opened on 9 November 1989.

name: Brandenburg-Prussia
summary: Hohenzollern union of Brandenburg and Prussia built into a military-bureaucratic state by the Great Elector.

name: Chancellorship of Angela Merkel
summary: First woman chancellor; steered Germany through the eurozone crisis, the 2015 refugee influx and COVID-19.

name: Chancellorship of Friedrich Merz
summary: CDU chancellor from 2025 heading a coalition with the Social Democrats.

name: Chancellorship of Gerhard Schroder
summary: SPD-Green government: Kosovo deployment, Agenda 2010 labour reforms, refusal to join the Iraq war.

name: Chancellorship of Helmut Kohl
summary: Longest-serving postwar chancellor; delivered reunification in 1990 and pushed the euro at Maastricht.

name: Chancellorship of Helmut Schmidt
summary: Managed oil shocks, the Red Army Faction's German Autumn and NATO's missile deployment.

name: Chancellorship of Konrad Adenauer
summary: First West German chancellor: Western integration, NATO entry, reconciliation with France and Israel.

name: Chancellorship of Kurt Georg Kiesinger
summary: Led the first grand coalition of CDU and SPD.

name: Chancellorship of Ludwig Erhard
summary: Architect of the social market economy who succeeded Adenauer as chancellor.

name: Chancellorship of Olaf Scholz
summary: Led a three-party coalition through the Zeitenwende response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine and an energy crisis.

name: Chancellorship of Willy Brandt
summary: Social Democrat who pursued Ostpolitik, knelt at the Warsaw Ghetto memorial and won the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Confederation of the Rhine
summary: Napoleonic client league of German states whose creation ended the Holy Roman Empire.

name: German Democratic Republic (East Germany)
summary: Communist state in the Soviet zone, ruled by the SED, dissolved when it acceded to the Federal Republic in 1990.

name: East German Uprising of 1953
summary: Workers' strikes and protests on 17 June 1953 crushed by Soviet tanks.

name: Federal Republic of Germany
summary: Reunified democratic Germany, the European Union's largest economy, with its capital returned to Berlin.

name: Frankfurt Parliament
summary: First freely elected all-German assembly; drafted a liberal constitution that Prussia's king refused.

name: German Confederation
summary: Loose association of 39 German states created at Vienna under Austrian presidency, dissolved after the 1866 war.

name: German Reunification
summary: On 3 October 1990 the GDR acceded to the Federal Republic under the Two Plus Four Treaty.

name: German Revolution of 1918-19
summary: Naval mutiny and workers' councils toppled the monarchy and produced the Weimar Republic amid failed communist risings.

name: German Unification of 1871
summary: Proclamation of the German Empire at Versailles on 18 January 1871, completing Bismarck's unification by war and diplomacy.

name: Holy Roman Empire (Early Modern)
summary: Loose confederation of hundreds of German states under an elected emperor, dissolved by Napoleon in 1806.

name: Kingdom of Prussia
summary: Hohenzollern kingdom that rose to great-power status, led German unification and dominated the German Empire.

name: Reign of Frederick the Great
summary: Frederick II seized Silesia, survived the Seven Years' War and made Prussia a great power while patronising the Enlightenment.

name: Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact
summary: Nazi-Soviet non-aggression pact with secret protocols dividing Eastern Europe, signed days before war.

name: North German Confederation
summary: Prussian-dominated federal state that became the framework for the German Empire.

name: Nuremberg Trials
summary: International Military Tribunal that tried surviving Nazi leaders and established modern precedents for crimes against humanity.

name: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
summary: Bolshevik peace with Germany that surrendered Ukraine, the Baltics and Poland, annulled in November 1918.

name: Zollverein
summary: Prussian-led customs union that economically integrated Germany ahead of political unification.

name: Habsburg Monarchy
summary: Composite realm of Austria, Bohemia and Hungary that anchored Catholic Europe and fought the Ottomans and Prussia.

name: Reign of Joseph II
summary: Radical enlightened absolutist who abolished serfdom and issued the Patent of Toleration.

name: Reign of Maria Theresa
summary: Only female ruler of the Habsburg lands: survived the succession war, lost Silesia and reformed the state.

name: Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867
summary: Agreement creating the Dual Monarchy with separate Austrian and Hungarian governments under one emperor-king.

name: Austro-Hungarian Annexation of Bosnia
summary: Formal annexation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, inflaming Serbian nationalism and Russian rivalry.

name: Reign of Charles I of Austria
summary: Last Habsburg emperor, whose peace efforts failed and whose empire dissolved in 1918.

name: Reign of Franz Joseph I
summary: Sixty-eight-year reign spanning 1848, the Compromise of 1867, and the outbreak of the First World War.

name: Peace of Augsburg
summary: Settlement letting each German prince choose Lutheranism or Catholicism for his territory, cuius regio eius religio.

name: Kingdom of Bohemia under the Habsburgs
summary: Bohemian crown lands within the Habsburg realm, Germanised after 1620 and industrialised in the 19th century.

name: Hitler's Rule of Germany
summary: Adolf Hitler as chancellor and Fuhrer held dictatorial power from 1933 until his suicide in Berlin in April 1945.

name: Kristallnacht
summary: November 1938 pogrom that destroyed synagogues and Jewish businesses across Germany and Austria.

name: Nuremberg Laws
summary: Racial laws stripping German Jews of citizenship and criminalising intermarriage.

name: Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
summary: German protectorate over the Czech lands, site of Heydrich's assassination and the Lidice massacre.

name: Beer Hall Putsch
summary: Hitler's failed Munich coup, after which he wrote Mein Kampf in prison.

name: German Hyperinflation of 1923
summary: Currency collapse that destroyed savings and discredited the young republic before the Rentenmark stabilisation.

name: Cod Wars
summary: Disputes with Britain over fishing limits that Iceland won, extending its zone to 200 miles.

name: Icelandic Sovereignty and Republic
summary: Iceland became a sovereign kingdom in personal union with Denmark in 1918 and a republic in 1944.

name: Republic of Iceland
summary: Republic declared in 1944, NATO founder, hit hard by the 2008 banking collapse.

name: North Macedonia
summary: Independent since 1991; renamed under the 2018 Prespa Agreement and a NATO member since 2020.

name: Concert of Europe
summary: System of great-power consultation and congresses that limited general European war for a century.

name: Congress of Vienna
summary: Great-power settlement that redrew Europe's map, restored monarchies and created a balance of power lasting decades.

name: Continental System
summary: Napoleon's blockade of British trade, which damaged European economies and provoked the Peninsular and Russian wars.

name: Council of Europe
summary: Pan-European human rights body that created the European Convention and its court.

name: Balkan Wars
summary: Two wars that expelled the Ottomans from most of Europe and then set the victors against each other over Macedonia.

name: Congress of Berlin
summary: Great-power settlement that recognised Serbia, Montenegro and Romania and shrank Bulgaria.

name: Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
summary: Rump federation of Serbia and Montenegro under Slobodan Milosevic, renamed Serbia and Montenegro in 2003.

name: Axis Invasion of Yugoslavia
summary: German-led attack that dismembered the kingdom and produced the Ustase state and partisan resistance.

name: Crimean Khanate
summary: Tatar successor of the Golden Horde, an Ottoman vassal and slave-raiding power, annexed by Russia in 1783.

name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia
summary: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes renamed Yugoslavia in 1929, a royal dictatorship destroyed by Axis invasion.
aliases: Kingdom of Serbs Croats and Slovenes

name: Kosovo War
summary: Insurgency and Serbian counter-offensive that triggered NATO's 78-day bombing campaign and UN administration.

name: Constitution of 3 May 1791
summary: Europe's first modern codified constitution, an attempt at reform that provoked partition.

name: The Deluge
summary: Swedish and Russian invasions that devastated Poland-Lithuania and began its long decline.

name: Republic of Kosovo
summary: Declared independence from Serbia in 2008, recognised by about half the world's states.

name: Presidency of Dmitry Medvedev
summary: Interim presidency with Putin as premier; the 2008 Georgia war and the financial crisis.

name: Rule of Vladimir Putin
summary: President from 2000 (prime minister 2008-12), centralising power, curbing media and pursuing war in Ukraine.

name: Presidency of Boris Yeltsin
summary: First Russian president: market shock therapy, the 1993 constitutional crisis, Chechnya and the 1998 default.

name: Decembrist Revolt
summary: Failed liberal officers' coup at Nicholas I's accession, followed by decades of repression.

name: Emancipation of the Serfs
summary: Alexander II's manifesto freeing some 23 million serfs, with land redemption payments.

name: Pugachev's Rebellion
summary: Massive Cossack and peasant revolt suppressed by Catherine II, hardening noble control over serfs.

name: Reign of Alexander I of Russia
summary: Tsar who defeated Napoleon's invasion, entered Paris and shaped the Holy Alliance at Vienna.

name: Reign of Alexander II
summary: Tsar-liberator who emancipated the serfs and reformed law and local government; assassinated in 1881.

name: Reign of Alexander III
summary: Counter-reforming tsar of Russification, pogroms and rapid railway-led industrialisation.

name: Reign of Catherine the Great
summary: Enlightened empress who annexed Crimea and much of Poland, expanded serfdom and corresponded with the philosophes.

name: Reign of Nicholas I
summary: Autocracy of orthodoxy and censorship, the 'gendarme of Europe', ending in defeat in the Crimean War.

name: Reign of Nicholas II
summary: Last tsar: defeat by Japan, the 1905 revolution, the Duma, war in 1914 and abdication in 1917.

name: Russian Revolution of 1905
summary: Bloody Sunday, mass strikes and mutinies forced Nicholas II to grant the October Manifesto and a Duma.

name: Serbia and Montenegro
summary: Loose state union that dissolved when Montenegro voted for independence in 2006.

name: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
summary: Tito's federation of six republics, non-aligned and self-managing, which disintegrated in war after his death.

name: Andropov and Chernenko Interregnum
summary: Two brief, ailing general secretaries between Brezhnev and Gorbachev.

name: Brezhnev Era
summary: Stagnation and stability: Prague Spring suppression, detente, oil-funded consumerism and the Afghan invasion.

name: Chernobyl Disaster
summary: Reactor explosion on 26 April 1986 that spread radiation across Europe and discredited Soviet secrecy.

name: Gorbachev Era
summary: Perestroika, glasnost and arms control that ended the Cold War and unintentionally dissolved the USSR.

name: Great Patriotic War
summary: Soviet war against Germany from Barbarossa to Berlin, with roughly 27 million Soviet dead.

name: Great Purge
summary: Stalin's terror: show trials, mass executions of some 700,000 people and destruction of the party and army leadership.

name: Gulag System
summary: Vast network of forced-labour camps that held millions of prisoners, wound down after Stalin's death.

name: Khrushchev Era
summary: De-Stalinisation, the Secret Speech, Sputnik, the Virgin Lands and the Cuban missile crisis, ending in his ouster.

name: Khrushchev Thaw
summary: Relative cultural and political liberalisation after the denunciation of Stalin's crimes.

name: New Economic Policy
summary: Partial market restoration in agriculture and small trade that revived the economy after war communism.

name: August Coup
summary: Failed hardline putsch against Gorbachev that accelerated the union's collapse and Yeltsin's rise.

name: Soviet Collectivisation
summary: Forced collectivisation of agriculture and dekulakisation, causing famine across Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Russia.

name: Rule of Josip Broz Tito
summary: Partisan leader turned president for life who split with Stalin in 1948 and led the Non-Aligned Movement.

name: Reign of Ivan IV the Terrible
summary: First crowned tsar; conquered Kazan and Astrakhan, launched the Livonian War and terrorised the boyars with the oprichnina.

name: Yugoslav Wars
summary: Series of wars accompanying Yugoslavia's breakup, with ethnic cleansing, siege warfare and NATO intervention.

name: EU Enlargement of 2004
summary: Ten mostly post-communist states joined the European Union, the largest single enlargement.

name: Introduction of the Euro
summary: Single currency launched for accounting in 1999 and as cash in 2002, now used by 20 states.

name: European Coal and Steel Community
summary: Six-nation pooling of coal and steel, the first step of European integration.

name: European Economic Community
summary: Common market of six then twelve states that became the European Union at Maastricht.

name: European Migrant Crisis
summary: Arrival of over a million asylum seekers, mainly from Syria, straining EU cohesion and border policy.

name: European Union
summary: Union of 27 states with a single market, common currency for most members and supranational institutions.

name: Eurozone Debt Crisis
summary: Sovereign-debt crisis in Greece, Ireland, Portugal, Spain and Cyprus that tested monetary union.

name: February Revolution
summary: Petrograd bread riots and mutiny toppled the tsar and created a Provisional Government and soviets.

name: First Chechen War
summary: Russian invasion of separatist Chechnya ending in a humiliating ceasefire at Khasavyurt.

name: Founding of St Petersburg
summary: Peter I founded his new capital on the Neva as a window on Europe.

name: French Invasion of Russia
summary: Napoleon's Grande Armee reached Moscow and was destroyed in retreat, losing most of half a million men.

name: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
summary: Grand duchy created at Vienna, fully independent since 1839-1890, a founding member of the European communities.

name: Helsinki Final Act
summary: Agreement recognising postwar borders while committing signatories to human rights, empowering dissidents.

name: House of Romanov
summary: Dynasty that ruled Russia for three centuries, from Michael I to Nicholas II.

name: Ukraine
summary: Independent since the 1991 referendum; the Orange Revolution, Euromaidan and war with Russia have shaped its statehood.

name: Russian Annexation of Crimea
summary: Russian forces seized Crimea and staged a referendum, triggering Western sanctions and war in the Donbas.

name: Cossack Hetmanate
summary: Cossack state under Khmelnytsky that allied with Muscovy at Pereiaslav and was absorbed by Russia.

name: Euromaidan
summary: Kyiv protests against a shelved EU agreement that ousted President Yanukovych.

name: Holodomor
summary: Man-made famine in Soviet Ukraine that killed roughly four million people, recognised by many states as genocide.

name: Orange Revolution
summary: Mass protests that overturned a rigged presidential election in favour of Viktor Yushchenko.

name: Russian Invasion of Ukraine
summary: Full-scale Russian invasion from 24 February 2022, Europe's largest war since 1945.

name: Ukrainian People's Republic
summary: Short-lived independent Ukraine under Hrushevsky, Skoropadsky and Petliura, defeated by Bolshevik forces.

name: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic
summary: Soviet Ukraine, site of the Holodomor, brutal Nazi occupation and postwar industrialisation.

name: War in Donbas
summary: Russian-backed separatist conflict in eastern Ukraine that killed over 13,000 before the full invasion.

name: Iron Curtain
