summary: Division of Europe between Soviet-dominated east and Western-aligned west, symbolised by Churchill's 1946 speech.

name: Italian Republic
summary: Republic established by the 1946 referendum, a founding member of NATO and the European communities.

name: Capture of Rome
summary: Italian troops breached Porta Pia on 20 September 1870, ending papal temporal rule and completing unification.

name: Spanish then Austrian Milan
summary: Duchy of Milan ruled by Habsburg Spain and then Austria before the Napoleonic conquest.

name: Expedition of the Thousand
summary: Garibaldi's volunteers conquered Sicily and Naples and handed the south to Victor Emmanuel II.

name: Fascist Italy
summary: Mussolini's one-party regime: Lateran Pacts, Ethiopian conquest, Axis alliance and wartime collapse.

name: First Italian War of Independence
summary: Piedmontese and revolutionary attempt to expel Austria from northern Italy, defeated at Custoza and Novara.

name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
summary: Medici then Habsburg-Lorraine state centred on Florence, absorbed into unified Italy.

name: Italian Social Republic
summary: German-backed Salo Republic under Mussolini in northern Italy, fought by the partisan Resistance.

name: Italian Wars
summary: Six decades of conflict over Italy between France, Spain and the Habsburgs, ending in Spanish dominance of the peninsula.

name: Years of Lead
summary: Two decades of left- and right-wing terrorism in Italy, including the Red Brigades' murder of Aldo Moro.

name: Italo-Turkish War
summary: Italian conquest of Libya and the Dodecanese from the Ottomans.

name: Kingdom of Italy
summary: Unified Italian monarchy proclaimed in 1861, which annexed Venetia and Rome, fought both world wars and fell to fascism.

name: Reign of Umberto I
summary: King during colonial expansion in Eritrea and the defeat at Adwa; assassinated by an anarchist in 1900.

name: Reign of Victor Emmanuel II
summary: First king of united Italy, who annexed Venetia in 1866 and Rome in 1870.

name: Reign of Victor Emmanuel III
summary: King who took Italy into the First World War, appointed Mussolini, dismissed him in 1943 and abdicated in 1946.

name: Kingdom of Naples (Early Modern)
summary: Spanish then Austrian then Bourbon kingdom of southern Italy, merged into the Two Sicilies in 1816.

name: Kingdom of Sardinia
summary: Savoyard state based in Piedmont that led the Risorgimento and became the Kingdom of Italy.

name: Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
summary: Bourbon kingdom of southern Italy and Sicily, conquered by Garibaldi's volunteers in 1860.

name: Lateran Treaty
summary: Agreement creating Vatican City and settling the Roman Question between Italy and the papacy.

name: March on Rome
summary: Fascist mobilisation that led the king to appoint Mussolini prime minister in October 1922.

name: Papal States (Early Modern to 1870)
summary: Territorial dominion of the popes across central Italy, reduced in 1860 and ended by the capture of Rome in 1870.

name: Republic of Genoa (late)
summary: Banking and maritime republic tied to Habsburg Spain, annexed to Napoleon's Ligurian Republic.

name: Republic of Venice (late)
summary: Declining maritime republic that lost Cyprus and Crete to the Ottomans and was extinguished by Napoleon in 1797.

name: Risorgimento
summary: Movement of ideas, wars and diplomacy that unified Italy under the House of Savoy.

name: Roman Republic of 1849
summary: Short-lived republic led by Mazzini and defended by Garibaldi until French troops restored the Pope.

name: Republic of San Marino
summary: Ancient micro-republic in the Apennines that preserved independence through Italian unification.

name: Second Italian War of Independence
summary: Franco-Piedmontese victory over Austria at Magenta and Solferino won Lombardy for Piedmont.

name: Third Italian War of Independence
summary: Italy's war alongside Prussia against Austria, which gained Venetia despite defeats at Custoza and Lissa.

name: Vatican City
summary: Sovereign city-state created in 1929 as the seat of the papacy, the world's smallest state.

name: Kingdom of Belgium
summary: Constitutional monarchy independent since 1830, twice invaded by Germany, now a federal state and EU seat.

name: Federalisation of Belgium
summary: Series of state reforms that turned unitary Belgium into a federation of language communities and regions.

name: Belgian Revolution
summary: Brussels rising against Dutch rule that created an independent, neutral Belgium recognised in 1839.

name: Reign of Albert I of Belgium
summary: Knight-king who led Belgian resistance to the German invasion of 1914.

name: Reign of King Baudouin
summary: King during Congolese independence and the federalisation of Belgium.

name: Reign of Leopold I of Belgium
summary: First king of the Belgians, who secured recognition and neutrality for the new state.

name: Reign of Leopold II of Belgium
summary: King who ran the Congo Free State as personal property, causing mass death, and industrialised Belgium.

name: Reign of Leopold III of Belgium
summary: Surrendered in 1940 and remained in occupied Belgium; abdicated after the postwar Royal Question.

name: Kingdom of Denmark
summary: Europe's oldest continuous monarchy, constitutional since 1849, occupied 1940-45, an EU member since 1973.

name: Danish Absolutism
summary: Hereditary absolute monarchy codified in the Lex Regia of 1665, ended by the 1849 constitution.

name: Danish June Constitution
summary: Constitution ending absolutism and creating a bicameral parliament.

name: First Schleswig War
summary: Danish victory over Schleswig-Holstein German nationalists and their German allies.

name: Greenland Home Rule and Self-Government
summary: Greenland gained home rule in 1979, extended to self-government in 2009 within the Danish realm.

name: Reign of Christian X of Denmark
summary: King during the Easter Crisis, Icelandic separation and the German occupation, when he became a symbol of resistance.

name: Reign of Frederik X
summary: King of Denmark since January 2024.

name: Reign of Margrethe II
summary: Denmark's first queen regnant in modern times, who abdicated in 2024 after 52 years.

name: Second Schleswig War
summary: Prussian-Austrian defeat of Denmark, which lost Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg.

name: Kingdom of Norway
summary: Independent constitutional monarchy since the 1905 dissolution of the union with Sweden; oil wealth since the 1970s.

name: Norwegian Constitution of 1814
summary: Eidsvoll assembly's liberal constitution, still in force and celebrated on 17 May.

name: Dissolution of the Union with Sweden
summary: Peaceful separation confirmed by referendum, with Prince Carl of Denmark crowned Haakon VII.

name: German Occupation of Norway
summary: Five years of German rule under Quisling's collaborationist administration.

name: Reign of Haakon VII
summary: First king of independent Norway, who refused to legitimise the German occupation and led resistance from London.

name: Reign of Harald V
summary: King of Norway since 1991.

name: Kingdom of Spain
summary: Parliamentary monarchy since Franco's death, a member of the EU since 1986 and NATO since 1982.

name: Bourbon Restoration in Spain
summary: Restored monarchy under Alfonso XII and Alfonso XIII with alternating parties, the 1898 disaster and Rivera's dictatorship.

name: Bourbon Spain
summary: Reforming Bourbon monarchy that centralised administration and reorganised the American empire.

name: Reign of Charles III of Spain
summary: Enlightened absolutist who reformed the empire, expelled the Jesuits and modernised Madrid.

name: Constitution of Cadiz
summary: Liberal constitution of 1812 that inspired constitutionalism across Spain and Latin America.

name: Carlist Wars
summary: Three dynastic civil wars between supporters of Don Carlos and the liberal monarchy of Isabella II.

name: Catalan Independence Crisis
summary: Unauthorised referendum and unilateral declaration in Catalonia met by direct rule from Madrid.

name: First Spanish Republic
summary: Short-lived federal republic with four presidents in eleven months, ended by a military coup.

name: Francoist Spain
summary: Franco's authoritarian regime: repression, autarky then technocratic growth, ending with his death in 1975.

name: Habsburg Spain
summary: Spain under the Austrias, ruling a global empire from the Americas to the Philippines before dynastic extinction in 1700.

name: Reign of Charles II of Spain
summary: Last Habsburg king of Spain, childless, whose death triggered the War of the Spanish Succession.

name: Reign of Charles V
summary: Ruled Spain, the Netherlands, Naples and the Holy Roman Empire; faced Luther and the Ottomans before abdicating.

name: Reign of Philip II of Spain
summary: Height of Spanish power: Lepanto, annexation of Portugal, the Dutch Revolt and the Armada's failure.

name: Reign of Philip III of Spain
summary: Reign of truce with the Dutch and the expulsion of the Moriscos.

name: Reign of Philip IV of Spain
summary: Golden-age culture amid decline: loss of the Dutch and Portugal, Catalan revolt and defeat by France.

name: Dictatorship of Primo de Rivera
summary: Military dictatorship under Alfonso XIII that modernised infrastructure but collapsed in the Depression.

name: Reign of Felipe VI
summary: King since 2014, whose reign has confronted the Catalan independence crisis of 2017.

name: Reign of Isabella II of Spain
summary: Turbulent reign of civil war and pronunciamientos, ended by the Glorious Revolution of 1868.

name: Reign of Juan Carlos I
summary: King who oversaw the democratic transition and faced down the 1981 coup attempt; abdicated in 2014.

name: Second Spanish Republic
summary: Democratic republic of land reform, regional autonomy and polarisation, destroyed by the Civil War.

name: Spanish-American War
summary: War that stripped Spain of Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines, the 'Disaster of 98'.

name: Spanish Civil War
summary: Nationalist rebels under Franco, aided by Germany and Italy, defeated the Republic, aided by the USSR and volunteers.

name: Spanish Transition to Democracy
summary: Dismantling of Francoism under Juan Carlos I and Adolfo Suarez, producing the 1978 constitution.

name: Kingdom of Sweden
summary: Continuous Swedish state since 1523, neutral through both world wars, an EU member from 1995 and NATO from 2024.

name: House of Bernadotte
summary: Dynasty founded by Napoleon's marshal Jean Bernadotte, still reigning in Sweden.

name: House of Vasa
summary: Dynasty that made Sweden Protestant, hereditary and a great power in the Baltic.

name: Reign of Carl XVI Gustaf
summary: Swedish king since 1973 under the 1974 instrument of government that stripped royal political power.

name: Reign of Queen Christina
summary: Learned queen who ended the Thirty Years' War, then abdicated and converted to Catholicism.

name: Reign of Gustaf V of Sweden
summary: Longest-reigning modern Swedish king, on the throne through both world wars and the rise of social democracy.

name: Reign of Gustav I Vasa
summary: Founder of modern Sweden: broke with Denmark and Rome, created a hereditary Lutheran monarchy.

name: Reign of Gustav III of Sweden
summary: Enlightened absolutist who restored royal power by coup and was assassinated at a masked ball.

name: Reign of Gustavus Adolphus
summary: Warrior king who reformed the army and intervened decisively in the Thirty Years' War; killed at Lutzen.

name: Swedish Age of Liberty
summary: Period of parliamentary dominance by the Riksdag over a weakened crown, ended by Gustav III's coup.

name: Swedish Accession to NATO
summary: Sweden abandoned two centuries of non-alignment and joined NATO in March 2024 after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

name: Swedish War of Liberation
summary: Rising led by Gustav Vasa after the Stockholm Bloodbath that ended Danish rule and the Kalmar Union.

name: Principality of Liechtenstein
summary: Alpine principality created in 1719, sovereign since 1806 and closely tied to Switzerland.

name: Maastricht Treaty
summary: Treaty creating the European Union, EU citizenship and the path to monetary union.

name: Roman Britain
summary: The Roman province of Britannia, from the Claudian invasion of AD 43 to the effective end of imperial administration around 410.

name: Building of the Antonine Wall
summary: Turf frontier across the Forth-Clyde isthmus, occupied for barely a generation.

name: Boudican revolt
summary: Iceni rising led by Boudica that destroyed Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium before defeat at Watling Street.

name: Division of Britannia into provinces
summary: Severus divided Britain into Britannia Superior and Inferior; Diocletian later subdivided it further into a diocese of four or five provinces.

name: End of Roman rule in Britain
summary: Withdrawal of the last field armies and the traditional Rescript of Honorius telling the cities to look to their own defence. Dating is received tradition.

name: Building of Hadrian's Wall
summary: Frontier wall from Tyne to Solway begun under Hadrian, later Rome's northern boundary in Britain.

name: Roman conquest of Britain
summary: Campaigns from Aulus Plautius' landing in AD 43 to Agricola's victory at Mons Graupius, bringing most of Britain under Rome.

name: Republic of Moldova
summary: Former Soviet republic independent since 1991, with the breakaway Transnistria region and EU candidate status.

name: Transnistria
summary: Unrecognised Russian-backed breakaway statelet on the left bank of the Dniester.

name: Principality of Monaco
summary: Grimaldi principality on the Riviera whose sovereignty was confirmed in 1861 under French protection.

name: Munich Agreement
summary: Britain, France, Germany and Italy ceded the Sudetenland to Hitler, the high point of appeasement.

name: Baltic Provinces of the Russian Empire
summary: Estonia, Livonia and Courland under Russian rule with Baltic German elites, until 1918 independence.

name: Denmark-Norway
summary: Oldenburg composite monarchy of Denmark, Norway, Iceland and the North Atlantic islands, split at Kiel in 1814.

name: Great Northern War
summary: Coalition war that destroyed Sweden's Baltic empire and established Russia as a great power.

name: Kalmar Union (late)
summary: Dynastic union of Denmark, Norway and Sweden that broke up when Sweden seceded under Gustav Vasa.

name: Singing Revolution
summary: Mass non-violent movement, including the 1989 Baltic Way human chain, that restored Baltic independence.

name: Soviet Annexation of the Baltic States
summary: Forced incorporation of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania into the USSR, followed by deportations.

name: Reign of Charles XII of Sweden
summary: Warrior king whose victories ended at Poltava in 1709; killed besieging Fredriksten.

name: Swedish and Polish Livonia
summary: Partition of the Livonian Order's lands among Sweden, Poland-Lithuania and Denmark after the Livonian War.

name: Treaty of Kiel
summary: Denmark ceded Norway to Sweden after backing Napoleon, keeping Iceland, Greenland and the Faroes.

name: Union of Sweden and Norway
summary: Personal union imposed after Denmark ceded Norway, dissolved peacefully in 1905.

name: October Revolution
summary: Bolshevik seizure of power in Petrograd under Lenin and Trotsky, creating the world's first communist state.

name: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe
summary: Security and human-rights organisation growing out of the Helsinki process.

name: Peace of Westphalia
summary: Treaties of Munster and Osnabruck that ended the Thirty Years' War and framed the modern system of sovereign states.

name: Portuguese Republic
summary: Democratic republic under the 1976 constitution, an EU member since 1986 and euro founder.

name: Carnation Revolution
summary: Bloodless captains' coup of 25 April 1974 that ended dictatorship and led to decolonisation.

name: Estado Novo (Portugal)
summary: Salazar's corporatist dictatorship, which clung to the African colonies until the Carnation Revolution.

name: House of Braganza
summary: Dynasty that ruled Portugal and later Brazil until the republican revolution of 1910.

name: Iberian Union
summary: Sixty years in which Habsburg kings of Spain also ruled Portugal and its empire.

name: Lisbon Earthquake
summary: Earthquake, tsunami and fire that destroyed Lisbon and prompted Pombal's rebuilding and Enlightenment debate.

name: Portuguese Republican Revolution
summary: Lisbon rising that deposed Manuel II and established the First Portuguese Republic.

name: Portuguese Colonial War
summary: Thirteen-year war against independence movements in Angola, Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau that broke the Estado Novo.

name: First Portuguese Republic
summary: Unstable republic with dozens of governments, ended by the 28 May military coup.

name: Portuguese Restoration War
summary: Revolt that installed the House of Braganza and won recognition of Portuguese independence from Spain.

name: Reign of Charles X of France
summary: Ultra-royalist king whose July Ordinances provoked the 1830 revolution; began the conquest of Algiers.

name: Reign of Louis XVIII
summary: Restored Bourbon king who accepted the Charter of 1814 and steered a moderate course between ultras and liberals.

name: Reign of Peter the Great
summary: Westernising tsar who built St Petersburg and a navy, beat Sweden at Poltava and proclaimed the Russian Empire.

name: Republic of Albania
summary: Post-communist democracy since 1992, a NATO member from 2009 and EU candidate.

name: Albanian Declaration of Independence
summary: Ismail Qemali proclaimed Albanian independence at Vlore during the First Balkan War.

name: Kingdom of Albania
summary: Zog I's kingdom, increasingly an Italian dependency until Italy invaded in 1939.

name: People's Socialist Republic of Albania
summary: Enver Hoxha's isolated Stalinist state, which broke with Yugoslavia, the USSR and finally China.

name: Republic of Belarus
summary: Independent since 1991 and ruled by Alexander Lukashenko since 1994 in close alignment with Russia.

name: Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic
summary: Soviet Belarus, which lost about a quarter of its population in the Second World War.

name: Republic of Bulgaria
summary: Democratic republic since 1990, in NATO from 2004 and the EU from 2007.

name: Kingdom of Bulgaria
summary: Independent tsardom that fought on the losing side in both world wars.

name: People's Republic of Bulgaria
summary: Communist state closely tied to the USSR under Todor Zhivkov for 35 years.

name: Principality of Bulgaria
summary: Autonomous Ottoman tributary created at Berlin, which absorbed Eastern Rumelia in 1885.

name: Republic of Croatia
summary: Independent since 1991, a NATO member from 2009, EU from 2013 and eurozone from 2023.

name: Croatian War of Independence
summary: War between Croatia and Serb forces, including the siege of Dubrovnik and Vukovar and Operation Storm.

name: Independent State of Croatia
summary: Ustase puppet state under Ante Pavelic responsible for the Jasenovac camps and genocide of Serbs, Jews and Roma.

name: Republic of Estonia
summary: Baltic republic that restored independence in 1991 and joined the EU and NATO in 2004; a digital-government pioneer.

name: Republic of Estonia (first period)
summary: Independent Estonia after the War of Independence against Soviet Russia and the Baltic Germans, annexed by the USSR in 1940.

name: Republic of Finland
summary: Nordic republic that preserved independence against the USSR, joined the EU in 1995 and NATO in 2023.

name: Continuation War
summary: Finland's co-belligerent war alongside Germany, ended by armistice and territorial loss.

name: Finlandization
summary: Cold War policy of neutrality and accommodation with the USSR while remaining a Western democracy.

name: Finnish Civil War
summary: Whites under Mannerheim defeated the Reds in a brief, bloody conflict after independence.

name: Finnish Declaration of Independence
summary: Finland declared independence from revolutionary Russia on 6 December 1917.

name: Finnish Accession to NATO
summary: Finland joined NATO in April 2023, ending decades of military non-alignment.

name: Grand Duchy of Finland
summary: Autonomous Russian grand duchy where Finnish national identity and institutions took shape.

name: Winter War
summary: Soviet invasion resisted fiercely by Finland, which ceded Karelia in the Moscow Peace.

name: Hungary
summary: Democratic republic since 1989, in NATO from 1999 and the EU from 2004; governed by Viktor Orban since 2010.

name: Horthy Regency
summary: Admiral Miklos Horthy ruled Hungary as regent of a kingdom without a king, allying with Nazi Germany.

name: Hungarian People's Republic
summary: Communist Hungary under Rakosi then Kadar's 'goulash communism' after the crushed 1956 revolution.

name: Hungarian Revolution of 1848
summary: Kossuth's national revolution and war of independence, defeated by Austrian and Russian armies.

name: Hungarian Revolution of 1956
summary: National uprising against Soviet domination, crushed by Red Army intervention with thousands killed.

name: Hungarian Soviet Republic
summary: Bela Kun's 133-day communist regime, overthrown after Romanian invasion.

name: Kingdom of Hungary under the Habsburgs
summary: Hungarian crown held by the Habsburgs, partly Ottoman-occupied until 1699 and repeatedly in revolt.

name: Ottoman Hungary
summary: Central Hungary under Ottoman rule after Mohacs, recovered by the Habsburgs at Karlowitz.

name: Rakoczi's War of Independence
summary: Large anti-Habsburg revolt led by Francis II Rakoczi, ended by the Peace of Szatmar.

name: Treaty of Trianon
summary: Peace treaty that reduced Hungary to a third of its prewar territory, a lasting national grievance.

name: Republic of Latvia
summary: Baltic republic independent again from 1991, in the EU and NATO since 2004 and the euro since 2014.

name: Republic of Latvia (first period)
summary: Independent Latvia between the wars, ended by Soviet annexation under the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact.

name: Republic of Lithuania
summary: First Soviet republic to declare independence, in March 1990; EU and NATO member since 2004.

name: Republic of Lithuania (first period)
summary: Interwar Lithuania, which lost Vilnius to Poland and was annexed by the USSR in 1940.

name: Republic of Malta
summary: Mediterranean island state independent from Britain in 1964, a republic from 1974 and EU member from 2004.

name: Hospitaller Malta
summary: Rule of the Knights of St John, who withstood the Great Siege of 1565 and built Valletta.

name: Montenegro
summary: Adriatic republic independent since a 2006 referendum, a NATO member since 2017.

name: Principality and Kingdom of Montenegro
summary: Independent mountain state under the Petrovic-Njegos dynasty, recognised in 1878 and merged into Yugoslavia.

name: Romania
summary: Democratic republic since 1989, in NATO from 2004 and the EU from 2007.

name: Kingdom of Romania
summary: Kingdom that doubled in size as Greater Romania in 1918 and fell to communism after 1944.

name: Wallachia and Moldavia
summary: Ottoman tributary principalities, later under Phanariot then Russian-protected regimes, united in 1859.

name: Romanian Revolution of 1989
summary: Violent uprising that overthrew and executed Nicolae Ceausescu in December 1989.

name: Socialist Republic of Romania
summary: Communist Romania, independent-minded under Ceausescu's increasingly repressive personality cult.

name: United Principalities of Romania
summary: Union under Alexandru Ioan Cuza and then Carol I, independent from the Ottomans in 1878.

name: Republic of Serbia
summary: Independent Serbia since Montenegro's separation; an EU candidate that does not recognise Kosovo.

name: First Serbian Uprising
summary: Revolt under Karadjordje against Ottoman rule that began modern Serbian statehood.

name: Kingdom of Serbia
summary: Independent kingdom that won the Balkan Wars, suffered occupation in 1915 and became the core of Yugoslavia.

name: Principality of Serbia
summary: Autonomous then independent Serbian principality under the Obrenovic and Karadjordjevic houses.

name: Republic of Slovenia
summary: First Yugoslav republic to secede successfully; joined the EU and NATO in 2004 and the euro in 2007.

name: Slovenian Ten-Day War
summary: Brief conflict after Slovenia's independence declaration, ending with Yugoslav withdrawal.

name: Revolutions of 1848
summary: Liberal and nationalist uprisings across France, the German states, Italy, Austria and Hungary, mostly defeated.

name: Revolutions of 1989
summary: Peaceful collapse of communist regimes across Eastern Europe, from Poland to Romania.

name: Russian Civil War
summary: Reds defeated Whites, nationalists and Allied interventions at a cost of millions of lives and famine.

name: Russian Conquest of Siberia
summary: Cossack and merchant expansion across northern Asia to the Pacific, driven by the fur trade.

name: Russian Provisional Government
summary: Liberal-socialist government under Lvov then Kerensky that kept Russia in the war and fell in October.

name: Schengen Agreement
summary: Agreement abolishing internal border checks, implemented in 1995 and now covering most of the EU.

name: Republic of Austria
summary: Neutral democratic republic, sovereign from 1955 and an EU member since 1995.

name: Allied Occupation of Austria
summary: Four-power occupation ended by the State Treaty, which restored sovereignty on condition of neutrality.

name: Austrian Empire
summary: Empire proclaimed by Francis II in response to Napoleon, dominant in the German Confederation until 1866.

name: Federal State of Austria
summary: Dollfuss and Schuschnigg's clerical-authoritarian state, ended by German annexation.

name: First Austrian Republic
summary: Rump Austrian republic of political violence between Social Democrats and Christian Socials.

name: Metternich Era
summary: Conservative order of censorship, congresses and repression of nationalism directed from Vienna.

name: Silesian Wars
summary: Three wars in which Prussia took and kept Silesia from Habsburg Austria.

name: Second Chechen War
summary: Renewed campaign that reasserted Moscow's control over Chechnya under Kadyrov.

name: Slovakia
summary: Independent Slovak republic since 1993, in NATO and the EU from 2004 and the euro from 2009.

name: Slovak State
summary: German client state under Jozef Tiso, which deported most Slovak Jews and faced the 1944 national uprising.

name: Swiss Confederation
summary: Federal state created by the 1848 constitution, neutral, directly democratic and home to many international bodies.

name: Helvetic Republic
summary: French-imposed centralised republic that replaced the cantonal confederacy.

name: Old Swiss Confederacy
summary: League of thirteen cantons whose independence from the Empire was recognised in 1648 and which pioneered armed neutrality.

name: Sonderbund War
summary: Brief civil war in which federal forces defeated a league of Catholic cantons, clearing the way for the 1848 constitution.

name: Restored Swiss Confederation
summary: Confederation of 22 cantons whose perpetual neutrality was guaranteed at the Congress of Vienna.

name: Swiss Reformation
summary: Zwingli in Zurich and later Calvin in Geneva made Switzerland a centre of Reformed Protestantism.

name: Swiss Women's Suffrage
summary: Federal referendum granting women the vote, among the last in Europe.

name: Hellenic Republic
summary: Democratic Greece since the fall of the junta, an EU member since 1981 and euro member since 2001.

name: Axis Occupation of Greece
summary: German, Italian and Bulgarian occupation with famine, the destruction of Greek Jewry and mass resistance.

name: First Hellenic Republic
summary: Provisional revolutionary government under Kapodistrias until the powers imposed a monarchy.

name: Greco-Turkish War
summary: Greek invasion of Anatolia defeated by Kemal's forces, ending with the burning of Smyrna.

name: Greek Civil War
summary: Communist insurgency defeated by the government with British and then American support under the Truman Doctrine.

name: Greek Government-Debt Crisis
summary: Sovereign-debt collapse and three bailout programmes with severe austerity inside the eurozone.

name: Greek Military Junta
summary: Colonels' dictatorship that abolished the monarchy and fell after the Cyprus crisis.

name: Greek-Turkish Population Exchange
summary: Compulsory exchange under the Lausanne Convention that uprooted about 1.6 million people.

name: Greek War of Independence
summary: Revolt against Ottoman rule, won with British, French and Russian help at Navarino and by Russian invasion.

name: Kingdom of Greece
summary: Monarchy created by the great powers, which expanded through the Balkan Wars and collapsed after the Asia Minor defeat.

name: Reign of George I of Greece
summary: Long-reigning Danish-born king who gained the Ionian Islands, Thessaly and Macedonia; assassinated in 1913.

name: Reign of Otto of Greece
summary: Bavarian prince installed as first king of Greece, deposed by a military revolt.

name: Metaxas Regime
summary: Authoritarian '4th of August' government that rejected Mussolini's 1940 ultimatum with 'Oxi'.

name: Second Hellenic Republic
summary: Interwar republic of coups and refugee resettlement, ended by the restoration of the monarchy.

name: Third Polish Republic
summary: Democratic Poland since 1989, in NATO from 1999 and the EU from 2004.

name: Kingdom of Poland (Congress Poland)
summary: Russian-ruled Polish kingdom whose autonomy was stripped after the 1830 and 1863 uprisings.

name: Duchy of Warsaw
summary: Napoleonic Polish state that revived hopes of independence and supplied troops for the Grande Armee.

name: First Partition of Poland
summary: Russia, Prussia and Austria seized about a third of Commonwealth territory.

name: General Government
summary: German occupation regime in central Poland, site of mass murder including the extermination camps.

name: Invasion of Poland
summary: German attack on 1 September and Soviet attack on 17 September partitioned Poland and began the Second World War.

name: January Uprising
summary: Largest Polish insurrection against Russia, followed by Russification and the abolition of serfdom.

name: Kosciuszko Uprising
summary: National insurrection led by Tadeusz Kosciuszko, defeated by Russia and Prussia.

name: November Uprising
summary: Polish revolt against Russian rule, crushed with the loss of the kingdom's army and constitution.

name: Polish Martial Law
summary: General Jaruzelski's crackdown that interned Solidarity leaders and suspended civil liberties.

name: Polish People's Republic
summary: Communist Poland, shaken by 1956, 1968, 1970 and 1980 protests and by martial law in 1981.

name: Polish Round Table Talks
summary: Negotiations that produced semi-free elections and the first non-communist government in the bloc.

name: Polish-Soviet War
summary: War ended by Poland's victory at the Vistula in 1920 and the Treaty of Riga.

name: Second Partition of Poland
summary: Russia and Prussia took further large territories after the war in defence of the 1791 constitution.

name: Second Polish Republic
summary: Poland restored in 1918, victorious over Soviet Russia in 1920, ruled after 1926 by Pilsudski's Sanacja, destroyed in 1939.

name: Solidarity
summary: Independent trade union born in Gdansk under Lech Walesa that led the peaceful end of communist rule.

name: Third Partition of Poland
summary: Final partition erased Poland-Lithuania from the map for 123 years.

name: Union of Lublin
summary: Treaty creating a single Commonwealth with one monarch, diet and currency.

name: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
summary: Jewish armed revolt against deportations to Treblinka, crushed with the ghetto's destruction.

name: Warsaw Uprising
summary: Home Army rising for 63 days, defeated while Soviet forces halted; Warsaw was razed in reprisal.

name: Time of Troubles
summary: Dynastic vacuum, famine, false Dmitrys and Polish-Swedish intervention, ended by the election of the Romanovs.

name: Treaty of Rome
summary: Founding treaty of the European Economic Community and Euratom, creating a common market.

name: War Communism
summary: Forced grain requisitioning and nationalisation during the civil war, ended by famine and the New Economic Policy.

name: Anglo-Irish Treaty
summary: Treaty of December 1921 creating the Irish Free State as a dominion, with Northern Ireland opting out.

name: Anglo-Saxon England
summary: The era of Germanic-speaking kingdoms in lowland Britain, from the traditional adventus Saxonum to the Norman Conquest. The start date is received tradition, not a fixed event.

name: The Danelaw
summary: The area of eastern and northern England under Danish law and settlement after the Treaty of Alfred and Guthrum, gradually reconquered by the West Saxon kings.

name: Kingdom of York (Jorvik)
summary: Norse kingdom centred on York, ruled by Viking kings until Eric Bloodaxe's expulsion and death in 954. Dates are received from chronicles.

name: The Heptarchy
summary: Conventional label for the seven principal Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of Wessex, Mercia, Northumbria, Kent, East Anglia, Essex and Sussex. The scheme is a later historiographical construct.

name: Kingdom of East Anglia
summary: Kingdom of the North and South Folk, home of the Sutton Hoo burial and the Wuffing dynasty, later part of the Danelaw. Dates are first-attestation approximations.

name: Kingdom of Essex
summary: Kingdom of the East Saxons, including London for a time, absorbed by Wessex in 825. Dates are received tradition.

name: Kingdom of Kent
summary: Earliest recorded Anglo-Saxon kingdom, traditionally founded by Hengist, first to be converted by Augustine's mission in 597. Foundation date is received tradition.

name: Gregorian mission of Augustine
summary: Augustine's arrival in Kent began the conversion of the Anglo-Saxons and the founding of the see of Canterbury. Date received from Bede.

name: Kingdom of Mercia
summary: Midland kingdom dominant in the eighth century under Aethelbald and Offa, absorbed into the English realm after 918. Foundation date is first-attestation rather than calendar.

name: Kingdom of Northumbria
summary: Northern kingdom formed by the union of Bernicia and Deira, a centre of Insular learning, later a Viking kingdom of York. Dates are received from chronicle tradition.

name: Kingdom of Bernicia
summary: Northern Anglian kingdom between the Tees and the Forth, later joined with Deira to form Northumbria. Dates are received tradition.

name: Kingdom of Deira
summary: Anglian kingdom in what became Yorkshire, absorbed into Northumbria in the seventh century. Dates are received tradition.

name: Synod of Whitby
summary: Northumbrian council that adopted Roman rather than Irish practice for Easter and the tonsure. Date received from Bede.

name: Kingdom of Sussex
summary: Kingdom of the South Saxons, traditionally founded by AElle, annexed by Wessex in the ninth century. Foundation date is received tradition.

name: Kingdom of Wessex
summary: Kingdom of the West Saxons, founded according to tradition by Cerdic and Cynric, which under Alfred and his heirs became the nucleus of England. Foundation date is received tradition.

name: AElfweard of Wessex
summary: Son of Edward the Elder who may have reigned in Wessex for a few weeks in 924; his kingship is disputed. Dates are received from chronicle tradition.

name: Alfred the Great
summary: King of the West Saxons who resisted the Viking Great Heathen Army, secured the Danelaw frontier and promoted learning and law. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

name: Edward the Elder
summary: Son of Alfred who conquered much of the southern Danelaw and extended West Saxon overlordship over Mercia. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

name: Treaty of Alfred and Guthrum
summary: Agreement partitioning England between English and Danish rule along the Watling Street line. Dating is uncertain and received.

name: Viking invasions of Britain
summary: Two and a half centuries of Scandinavian raiding, settlement and conquest, from Lindisfarne to Stamford Bridge. Start date received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

name: Austrian Netherlands
summary: Habsburg Austrian rule over the southern Low Countries, disrupted by the Brabant Revolution and French annexation.

name: Channel Islands (Bailiwicks of Jersey and Guernsey)
summary: Remnants of the Duchy of Normandy that stayed loyal to the English crown in 1204 and remain self-governing Crown Dependencies.

name: Commonwealth of England
summary: The republic established after the execution of Charles I, governing England, and after conquest Scotland and Ireland, until the Restoration.
aliases: Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland

name: Oliver Cromwell as Lord Protector
summary: Head of state of the Protectorate over England, Scotland and Ireland after dissolving the Rump Parliament; refused the crown in 1657.

name: Richard Cromwell as Lord Protector
summary: Succeeded his father but lacked army support and resigned in May 1659, opening the way to the Restoration.

name: The Protectorate
summary: Constitutional regime under the Instrument of Government in which Oliver and then Richard Cromwell governed as Lord Protector.

name: Dal Riata
summary: Gaelic kingdom of Argyll and northern Ireland whose dynasty gave rise to the kings of Alba. Dates are received tradition.

name: Bourbon Restoration
summary: Constitutional monarchy under Louis XVIII and Charles X, ended by the July Revolution.

name: Edict of Nantes
summary: Henry IV's grant of limited toleration and fortified towns to French Protestants, revoked in 1685.

name: First French Empire
summary: Napoleon I's empire, dominant over continental Europe until defeat in Russia, Leipzig and finally Waterloo.

name: Reign of Napoleon I
summary: Emperor of the French who remade Europe's map and law before abdicating in 1814; briefly restored in 1815.

name: Franco-Prussian War
summary: Prussian-led German victory that destroyed the Second Empire, annexed Alsace-Lorraine and completed German unification.

name: Free France
summary: De Gaulle's government-in-exile and its forces, which rallied the empire and the Resistance against Vichy and Germany.

name: French Colonial Empire
summary: Two successive empires spanning the Americas, Africa, Indochina and the Pacific, largely dissolved between 1954 and 1962.

name: French Consulate
summary: Napoleon Bonaparte ruled as First Consul, creating the Bank of France, the Concordat and the Civil Code.

name: French Fifth Republic
summary: De Gaulle's semi-presidential republic, France's current constitutional order since 1958.

name: May 1968 in France
summary: Student revolt and general strike of ten million workers that shook de Gaulle's government.

name: Presidency of Charles de Gaulle
summary: Founding president of the Fifth Republic: Algerian independence, nuclear force de frappe, NATO withdrawal, and resignation after 1968.

name: Presidency of Emmanuel Macron
summary: Centrist president elected 2017 and re-elected 2022, facing gilets jaunes protests, COVID-19 and pension reform.

name: Presidency of Francois Hollande
summary: Socialist president who legalised same-sex marriage and led France through the 2015 terror attacks and COP21.

name: Presidency of Francois Mitterrand
summary: First Socialist president of the Fifth Republic; nationalisations then austerity, abolition of the death penalty, Maastricht.

name: Presidency of Georges Pompidou
summary: Gaullist president who oversaw industrial modernisation and accepted British entry into the EEC; died in office.

name: Presidency of Valery Giscard d'Estaing
summary: Centrist president who liberalised social law, legalised abortion and helped create the European Monetary System.

name: Presidency of Jacques Chirac
summary: Gaullist president who ended conscription, adopted the euro and opposed the 2003 Iraq war.

name: Presidency of Nicolas Sarkozy
summary: Presidency marked by the 2008 financial crisis, NATO reintegration and the Libya intervention.

name: French First Republic
summary: Republic proclaimed after the fall of the monarchy, passing through Convention, Terror, Directory and Consulate before Napoleon's empire.

name: French Directory
summary: Five-man executive governing France between the Terror and Bonaparte's Brumaire coup.

name: Reign of Terror
summary: Robespierre and the Committee of Public Safety executed tens of thousands until Thermidor ended the Jacobin dictatorship.

name: French Fourth Republic
summary: Unstable parliamentary republic that rebuilt the economy and began European integration but foundered on Indochina and Algeria.

name: Provisional Government of the French Republic
summary: De Gaulle-led government that restored republican legality, nationalised key industries and gave women the vote.

name: French Second Republic
summary: Republic born of the February Revolution, introduced universal male suffrage, ended by Louis-Napoleon's coup.

name: French Third Republic
summary: Longest-lived French republic: secular laicite laws, colonial expansion, victory in 1914-18, defeat in 1940.

name: Dreyfus Affair
summary: Wrongful conviction of a Jewish officer for treason that split France over antisemitism, army and republic.

name: French Law on the Separation of Church and State
summary: 1905 law establishing laicite by ending state recognition and funding of religions.

name: French Wars of Religion
summary: Eight civil wars between Catholics and Huguenots that devastated France and ended with Henry IV's conversion and the Edict of Nantes.

name: The Fronde
summary: Series of aristocratic and parlementaire revolts during Louis XIV's minority that hardened his commitment to absolutism.

name: The Hundred Days
summary: Napoleon's return from Elba, restored rule of about a hundred days, and final defeat at Waterloo.

name: July Monarchy
summary: Bourgeois constitutional monarchy of Louis-Philippe, the 'citizen king', toppled in February 1848.

name: Reign of Louis-Philippe I
summary: Orleanist king of the French whose narrow franchise and refusal of reform ended in the February Revolution.

name: July Revolution
summary: Three days of Parisian fighting in July 1830 that replaced Charles X with Louis-Philippe.

name: Kingdom of France (Early Modern)
summary: Valois and Bourbon monarchy that centralised the French state, fought the Italian and Religious wars, and built Europe's leading absolutist power before the Revolution abolished it.

name: Reign of Charles IX of France
summary: Ruled under his mother Catherine de' Medici; his reign saw the St Bartholomew's Day massacre of Huguenots in 1572.

name: Reign of Francis I of France
summary: Renaissance king who fought Charles V in Italy, patronised Leonardo and Chambord, and made French the language of administration in 1539.

name: Reign of Francis II of France
summary: Teenage king married to Mary Stuart whose brief reign was dominated by the Guise faction.

name: Reign of Henry II of France
summary: Ended the Italian Wars at Cateau-Cambresis in 1559 and died in a tournament accident, leaving power to Catherine de' Medici.

name: Reign of Henry III of France
summary: Last Valois king, caught between the Catholic League and Henry of Navarre; assassinated in 1589.

name: Reign of Henry IV of France
summary: First Bourbon king; converted to Catholicism, issued the Edict of Nantes in 1598 and rebuilt the kingdom before his assassination.

name: Reign of Louis XIII
summary: Reign dominated by Cardinal Richelieu, who broke Huguenot autonomy and entered the Thirty Years' War against the Habsburgs.

name: Reign of Louis XIV
summary: Seventy-two-year reign of the Sun King: Versailles, absolutism, revocation of the Edict of Nantes and near-continuous European war.

name: Reign of Louis XV
summary: Long reign marked by regency, the War of the Austrian Succession, and the loss of New France and India in the Seven Years' War.

name: Reign of Louis XVI
summary: Fiscal crisis and the summoning of the Estates-General led to revolution; deposed in 1792 and guillotined in 1793.

name: Napoleonic Code
summary: Civil Code of 1804 that codified French private law and became a model across Europe and Latin America.

name: Paris Commune
summary: Radical revolutionary government of Paris from March to May 1871, crushed in the semaine sanglante.

name: Revocation of the Edict of Nantes
summary: Edict of Fontainebleau outlawed Protestantism and drove several hundred thousand Huguenots into exile.

name: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
summary: Foundational statement of natural rights adopted by the National Assembly in August 1789.

name: Storming of the Bastille
summary: Parisian crowds seized the royal fortress-prison on 14 July 1789, the symbolic start of the Revolution.

name: Second French Empire
summary: Napoleon III's authoritarian then liberal empire: Haussmann's Paris, Crimea, Italy, Mexico, and collapse at Sedan.

name: Reign of Napoleon III
summary: Emperor whose modernising rule ended in capture at Sedan and the fall of the empire.

name: St Bartholomew's Day Massacre
summary: Mass killing of Huguenots in Paris and the provinces beginning 24 August 1572, a turning point in the Wars of Religion.

name: Vichy France
summary: Authoritarian French State under Marshal Petain that collaborated with Nazi Germany after the 1940 armistice.

name: Gaelic Ireland
summary: The network of Irish kingdoms and lordships under Gaelic law, ending with the Nine Years War and the Flight of the Earls. Dates are approximate and received.

name: House of Stuart
summary: Dynasty of Scottish kings from Robert II which acquired England in 1603 and ended with Queen Anne; interrupted by the Interregnum and the Revolution.

name: Interregnum
summary: The republican years between the execution of Charles I and the Restoration, under Commonwealth and Protectorate.

name: Irish Free State
summary: Dominion established by the Anglo-Irish Treaty, covering twenty-six counties, replaced by the constitution of Ireland in 1937.

name: Irish Civil War
summary: Conflict between pro- and anti-Treaty forces over the settlement with Britain, won by the Free State government.

name: Lordship and Crown Dependency of the Isle of Man
summary: Norse-Gaelic kingdom ceded to Scotland in 1266, later an English lordship and today a Crown Dependency with its own ancient parliament.

name: Jacobite line of succession
summary: The exiled Stuart claimants James II, James Francis Edward, Charles Edward and Henry Benedict, whose cause ended with the cardinal duke's death.

name: Kingdom of Deheubarth
summary: South-western Welsh kingdom formed from Seisyllwg and Dyfed, prominent under Hywel Dda and Rhys ap Gruffydd. Dates are received tradition.

name: Kingdom of England
summary: The English kingdom from AEthelstan's unification of the Anglo-Saxon realms to its merger with Scotland in the Kingdom of Great Britain in 1707.

name: Act of Settlement
summary: Vested the succession in Sophia of Hanover and her Protestant heirs and secured judicial tenure.

name: Act of Supremacy
summary: Statute declaring Henry VIII Supreme Head on earth of the Church of England.

name: AEthelred the Unready (restored)
summary: Second reign of AEthelred after Sweyn's death, ending with his own death in London amid Cnut's invasion. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

name: AEthelred the Unready
summary: Long reign dominated by renewed Viking invasions, Danegeld payments and the St Brice's Day massacre; driven out by Sweyn Forkbeard in 1013. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

name: AEthelstan
summary: First king to rule all England, victor at Brunanburh in 937 and a major legislator. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

name: Anglo-Spanish War
summary: Undeclared war with Philip II including the Armada of 1588 and Drake's raids, settled by the Treaty of London.

name: Founding of the Bank of England
summary: Chartered to fund the war with France, creating the basis of the national debt and modern public finance.

name: Bill of Rights
summary: Statute limiting royal power, requiring frequent parliaments and free elections and barring Catholics from the throne.

name: Black Death in England
summary: Plague that killed perhaps a third to a half of the population, transforming labour, wages and land tenure.

name: First Book of Common Prayer
summary: Cranmer's English liturgy, introduced by the Act of Uniformity and provoking the Western Rising.

name: Caroline Era
summary: Reign of Charles I before the Civil War, with Laudian church reform and personal rule.

name: Charles I
summary: Rule by personal prerogative and religious policy provoked the Civil Wars; tried and executed in Whitehall in January 1649.

name: Charles II
summary: Restored Stuart king whose reign covered the Great Plague, the Fire of London, the Popish Plot and the Exclusion Crisis.

name: Simon de Montfort's Parliament
summary: First English parliament to include elected burgesses from the towns as well as knights of the shire.

name: Dissolution of the Monasteries
summary: Suppression of religious houses and transfer of their vast wealth to the Crown and its supporters.

name: Domesday Book
summary: William I's great survey of landholding and resources in England, the most detailed record of its kind in medieval Europe.

name: Eadred
summary: King who finally ended the Norse kingdom of York with the death of Eric Bloodaxe in 954. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

name: Eadwig
summary: Teenage king whose reign saw conflict with Dunstan and the loss of Mercia and Northumbria to his brother Edgar. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

name: Edgar the AEtheling
summary: Last male of the house of Wessex, proclaimed king in London after Hastings but never crowned; submitted to William at Berkhamsted.

name: Edgar the Peaceful
summary: King associated with the Benedictine reform, monetary reform and a famous imperial coronation at Bath in 973. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

name: Edmund I
summary: Half-brother of AEthelstan who recovered the Five Boroughs from Norse rule; murdered at Pucklechurch. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

name: Edmund Ironside
summary: Warrior son of AEthelred who fought Cnut to a partition of England at Olney and died months later. Dates are received from chronicle tradition.

name: Edward I
summary: Conqueror of Wales, campaigner in Scotland and summoner of the Model Parliament of 1295.

name: Edward II
summary: Defeated at Bannockburn and dominated by favourites; deposed in 1327 and died at Berkeley Castle.

name: Edward III
summary: Claimed the French throne and opened the Hundred Years War, won Crecy and Poitiers, and ruled through the Black Death.

name: Edward IV (first reign)
summary: Yorkist king who seized the throne after Towton and was driven out in 1470 by Warwick and the Lancastrians.

name: Edward IV (second reign)
summary: Restored Yorkist rule, stabilised royal finances and reigned in comparative peace until his sudden death in 1483.

name: Edward the Confessor
summary: Restored king of the house of Wessex, builder of Westminster Abbey, whose childless death triggered the succession crisis of 1066. Dates received from chronicles.

name: Edward the Martyr
summary: Young king murdered at Corfe in 978 and swiftly venerated as a saint. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

name: Edward V
summary: Boy king deposed after eleven weeks by his uncle Richard of Gloucester; one of the Princes in the Tower, never crowned.

name: Edward VI
summary: Boy king under Somerset and Northumberland whose reign pushed England towards full Protestantism and the Books of Common Prayer.

name: Edwardian conquest of Wales
summary: Edward I's campaigns ending Welsh independence with the death of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd and a great programme of castle building.

name: Elizabethan Era
summary: Golden age of English drama and seafaring under Elizabeth I, with Shakespeare, Marlowe, Drake and the Armada.

name: Elizabethan Religious Settlement
summary: Acts of Supremacy and Uniformity establishing a Protestant church with the monarch as Supreme Governor.

name: Empress Matilda
summary: Daughter of Henry I who controlled England briefly in 1141 as Lady of the English but was never crowned queen.

name: English Reformation
summary: Break with Rome under Henry VIII, doctrinal change under Edward VI, Marian reversal and the Elizabethan settlement.

name: Exclusion Crisis
summary: Attempts to bar the Catholic James from the succession, giving rise to the Whig and Tory parties.

name: First Barons' War
summary: Rebellion against King John after Magna Carta, involving a French invasion, ended by the reissue of the charter under Henry III.

name: First English Civil War
summary: War between King and Parliament from Edgehill to Naseby and the surrender of Oxford.

name: Glorious Revolution
summary: Deposition of James II and accession of William and Mary on parliamentary terms, establishing constitutional monarchy.

name: Great Fire of London
summary: Fire that destroyed much of the medieval City, prompting rebuilding in brick and Wren's churches.

name: Great Plague of London
summary: Last major English bubonic plague epidemic, killing perhaps a quarter of London's population.

name: Gunpowder Plot
summary: Catholic conspiracy to blow up the Palace of Westminster, foiled on 5 November 1605.

name: Habeas Corpus Act
summary: Statute strengthening the writ against unlawful detention, a landmark of personal liberty.

name: Harold Godwinson
summary: Last crowned Anglo-Saxon king of England; won at Stamford Bridge and was killed at Hastings on 14 October 1066.

name: Harold Harefoot
summary: Son of Cnut who ruled England, first as regent then as king, against the claims of his half-brother Harthacnut. Dates received from chronicles.

name: Harthacnut
summary: Son of Cnut and Emma who united the English and Danish crowns briefly and died suddenly at Lambeth. Dates received from chronicles.

name: Henry I
summary: Youngest son of the Conqueror who took England and Normandy, issued the Charter of Liberties and left a disputed succession after his son's death.

name: Henry II
summary: First Plantagenet king, ruler of a vast Angevin domain, reformer of English common law and antagonist of Thomas Becket.

name: Henry III
summary: Boy king whose long reign saw baronial reform, the Provisions of Oxford, the Second Barons' War and the rebuilding of Westminster Abbey.

name: Henry IV
summary: First Lancastrian king, who usurped Richard II and spent his reign suppressing rebellion including Glyndwr's rising and the Percys.

name: Henry V
summary: Victor of Agincourt in 1415 whose Treaty of Troyes made him heir to France; died of dysentery in 1422.

name: Henry VI
summary: Inherited England and the French claim as an infant; his incapacity and factionalism led to the loss of France and the Wars of the Roses.

name: Henry VI (restoration)
summary: Brief Lancastrian restoration engineered by the Earl of Warwick, ending with Barnet, Tewkesbury and Henry's death in the Tower.

name: Henry VII
summary: First Tudor king, who won at Bosworth, married Elizabeth of York and restored royal finances and authority.

name: High Medieval England
summary: Era of Norman and Angevin consolidation, castle and cathedral building, common law, and population and town growth.

name: House of Blois
summary: The single-reign dynasty of King Stephen, whose disputed rule produced the Anarchy.

name: House of Denmark (Knytlinga) in England
summary: The Danish kings Sweyn, Cnut, Harold Harefoot and Harthacnut who ruled England as part of a North Sea empire. Dates received from chronicles.

name: House of Lancaster
summary: The cadet Plantagenet line of Henry IV, Henry V and Henry VI, symbolised by the red rose.

name: House of Normandy
summary: The Norman dynasty of William I, William II, Henry I and Stephen of Blois that transformed English land tenure, law and architecture.

name: House of Orange-Nassau in Britain
summary: The reign of William III, the only Dutch monarch of the British kingdoms, ruling first jointly with Mary II.

name: House of Plantagenet
summary: The Angevin and Plantagenet kings from Henry II to Richard III, under whom Parliament, common law and the Hundred Years War took shape.

name: House of Tudor
summary: The Welsh-descended dynasty of Henry VII to Elizabeth I, spanning the English Reformation and the growth of the Tudor state.

name: House of Wessex
summary: The Cerdicing dynasty of West Saxon kings who became kings of the English, ending with Edward the Confessor and Edgar the AEtheling. Foundation date is received tradition.

name: House of York
summary: The rival Plantagenet line of Edward IV, Edward V and Richard III, symbolised by the white rose.

name: Hundred Years' War
summary: Dynastic struggle between England and France over the French crown and Gascony, including Crecy, Poitiers, Agincourt and eventual English expulsion.

name: Jacobean Era
summary: Reign of James I, marked by the King James Bible, Jacobean drama and early colonisation of Virginia.

name: James I of England and VI of Scotland
summary: First Stuart king of England, uniting the English and Scottish crowns in his person and sponsoring the Authorised Version of the Bible.

name: James II of England and VII of Scotland
summary: Catholic king deposed by the Glorious Revolution after alienating the political nation; fled to France in December 1688.

name: Lady Jane Grey
summary: Proclaimed queen for nine to thirteen days in July 1553 under Northumberland's scheme; deposed by Mary I and later executed.

name: John
summary: Lost Normandy to Philip II, quarrelled with the papacy and was forced to seal Magna Carta in 1215.

name: Late Medieval England
summary: Period of famine, plague, French war, peasant revolt and dynastic conflict.

name: Laws in Wales Acts
summary: Tudor statutes annexing Wales to the realm of England, creating Welsh counties and parliamentary representation and making English the language of the courts.

name: Long Parliament
summary: Parliament summoned in 1640 that abolished the prerogative courts, tried Strafford and led the war against the king.

name: Magna Carta
summary: Charter sealed by King John at Runnymede limiting royal arbitrariness and guaranteeing due process; reissued and enshrined in later law.

name: Mary I
summary: Restored Roman Catholicism, married Philip II of Spain and presided over the Marian persecutions.

name: Mary II
summary: Joint sovereign with her husband William III after the Glorious Revolution; died of smallpox in 1694.

name: Model Parliament
summary: Edward I's assembly of lords, clergy, knights and burgesses, later seen as the pattern for Parliament.

name: Norman Conquest
summary: William of Normandy's invasion, victory at Hastings and subsequent subjugation of England, including the Harrying of the North.

name: Peasants' Revolt
summary: Rising against the poll tax and serfdom led by Wat Tyler and John Ball, suppressed after the confrontation at Smithfield.

name: Personal Rule of Charles I
summary: Eleven years of government without Parliament, financed by ship money and marked by Laudian church policy.

name: Petition of Right
summary: Parliamentary statement against non-parliamentary taxation, arbitrary imprisonment and billeting.

name: Philip of Spain as King of England
summary: Jure uxoris king alongside Mary I under the terms of their marriage treaty; his title lapsed on her death.

name: Pilgrimage of Grace
summary: Northern rising against religious change and Cromwell's government, the greatest Tudor rebellion.

name: Provisions of Oxford
summary: Baronial reform programme imposed on Henry III establishing a council of fifteen and regular parliaments.

name: Provisions of Westminster
summary: Further baronial reforms addressing local administration and legal grievances.

name: Trial and execution of Charles I
summary: The king was tried by a High Court of Justice and beheaded outside the Banqueting House on 30 January 1649.

name: Restoration of the Monarchy
summary: Charles II returned under the Declaration of Breda, restoring monarchy, Lords and the Church of England.

name: Restoration Era
summary: Period of restored monarchy, Restoration comedy, the Royal Society, plague and fire.

name: Richard I the Lionheart
summary: Crusader king who spent almost his entire reign abroad on the Third Crusade and in continental war, dying at Chalus.

name: Richard II
summary: Faced the Peasants' Revolt as a boy and later ruled autocratically; deposed by Henry Bolingbroke in 1399.

name: Richard III
summary: Last Yorkist and last Plantagenet king, killed at Bosworth in 1485; his remains were found in Leicester in 2012.

name: Second Barons' War
summary: Rising led by Simon de Montfort against Henry III, producing the parliament of 1265 before defeat at Evesham.

name: Second English Civil War
summary: Royalist and Scottish risings crushed at Preston, leading directly to the king's trial.

name: Somerset v Stewart
summary: Mansfield's judgment that slavery had no positive law in England, freeing James Somerset.

name: Statute of Labourers
summary: Post-plague attempt to cap wages and bind labourers, a grievance behind the Peasants' Revolt.

name: Stephen
summary: Nephew of Henry I whose contested accession produced the civil war known as the Anarchy; agreed to be succeeded by Henry of Anjou.

name: Sweyn Forkbeard
summary: Danish king who conquered England in 1013 and reigned for a few weeks before dying at Gainsborough. Dates are received from chronicle tradition.

name: The Anarchy
summary: Civil war between Stephen and Empress Matilda over the succession to Henry I, ended by the Treaty of Wallingford.

name: Third English Civil War
summary: Campaigns in Ireland and Scotland ending with Cromwell's victory at Worcester and Charles II's flight.

name: Unification of England under AEthelstan
summary: AEthelstan's takeover of Northumbria created a single kingdom of the English. Date received from chronicle tradition.

name: Wars of the Roses
summary: Dynastic wars between Lancaster and York from St Albans to Stoke Field, ending with Tudor rule.

name: William II Rufus
summary: Second Norman king, quarrelsome with the Church and killed by an arrow in the New Forest.

name: William III
summary: Dutch stadtholder invited to rule jointly with Mary II; accepted the Bill of Rights and led the Grand Alliance against Louis XIV.

name: William I the Conqueror
summary: Duke of Normandy who conquered England in 1066, imposed Norman lordship, built castles and commissioned Domesday Book.

name: Kingdom of Great Britain
summary: State created by the Acts of Union of 1707 uniting England and Scotland under one parliament at Westminster, until the union with Ireland in 1801.

name: Acts of Union 1707
summary: Parallel Acts of the English and Scottish parliaments creating one Kingdom of Great Britain with a single parliament.

name: British Agricultural Revolution
summary: Enclosure, crop rotation, selective breeding and improved yields that fed a rapidly growing urban population.

name: Anne, Queen of Great Britain
summary: First sovereign of the united Kingdom of Great Britain, whose reign saw the War of the Spanish Succession and Marlborough's victories.

name: Augustan Age
summary: Literary and political era of Pope, Swift and Addison, and of Whig oligarchy under Walpole.

name: William Cavendish, Duke of Devonshire
summary: Caretaker premier of the Pitt-Devonshire ministry during the crisis after the loss of Minorca.

name: Augustus FitzRoy, Duke of Grafton
summary: Led a divided ministry through the Wilkes affair and rising American discontent.

name: Thomas Pelham-Holles, Duke of Newcastle (first ministry)
summary: Succeeded his brother Henry Pelham but proved unable to manage the opening disasters of the Seven Years War.

name: Duke of Newcastle (second ministry)
summary: Partnership with Pitt the Elder that produced the victories of the annus mirabilis of 1759.

name: William Cavendish-Bentinck, Duke of Portland (first ministry)
summary: Figurehead of the Fox-North coalition, dismissed by George III over the India Bill.

name: John Stuart, Earl of Bute
summary: Favourite of George III who concluded the Peace of Paris and resigned amid intense unpopularity.

name: William Pitt the Elder, Earl of Chatham
summary: Architect of victory in the Seven Years War who as premier was incapacitated by illness.

name: William Petty, Earl of Shelburne
summary: Concluded the Peace of Paris recognising American independence.

name: Spencer Compton, Earl of Wilmington
summary: Nominal head of the ministry that succeeded Walpole, with real power held by Carteret and the Pelhams.

name: French Revolutionary Wars
summary: British participation in the coalitions against revolutionary France, including naval victories at the Nile and Camperdown.

name: George Grenville
summary: Premier responsible for the Stamp Act and the prosecution of John Wilkes.

name: George I
summary: Elector of Hanover who succeeded under the Act of Settlement; his reign saw the 1715 Jacobite rising and the South Sea Bubble.

name: George II
summary: Last British monarch to lead troops in battle, at Dettingen in 1743; his reign covered the 1745 rising and the Seven Years War's opening.

name: George III
summary: Reigned through the loss of the American colonies, the union with Ireland and the wars with France, and suffered recurrent mental illness.

name: Georgian Era
summary: Age of the four Georges and William IV, spanning agricultural improvement, empire, industrialisation and classical architecture.

name: Gordon Riots
summary: Anti-Catholic riots that overwhelmed London for a week, the worst civil disorder of the century.

name: Henry Pelham
summary: Whig premier who ended the War of the Austrian Succession, reduced the debt and presided over the Broad Bottom ministry.

name: Jacobite rising of 1715
summary: The Fifteen, led by the Earl of Mar for the Old Pretender, halted at Sheriffmuir and Preston.

name: Jacobite rising of 1719
summary: Spanish-backed attempt defeated at Glen Shiel.

name: Jacobite rising of 1745
summary: The Forty-Five, in which Charles Edward Stuart advanced to Derby before annihilation at Culloden.

name: Frederick North, Lord North
summary: Premier throughout the American War of Independence, resigning after Yorktown.

name: Charles Watson-Wentworth, Marquess of Rockingham (first ministry)
summary: Whig ministry that repealed the Stamp Act while passing the Declaratory Act.

name: Marquess of Rockingham (second ministry)
summary: Short second ministry that opened peace negotiations with America and passed Irish legislative independence; ended with his death.

name: Robert Walpole
summary: Regarded as the first prime minister, Whig dominator of politics for two decades who kept Britain out of war until Jenkins' Ear.

name: Septennial Act
summary: Extended the maximum life of a parliament from three years to seven.

name: Seven Years' War
summary: Global war in which Britain took Canada, expelled France from India and emerged as the leading colonial power.

name: South Sea Bubble
summary: Speculative collapse in South Sea Company shares that discredited ministers and elevated Walpole.

name: War of the Austrian Succession
summary: British participation against France and Prussia, including George II's victory at Dettingen.

name: War of the Spanish Succession
summary: European war in which Marlborough won Blenheim and Ramillies, ending with the Treaty of Utrecht and the acquisition of Gibraltar.

name: William Pitt the Younger (first ministry)
summary: Youngest prime minister at 24, reformer of finance and administration who led Britain into the French revolutionary wars; resigned over Catholic emancipation.

name: Kingdom of Gwynedd
summary: The dominant kingdom of north Wales, whose rulers claimed the principality of Wales until Edward I's conquest. Foundation date is received tradition.

name: Kingdom of Ireland
summary: Created by the Crown of Ireland Act of 1542, a client kingdom under the English and then British crown until the Union of 1801.

name: Cromwellian conquest of Ireland
summary: Parliamentarian reconquest marked by the sieges of Drogheda and Wexford and massive land confiscation.

name: Easter Rising
summary: Republican insurrection in Dublin, suppressed within a week, whose executions transformed Irish public opinion.

name: Great Famine in Ireland
summary: Potato blight and government policy produced about a million deaths and a million emigrants, halving Ireland's population over decades.

name: Irish Rebellion of 1798
summary: United Irishmen rising inspired by revolutionary France, suppressed with great bloodshed and leading to the Union of 1801.

name: Irish War of Independence
summary: Guerrilla war between the IRA and Crown forces including the Black and Tans, ended by truce and the Anglo-Irish Treaty.

name: Nine Years' War in Ireland
summary: Rebellion of Hugh O'Neill against Tudor rule, ending at Kinsale and Mellifont and opening the way to the Ulster plantation.

name: Plantation of Ulster
summary: Organised settlement of English and Scottish Protestants on confiscated Ulster land, with enduring consequences.

name: Williamite War in Ireland
summary: War between Jacobite and Williamite forces including the Siege of Derry, the Boyne and Aughrim, ending with the Treaty of Limerick.

name: Kingdom of Powys
summary: Kingdom of eastern mid-Wales, later divided into Powys Fadog and Powys Wenwynwyn. Dates are received tradition.

name: Kingdom of Scotland
summary: The Scottish kingdom, from the traditional union of Picts and Gaels under Kenneth MacAlpin to the Union of 1707. The foundation date is received tradition.

name: Aed
summary: Brief-reigning king of Alba, killed after about a year. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Alexander I
summary: King who ruled southern Scotland while his brother David held the south-west; patron of the reformed Church.

name: Alexander II
summary: Settled the border by the Treaty of York in 1237 and extended royal power into the west.

name: Alexander III
summary: Won the Hebrides by the Treaty of Perth in 1266; his death without an heir precipitated the succession crisis.

name: Amlaib
summary: Brother of Cuilen recorded as briefly ruling Alba in opposition to Kenneth II. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Anne, Queen of Scots
summary: Last monarch of an independent Kingdom of Scotland before the Union of 1707.

name: Bishops' Wars
summary: Scottish Covenanter resistance to Charles I's prayer book, whose cost forced him to recall Parliament.

name: Charles I of Scotland
summary: King of Scots whose prayer book policy provoked the Covenanting revolt and the Bishops' Wars.

name: Charles II of Scotland
summary: Proclaimed King of Scots in 1649 and crowned at Scone in 1651, though exiled until the Restoration of 1660.

name: Claim of Right
summary: Scottish counterpart to the Bill of Rights, declaring the throne forfeited by James VII.

name: Constantine I
summary: King of Alba during heavy Viking pressure; killed fighting Norse raiders. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Constantine II
summary: Long-reigning king who fought AEthelstan and lost at Brunanburh, later retiring to St Andrews. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Constantine III
summary: Short-reigning king of Alba killed in the continuing dynastic feud. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Cuilen
summary: King of Alba killed by the men of Strathclyde. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: David I
summary: Reforming king who introduced feudal tenure, burghs, sheriffs and a silver coinage, and invaded England during the Anarchy.

name: David II
summary: Son of Bruce whose reign included defeat and long captivity in England after Neville's Cross.

name: Declaration of Arbroath
summary: Letter of the Scottish barons to the pope asserting Scotland's independence and the community of the realm.

name: Donald I
summary: Brother of Kenneth I, remembered for promulgating the 'laws of Aed' in Alba. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Donald II
summary: First king styled ri Alban, king of Alba, in the annals. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Donald III Bane
summary: Brother of Malcolm III who twice seized the throne in reaction against Anglo-Norman influence; deposed and blinded.

name: Dub
summary: King of Alba killed in the dynastic feuding between the rival Alpinid branches. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Duncan I
summary: Grandson of Malcolm II whose failed campaigns ended with his killing by Macbeth. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Duncan II
summary: Son of Malcolm III installed with English help and killed within months.

name: Edgar
summary: Son of Malcolm III and Margaret, who ruled peacefully under English patronage.

name: Edward Balliol
summary: English-backed claimant crowned in 1332 who held parts of Scotland intermittently before abandoning his claim.

name: Eochaid
summary: Grandson of Kenneth I recorded as ruling Alba, perhaps jointly with Giric. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: First War of Scottish Independence
summary: War from Edward I's invasion through Wallace, Bruce and Bannockburn to the Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton.

name: Giric
summary: King of Alba whose relationship to the Alpinid line is obscure; may have ruled jointly with Eochaid. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Highland Clearances
summary: Displacement of Highland tenantry for sheep and sporting estates, driving mass emigration. Dating is conventional.

name: House of Alpin
summary: The Alpinid kings of Alba descended from Kenneth MacAlpin, ruling by alternating succession between two branches. Dates received from king-lists.

name: House of Balliol
summary: The rival royal line of John and Edward Balliol, sustained by English support against the Bruces.

name: House of Bruce
summary: The dynasty of Robert I and David II which secured Scottish independence.

name: House of Dunkeld
summary: The Scottish royal line descended from Malcolm III and Duncan I that presided over the feudalisation of Scotland.

name: Indulf
summary: King of Alba during whose reign Edinburgh was said to have been taken from the Northumbrians. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Jacobite rising of 1689
summary: Highland rising for James VII including the victory at Killiecrankie and the massacre of Glencoe in 1692.

name: James I of Scotland
summary: Held prisoner in England until 1424, then ruled forcefully at home; assassinated at Perth in 1437.

name: James II of Scotland
summary: Broke the power of the Black Douglases and was killed by an exploding cannon at Roxburgh.

name: James III of Scotland
summary: Unpopular king who pursued peace with England and was killed at Sauchieburn.

name: James IV of Scotland
summary: Renaissance king who married Margaret Tudor and died with much of his nobility at Flodden.

name: James V of Scotland
summary: King who allied with France, taxed the Church heavily and died shortly after the defeat at Solway Moss.

name: James VI of Scotland
summary: King of Scots from infancy who inherited England in 1603 and thereafter ruled both kingdoms from London.

name: James VII of Scotland
summary: Scottish reign of James II of England, ended when the Convention of Estates declared the throne forfeited.

name: John Balliol
summary: Chosen king by Edward I's arbitration in the Great Cause and deposed after refusing English demands.

name: Kenneth I MacAlpin
summary: Traditionally the first king of a united Picto-Gaelic kingdom of Alba, though the union was a longer process than the king-lists suggest. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Kenneth II
summary: King of Alba who raided Northumbria and was killed in a dynastic conspiracy. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Kenneth III
summary: King of Alba killed at Monzievaird by his successor Malcolm II. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Lordship of the Isles
summary: MacDonald lordship dominating the Hebrides and west coast, forfeited to James IV in 1493.

name: Lulach
summary: Stepson of Macbeth, briefly king and killed in 1058. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Macbeth
summary: King of Alba for seventeen years, remembered as a capable ruler who went on pilgrimage to Rome; killed at Lumphanan. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Malcolm I
summary: King of Alba who received Strathclyde or Cumbria from the English and raided Northumbria. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Malcolm II
summary: King who won at Carham in 1018, securing Lothian, and extended Scottish authority southwards. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

name: Malcolm III Canmore
summary: King who killed Macbeth's heir, married the Saxon princess Margaret and raided England repeatedly until his death at Alnwick.

name: Malcolm IV
summary: Boy king known as the Maiden who ceded the northern English counties to Henry II.

name: Margaret, Maid of Norway
summary: Infant granddaughter of Alexander III recognised as heir; her death at sea in 1290 opened the Great Cause.

name: Mary, Queen of Scots
