summary: Queen from six days old, briefly Queen of France, forced to abdicate in 1567 and later executed in England.

name: Robert I the Bruce
summary: Won Scottish independence at Bannockburn in 1314 and secured recognition by the Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton.

name: Robert II
summary: First Stewart king, nephew of David II, whose reign saw renewed border war with England.

name: Robert III
summary: Physically infirm king whose government was largely run by his brother the Duke of Albany.

name: Scottish Enlightenment
summary: Flowering of philosophy, economics and science in Edinburgh and Glasgow, with Hume, Smith, Black and Hutton.

name: Scottish Reformation
summary: Parliament abolished papal jurisdiction and adopted a reformed confession, founding the Kirk under Knox's influence.

name: Second War of Scottish Independence
summary: Renewed conflict over the Balliol claim, including Neville's Cross and the captivity of David II.

name: William I the Lion
summary: Long-reigning king captured at Alnwick in 1174, whose Treaty of Falaise made Scotland briefly a fief of England.

name: William II and Mary II of Scotland
summary: Joint Scottish monarchs after the Revolution settlement, which also re-established Presbyterian church government.

name: Kingdom of Strathclyde
summary: Brittonic kingdom centred on Dumbarton and later Govan, absorbed into Scotland in the eleventh century. Dates are received and approximate.

name: Lordship of Ireland
summary: The papal-sanctioned lordship held by the kings of England after the Angevin invasion, effective authority often confined to the Pale.

name: Batavian Republic
summary: French-sponsored revolutionary republic that replaced the Dutch Republic.

name: Dutch Constitutional Reform of 1848
summary: Thorbecke's revision created ministerial responsibility and parliamentary government.

name: Dutch Hunger Winter
summary: Famine in German-occupied western Netherlands that killed some 20,000 people.

name: Dutch Golden Age
summary: Era of Dutch commercial primacy, Rembrandt and Vermeer, Spinoza, and global trading empire.

name: Dutch Republic
summary: Republic of the Seven United Provinces: a commercial, naval and financial superpower of the 17th century.

name: Disaster Year of 1672
summary: French, English and German attack that nearly destroyed the Republic and brought William III to power.

name: Dutch Revolt
summary: Eighty Years' War in which the northern Netherlands won independence from Habsburg Spain.

name: Kingdom of Holland
summary: Napoleonic kingdom under Louis Bonaparte, annexed to France in 1810.

name: Kingdom of the Netherlands
summary: Constitutional monarchy under the House of Orange-Nassau, a founding member of NATO and the European communities.

name: Reign of Queen Beatrix
summary: Queen for 33 years, abdicating in favour of her son in 2013.

name: Reign of Queen Juliana
summary: Queen during Indonesian independence, the 1953 North Sea flood and postwar reconstruction.

name: Reign of Queen Wilhelmina
summary: Queen through both world wars who led resistance broadcasts from London exile.

name: Reign of King Willem-Alexander
summary: Dutch king since 2013.

name: Reign of William I of the Netherlands
summary: First Dutch king; lost Belgium in 1830-39 and abdicated in 1840.

name: Union of Utrecht
summary: Alliance of northern provinces that became the constitutional basis of the Dutch Republic.

name: Peninsular War
summary: Spanish, Portuguese and British resistance to Napoleon's occupation of Iberia, a decisive drain on the French empire.

name: Pictland
summary: The kingdoms of the Picts north of the Forth, absorbed into the Gaelic-speaking kingdom of Alba during the ninth century. Dates are approximate and received.

name: Principality of Wales
summary: The Welsh principality of Gwynedd's rulers recognised as Princes of Wales, conquered by Edward I in 1283 and annexed to England by the Laws in Wales Acts.

name: Glyndwr Rising
summary: Owain Glyndwr's national revolt against English rule, briefly establishing a Welsh parliament at Machynlleth.

name: Republic of Ireland
summary: The sovereign Irish state under the 1937 constitution, formally declared a republic and outside the Commonwealth in 1949.

name: Spanish Netherlands
summary: Habsburg Spanish provinces of the southern Low Countries, roughly modern Belgium and Luxembourg.

name: Sub-Roman Britain
summary: The period between the end of Roman rule and the Augustinian mission, marked by British kingdoms, Saxon settlement and very thin sources. Dating is conventional rather than exact.

name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
summary: State created by the Acts of Union of 1800 and lasting until the secession of the Irish Free State in 1922.
aliases: UK of Great Britain and Ireland

name: Union of the Crowns
summary: James VI of Scotland's accession to the English throne joined the two crowns in one person while the kingdoms stayed separate.

name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
summary: The present United Kingdom, comprising England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, dating in its current form from the Irish Free State's separation in 1922.

name: United Kingdom of the Netherlands
summary: Congress of Vienna state joining the Dutch and Belgian provinces under William I, split by Belgian independence.

name: 1975 European Communities referendum
summary: First UK-wide referendum, in which two thirds voted to stay in the European Communities.

name: Abdication Crisis
summary: Constitutional crisis over Edward VIII's wish to marry Wallis Simpson, ending in his abdication in December 1936.

name: Abolition of the Slave Trade Act
summary: Outlawed British participation in the transatlantic slave trade after two decades of abolitionist campaigning.

name: Acts of Union 1800
summary: Legislation merging the Kingdoms of Great Britain and Ireland into the United Kingdom from 1 January 1801.

name: British involvement in the War in Afghanistan
summary: Combat operations, chiefly in Helmand, from the invasion of 2001 to the end of the combat mission in 2014.

name: Alec Douglas-Home
summary: Renounced his peerage to lead the Conservatives and narrowly lost the 1964 election.

name: Andrew Bonar Law
summary: Canadian-born Conservative premier who resigned after seven months with terminal illness.

name: Anthony Eden
summary: Premiership destroyed by the Suez Crisis of 1956.

name: Arthur Balfour
summary: Nephew of Salisbury whose ministry passed the 1902 Education Act and split over tariff reform.

name: Battle of Britain
summary: Air campaign in which RAF Fighter Command defeated the Luftwaffe's bid for air superiority over southern England.

name: Benjamin Disraeli (first ministry)
summary: Succeeded Derby and lost the general election within months.

name: Benjamin Disraeli (second ministry)
summary: Imperialist and social-reform ministry that bought Suez Canal shares and made Victoria Empress of India.

name: Beveridge Report
summary: Social Insurance and Allied Services, the blueprint for the postwar welfare state and its attack on the five giants.

name: Black Wednesday
summary: Sterling was forced out of the European Exchange Rate Mechanism on 16 September 1992, wrecking Conservative economic credibility.

name: Boris Johnson
summary: Won a large majority on getting Brexit done, led the Covid-19 response and resigned amid successive scandals.

name: Brexit Era
summary: Four years of referendum aftermath, parliamentary deadlock, two general elections and eventual withdrawal from the EU.

name: Brexit referendum
summary: The UK voted by 52 to 48 per cent to leave the European Union on 23 June 2016.

name: Withdrawal from the European Union
summary: The UK left the EU on 31 January 2020 and the transition period ended on 31 December 2020 under a trade agreement.

name: British Empire
summary: The worldwide network of English and then British colonies, dominions and dependencies, conventionally dated from Elizabethan claims to the handover of Hong Kong in 1997.

name: American War of Independence
summary: Loss of the thirteen American colonies after Saratoga and Yorktown, recognised at the Peace of Paris.

name: Founding of the modern Commonwealth
summary: The London Declaration made the Commonwealth a free association of equal states with the King as its head.

name: Decolonisation of the British Empire
summary: Withdrawal from India in 1947 through African independence in the 1960s to the handover of Hong Kong in 1997.

name: First Boer War
summary: Transvaal war of independence ending in British defeat at Majuba Hill.

name: Independence and partition of India
summary: British withdrawal created India and Pakistan, with mass displacement and communal violence.

name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
summary: Great uprising against East India Company rule that led to direct Crown government of India.

name: Malayan Emergency
summary: Long counter-insurgency campaign against communist guerrillas in Malaya.

name: Mau Mau Uprising
summary: Kenyan rebellion against colonial land policy, suppressed with mass detention and violence.

name: Navigation Acts
summary: Series of laws reserving colonial trade to English and British shipping, a pillar of mercantilism until repeal.

name: Second Boer War
summary: Long South African war involving sieges, guerrilla resistance, farm burning and concentration camps, ending at Vereeniging.

name: Second British Empire
summary: The eastward-facing empire centred on India, Africa and the settler dominions, at its greatest extent after the First World War.

name: Slavery Abolition Act
summary: Abolished slavery across most of the empire from 1834, with apprenticeship and compensation to slave owners.

name: Statute of Westminster
summary: Recognised legislative independence for the dominions, converting empire into Commonwealth.

name: War of 1812
summary: Anglo-American war fought in Canada and at sea, including the burning of Washington, settled by the Treaty of Ghent.

name: Catholic Emancipation
summary: Roman Catholic Relief Act admitting Catholics to Parliament and most offices, conceded after O'Connell's Clare election.

name: Charles III
summary: Acceded on the death of Elizabeth II in September 2022 and was crowned in May 2023; reigning monarch of the United Kingdom.

name: Chartism
summary: Mass working-class movement for the six points of the People's Charter, including universal male suffrage.

name: Clement Attlee
summary: Built the welfare state and the NHS, nationalised key industries and granted independence to India.

name: Cost of living crisis
summary: Surge in energy and food prices and the sharpest inflation in four decades, squeezing real incomes.

name: Crimean War
summary: Anglo-French war with Russia over the Ottoman Empire, remembered for Balaclava, Inkerman, Sevastopol and Florence Nightingale.

name: David Cameron
summary: Led coalition and then Conservative governments of austerity, the Scottish referendum and the Brexit referendum, resigning after the Leave vote.

name: David Lloyd George
summary: Dynamic wartime premier and peacemaker at Versailles, whose coalition ended with the Irish Treaty and the Chanak crisis.

name: Devolution to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
summary: Referendums of 1997 and the Acts of 1998 created the Scottish Parliament, Welsh Assembly and Northern Ireland Assembly.

name: Duke of Portland (second ministry)
summary: Presided over the Peninsular War's opening and the Walcheren fiasco before ill health forced resignation.

name: Arthur Wellesley, Duke of Wellington (first ministry)
summary: Victor of Waterloo who as premier reluctantly carried Catholic emancipation and opposed parliamentary reform.

name: Duke of Wellington (caretaker ministry)
summary: Held office for about three weeks in November and December 1834 while Peel returned from Italy.

name: Dunkirk evacuation
summary: Operation Dynamo lifted some 338,000 Allied troops from Dunkirk in late May and early June 1940.

name: Charles Grey, Earl Grey
summary: Whig premier who carried the Great Reform Act of 1832 and the abolition of slavery in the empire.

name: George Hamilton-Gordon, Earl of Aberdeen
summary: Peelite-Whig coalition premier who took Britain into the Crimean War and fell over its mismanagement.

name: Edward Smith-Stanley, Earl of Derby (first ministry)
summary: Minority Conservative ministry known as the Who? Who? ministry.

name: Earl of Derby (second ministry)
summary: Minority ministry that transferred Indian government to the Crown and admitted Jews to Parliament.

name: Earl of Derby (third ministry)
summary: Ministry that passed the Second Reform Act of 1867 nearly doubling the electorate.

name: Robert Jenkinson, Earl of Liverpool
summary: Long-serving Tory premier through the defeat of Napoleon, Peterloo, repressive legislation and later liberal reform.

name: Archibald Primrose, Earl of Rosebery
summary: Liberal premier who introduced death duties and was undermined by party divisions.

name: Early Victorian Period
summary: Years of Chartism, railway mania, the Hungry Forties and the repeal of the Corn Laws.

name: Education Act 1944
summary: Butler Act creating free secondary education for all and the tripartite system.

name: Edward Heath
summary: Took Britain into the European Communities in 1973 and fell during the miners' strike and three-day week.

name: Edward VII
summary: First Saxe-Coburg-Gotha monarch, whose reign saw the Entente Cordiale and the constitutional clash over the People's Budget.

name: Edward VIII
summary: Reigned for 326 days in 1936 before abdicating to marry Wallis Simpson; later Duke of Windsor.

name: Edwardian Era
summary: Confident, unequal decade of Edward VII, with Liberal welfare reform and mounting industrial and constitutional conflict.

name: Accession to the European Communities
summary: Britain joined the EEC on 1 January 1973 after two French vetoes, confirmed by referendum in 1975.

name: Elementary Education Act
summary: Forster's Act creating school boards and the framework of state elementary education.

name: Elizabeth II
summary: Longest-reigning British monarch, presiding over decolonisation, the creation of the Commonwealth as a free association and seven decades of change.

name: Equal Franchise Act
summary: Gave women the vote on the same terms as men, at twenty-one.

name: Falklands War
summary: Ten-week war to recover the Falkland Islands after the Argentine invasion of April 1982.

name: General Strike
summary: Nine-day national strike in support of the miners, called off by the TUC without concessions.

name: George Canning
summary: Shortest-serving prime minister, dying after 119 days in office.

name: George IV
summary: Regent from 1811 and then king, famous for extravagance, patronage of the arts and the failed attempt to divorce Queen Caroline.

name: George V
summary: Reigned through the First World War, renamed the dynasty Windsor in 1917 and oversaw Irish partition and the first Labour government.

name: George VI
summary: Unexpected king who became a symbol of resistance in the Second World War and saw Indian independence and the founding of the NHS.

name: Gordon Brown
summary: Former chancellor whose premiership was dominated by the global financial crisis.

name: Government of Ireland Act 1920
summary: Partitioned Ireland by creating separate parliaments for Northern and Southern Ireland.

name: Great Depression in Britain
summary: Slump that brought heavy unemployment to the industrial north and Wales, the Jarrow March and the abandonment of the gold standard.

name: Great Exhibition
summary: Crystal Palace showcase of industry and empire in Hyde Park, visited by six million people.

name: Great Reform Act
summary: Redistributed seats, abolished rotten boroughs and extended the franchise to much of the middle class.

name: Gulf War
summary: British participation in Operation Granby, the coalition campaign to expel Iraq from Kuwait.

name: H. H. Asquith
summary: Presided over the People's Budget, the Parliament Act, the constitutional crisis over Ireland and the first half of the Great War.

name: Harold Macmillan
summary: Presided over affluence and decolonisation's wind of change, resigning amid the Profumo affair.

name: Harold Wilson (first ministries)
summary: Labour premier of devaluation, comprehensive education, Open University and the permissive social reforms of the 1960s.

name: Harold Wilson (second ministries)
summary: Returned in 1974, held the 1975 referendum confirming EC membership and resigned unexpectedly in 1976.

name: Henry Addington
summary: Negotiated the Peace of Amiens and resumed war before making way for Pitt's return.

name: Henry Campbell-Bannerman
summary: Liberal landslide premier who granted self-government to the Transvaal and began welfare legislation.

name: House of Lords Act 1999
summary: Removed all but ninety-two hereditary peers from the House of Lords.

name: House of Saxe-Coburg-Gotha
summary: The dynastic name inherited from Prince Albert, borne by Edward VII and briefly George V until it was changed in 1917.

name: House of Windsor
summary: The reigning royal house, renamed from Saxe-Coburg-Gotha by George V in July 1917 amid wartime anti-German feeling.

name: Human Rights Act 1998
summary: Incorporated the European Convention on Human Rights into domestic law.

name: Iraq War
summary: Controversial British participation in the invasion and occupation of Iraq, later examined by the Chilcot Inquiry.

name: Irish Home Rule Bills
summary: Successive attempts to grant Ireland a devolved parliament, twice defeated and finally enacted but suspended in 1914.

name: James Callaghan
summary: Faced the IMF crisis and the Winter of Discontent, losing a confidence vote in 1979.

name: John Major
summary: Signed the Maastricht Treaty, endured Black Wednesday and began the Northern Ireland peace process.

name: Keir Starmer
summary: Labour leader who won a landslide in July 2024 and is the incumbent prime minister.

name: British involvement in the Korean War
summary: Commonwealth Division fought under United Nations command, notably at the Imjin River.

name: Late Victorian Period
summary: The Long Depression, new imperialism, mass literacy and the rise of organised labour.

name: Liz Truss
summary: Shortest-serving prime minister, resigning after 49 days following the market reaction to her mini-budget.

name: William Grenville, Lord Grenville
summary: Head of the Ministry of All the Talents, which abolished the British slave trade in 1807.

name: Lord John Russell (first ministry)
summary: Whig premier during the Great Irish Famine and the Public Health Act.

name: Earl Russell (second ministry)
summary: Attempted a new reform bill and resigned when it was defeated.

name: Margaret Thatcher
summary: First woman prime minister, who privatised industries, curbed the unions, won the Falklands War and reshaped British political economy.

name: Robert Gascoyne-Cecil, Marquess of Salisbury (first ministry)
summary: First of three Conservative ministries by the last premier to lead from the House of Lords.

name: Marquess of Salisbury (second ministry)
summary: Unionist government of free education, county councils and the scramble for Africa.

name: Marquess of Salisbury (third ministry)
summary: Ministry of the Diamond Jubilee, imperial expansion and the Second Boer War.

name: Mid-Victorian Boom
summary: Era of prosperity, free trade and the workshop of the world, opened by the Great Exhibition.

name: Miners' Strike
summary: Year-long strike against pit closures, defeated by the Thatcher government and decisive for union power.

name: Postwar nationalisations
summary: Attlee government took coal, rail, road haulage, electricity, gas, steel and the Bank of England into public ownership.

name: Neville Chamberlain
summary: Architect of appeasement and the Munich Agreement who declared war in 1939 and fell after the Norway debate.

name: New Labour Era
summary: Third Way project of Blair and Brown: constitutional reform, public investment, market-friendly economics and foreign intervention.

name: Founding of the National Health Service
summary: Bevan's NHS opened on 5 July 1948, providing healthcare free at the point of use across Britain.

name: Northern Ireland
summary: Constituted in 1921 from six Ulster counties under the Government of Ireland Act, remaining part of the United Kingdom after partition.

name: Bloody Sunday
summary: Paratroopers shot dead thirteen civil rights marchers in Derry on 30 January 1972, with a fourteenth dying later.

name: Good Friday Agreement
summary: Settlement establishing power-sharing devolution, cross-border bodies and consent for constitutional change.

name: The Troubles
summary: Three decades of conflict in Northern Ireland between republicans, loyalists and the British state, ending with the Good Friday Agreement.

name: Parliament Act 1911
summary: Removed the Lords' veto over money bills and replaced it with a delaying power, asserting Commons supremacy.

name: People's Budget
summary: Lloyd George's redistributive budget, rejected by the Lords and triggering the constitutional crisis.

name: Peterloo Massacre
summary: Cavalry charged a mass meeting for parliamentary reform at St Peter's Field, Manchester, killing at least eleven.

name: Poll tax and its riots
summary: The Community Charge provoked mass non-payment and rioting, contributing to Thatcher's fall and its abolition.

name: Poor Law Amendment Act
summary: Created the union workhouse system on principles of deterrence and less eligibility.

name: Postwar Austerity
summary: Years of rationing, dollar shortage, the 1947 fuel crisis and reconstruction under the Attlee and Churchill governments.

name: Postwar Consensus
summary: Broad agreement across parties on the welfare state, full employment, mixed economy and union consultation.

name: Privatisation programme
summary: Sale of state industries including BT, British Gas, water, electricity and rail, reshaping the British economy.

name: Ramsay MacDonald (first ministry)
summary: First Labour prime minister, heading a minority government for nine months.

name: Ramsay MacDonald (second and National ministries)
summary: Labour premier overwhelmed by the slump who formed a National Government in 1931 and was expelled from his party.

name: Regency Era
summary: Formal regency of the Prince of Wales during George III's incapacity, byword for elegance, dandyism and Austen's novels.

name: Repeal of the Corn Laws
summary: Peel's abolition of agricultural protection, embracing free trade and splitting the Conservative Party.

name: Representation of the People Act 1918
summary: Gave the vote to all men over 21 and to women over 30 with property qualifications, tripling the electorate.

name: Rishi Sunak
summary: First British Asian prime minister, governing amid inflation and losing the 2024 general election.

name: Robert Peel (first ministry)
summary: Minority ministry that issued the Tamworth Manifesto and fell after the 1835 election.

name: Robert Peel (second ministry)
summary: Reformed tariffs and income tax, founded the modern police tradition and split his party by repealing the Corn Laws.

name: Scottish independence referendum
summary: Scotland voted 55 to 45 per cent against independence on a record turnout.

name: Second Reform Act
summary: Extended the vote to urban working-class male householders, roughly doubling the electorate.

name: Ballot Act
summary: Introduced secret voting in parliamentary and local elections, curbing intimidation.

name: Spencer Perceval
summary: The only British prime minister to be assassinated, shot in the lobby of the House of Commons in May 1812.

name: Stanley Baldwin (first ministry)
summary: Called a snap election on protection and lost his majority.

name: Stanley Baldwin (second ministry)
summary: Ministry of the return to the gold standard, the General Strike of 1926 and the equal franchise of 1928.

name: Stanley Baldwin (third ministry)
summary: Managed the abdication crisis and began rearmament while pursuing conciliation abroad.

name: Suez Crisis
summary: Anglo-French-Israeli operation against Nasser's Egypt, abandoned under American and international pressure, exposing Britain's diminished power.

name: Women's suffrage movement
summary: Campaign of suffragists and suffragettes that won votes for women over thirty in 1918 and equal franchise in 1928.

name: Swinging Sixties
summary: Decade of British pop culture, fashion, the Beatles, permissive legislation and social liberalisation centred on London.

name: Thatcherism
summary: Programme of monetarism, privatisation, union curbs, deregulation and popular capitalism associated with Margaret Thatcher.

name: The Blitz
summary: German bombing of British cities from September 1940 to May 1941, killing over 40,000 civilians and devastating London, Coventry and others.

name: Theresa May
summary: Sought to deliver Brexit but could not pass her withdrawal agreement through Parliament.

name: Third Reform Act
summary: Extended household franchise to the counties, enfranchising agricultural labourers and miners.

name: Tony Blair
summary: New Labour premier of devolution, the Good Friday Agreement, public spending growth and the Iraq War.

name: Austerity
summary: Deficit-reduction programme of spending cuts and welfare reform after the financial crisis, under coalition and Conservative governments.

name: Frederick Robinson, Viscount Goderich
summary: Unable to hold his coalition together and resigned without facing Parliament.

name: William Lamb, Viscount Melbourne (first ministry)
summary: Brief first ministry dismissed by William IV, the last time a monarch removed a premier commanding Commons support.

name: Viscount Melbourne (second ministry)
summary: Mentor to the young Queen Victoria, presiding over Chartist agitation and the new Poor Law.

name: Henry Temple, Viscount Palmerston (first ministry)
summary: Brought the Crimean War to a close and suppressed the Indian Rebellion, ending Company rule.

name: Viscount Palmerston (second ministry)
summary: Steered neutrality in the American Civil War and died in office aged 81.

name: William Ewart Gladstone (first ministry)
summary: Great reforming Liberal ministry: Irish disestablishment, the Education Act, the secret ballot and army and civil service reform.

name: William Gladstone (second ministry)
summary: Third Reform Act, Egyptian occupation and the death of Gordon at Khartoum.

name: William Gladstone (third ministry)
summary: Introduced the First Irish Home Rule Bill, splitting the Liberal Party.

name: William Gladstone (fourth ministry)
summary: Aged premier whose Second Home Rule Bill passed the Commons but was rejected by the Lords.

name: William IV
summary: Sailor king whose short reign saw the Great Reform Act, the abolition of slavery in the colonies and the new Poor Law.

name: William Pitt the Younger (second ministry)
summary: Formed the Third Coalition against Napoleon and died in office weeks after Austerlitz.

name: Arrival of the Empire Windrush
summary: The Windrush brought Caribbean migrants to Tilbury, a symbolic beginning of large-scale postwar Commonwealth immigration.

name: Winston Churchill (wartime ministry)
summary: Led the wartime coalition to victory over Nazi Germany, defining British resolve in 1940.

name: Winston Churchill (peacetime ministry)
summary: Returned to office aged 76, ending rationing and accepting most of the postwar settlement.

name: Winter of Discontent
summary: Wave of public sector strikes against pay restraint that destroyed the Callaghan government's authority.

name: Wars of the Three Kingdoms
summary: The interlocking conflicts in England, Scotland and Ireland including the Civil Wars, Covenanter risings and the Cromwellian conquest of Ireland.

name: Global Abolition of Slavery
summary: Successive abolitions from revolutionary France and Britain to Brazil that ended legal chattel slavery in the Atlantic world.

name: Age of Revolutions
summary: Atlantic and European revolutions that spread republicanism, nationalism and abolition.

name: Anthropogenic Climate Change
summary: Industrial-era warming from greenhouse gases, now a central issue of international politics.

name: Rise of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Deep learning and large language models that moved AI into mainstream economic and political consequence.

name: Atlantic Slave Trade
summary: Forced transport of roughly 12.5 million Africans to the Americas, the foundation of the plantation economies.

name: Bretton Woods System
summary: Postwar monetary order of fixed exchange rates and dollar-gold convertibility, with the IMF and World Bank.

name: BRICS
summary: Grouping of major emerging economies, originally Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, later expanded.

name: Decolonisation
summary: Dissolution of the European empires and the emergence of scores of new states across Asia, Africa and the Pacific.

name: Early Modern Period
summary: Era of gunpowder empires, printing, global commerce, scientific revolution and Atlantic slavery.

name: End of the Cold War
summary: Collapse of the Eastern bloc and dissolution of the USSR, leaving the United States as sole superpower.

name: First Age of Globalisation
summary: Steamships, telegraphs, gold standard and mass migration that integrated the world economy before 1914.

name: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
summary: Postwar framework of trade negotiation rounds that lowered tariffs worldwide, replaced by the WTO.

name: Genocide Convention
summary: UN convention defining and criminalising genocide, drafted after the Holocaust.

name: Global Silver Trade
summary: American silver flowing via Europe and Manila to China, the first genuinely global commodity circuit.

name: Contemporary Globalisation
summary: Deepening integration of trade, finance, production and information, with container shipping and the internet.

name: Age of Mass Migration
summary: Roughly 55 million Europeans and millions of Asians migrated across oceans, reshaping settler societies.

name: Green Revolution
summary: High-yield crop varieties, fertiliser and irrigation that greatly increased food production in Asia and Latin America.

name: HIV/AIDS Pandemic
summary: Global epidemic that has killed tens of millions, transformed by antiretroviral therapy from the late 1990s.

name: The Holocaust
summary: Nazi genocide of about six million Jews, alongside the murder of Roma, disabled people and others.

name: Auschwitz-Birkenau
summary: Largest Nazi concentration and extermination camp, where about 1.1 million people were murdered.

name: Wannsee Conference
summary: Meeting of German officials to coordinate the deportation and murder of Europe's Jews.

name: International Monetary Fund
summary: Institution created at Bretton Woods to lend to countries in balance-of-payments difficulty.

name: Information Revolution
summary: Microprocessors, personal computing, the internet and mobile networks that reorganised economy and society.

name: International Criminal Court
summary: Permanent court for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity, created by the Rome Statute.

name: Interwar Period
summary: Two decades of fragile peace: reparations, boom, depression, fascism and the collapse of collective security.

name: Kyoto Protocol
summary: First binding treaty on greenhouse-gas emissions, in force from 2005 without US ratification.

name: League of Nations
summary: First general international organisation for collective security, weakened by absences and its failures in the 1930s.

name: Seventeenth-Century Crisis
summary: Cooling climate, harvest failure, war and rebellion from Europe to China in a century of upheaval.

name: League of Nations Mandate System
summary: Administration of former German and Ottoman territories by the victors as trusteeships in name.

name: Marshall Plan
summary: American aid programme of about 13 billion dollars that rebuilt Western European economies and tied them together.

name: Armenian Genocide
summary: Systematic deportation and killing of about 1.5 million Armenians, alongside Assyrians and Greeks.

name: Gallipoli Campaign
summary: Allied failure to force the Dardanelles, a formative event for Turkish, Australian and New Zealand identity.

name: Ottoman Decline and Reform
summary: Territorial losses to Russia and Austria, Janissary revolts, and the reforming reigns of Selim III and Mahmud II.

name: Ottoman Empire (Early Modern)
summary: Height of Ottoman power from Selim I's conquests to the Treaty of Karlowitz, spanning three continents.

name: Ottoman Entry into the First World War
summary: Alliance with Germany brought campaigns at Gallipoli, in Mesopotamia, the Caucasus and Palestine.

name: First Ottoman Constitutional Era
summary: Brief constitutional government under the 1876 Kanun-i Esasi, suspended by Abdulhamid II.

name: Sultanate of Women
summary: Period when imperial mothers and consorts exercised great political power in the Ottoman court.

name: Reign of Abdulhamid II
summary: Autocratic sultan of railways and pan-Islamism who suspended parliament and was deposed by the Young Turks.

name: Reign of Mahmud II
summary: Destroyed the Janissaries in 1826 and began sweeping military and administrative Westernisation.

name: Reign of Selim I
summary: Conquered the Mamluk sultanate and the Hejaz, bringing the caliphate and holy cities under Ottoman rule.

name: Reign of Suleiman the Magnificent
summary: Longest-reigning sultan: conquest of Belgrade, Rhodes and Hungary, legal codification and the siege of Vienna.

name: Tanzimat
summary: Reform era of legal equality, codified law, conscription and centralisation.

name: Treaty of Karlowitz
summary: First treaty in which the Ottomans ceded major territory, giving Hungary to the Habsburgs.

name: Treaty of Sevres
summary: Punitive partition treaty rejected by the Turkish nationalists and superseded by Lausanne.

name: Young Turk Revolution
summary: Committee of Union and Progress forced the restoration of the constitution and parliament.

name: North Atlantic Treaty Organization
summary: Transatlantic military alliance founded in 1949 on collective defence under Article 5, now 32 members.

name: New Imperialism
summary: Intense European, American and Japanese colonial expansion into Africa, Asia and the Pacific.

name: Non-Aligned Movement
summary: Grouping of states refusing Cold War alignment, founded at Belgrade after the Bandung Conference.

name: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
summary: Treaty limiting the spread of nuclear weapons while recognising five nuclear-weapon states.

name: 1973 Oil Crisis
summary: Arab oil embargo that quadrupled prices, ending the postwar boom and reshaping energy policy.

name: Paris Agreement
summary: Universal climate accord committing states to limit warming well below two degrees Celsius.

name: Paris Peace Conference and Treaty of Versailles
summary: Settlement that redrew Europe and the Middle East, imposed reparations on Germany and created the League and mandates.

name: Rise of Fascism
summary: Spread of fascist and authoritarian movements in Italy, Germany, Spain, Japan and beyond between the wars.

name: Comecon
summary: Soviet-led economic organisation coordinating the planned economies of the Eastern bloc.

name: Detente
summary: Easing of superpower tension with SALT, the Helsinki Accords and expanded trade, ended by Afghanistan.

name: Second Cold War
summary: Renewed confrontation after Afghanistan, with missile deployments, SDI and heightened nuclear risk.

name: Warsaw Pact
summary: Soviet-led military alliance of Eastern bloc states, dissolved in 1991.

name: Inchon Landing
summary: MacArthur's amphibious envelopment that recaptured Seoul and reversed the North Korean advance.

name: Eradication of Smallpox
summary: WHO campaign that eliminated smallpox, the only human disease so far eradicated.

name: Spanish Flu Pandemic
summary: Influenza pandemic that infected a third of humanity and killed an estimated 50 million people.

name: Third World and Global South
summary: Category for states outside the Western and Soviet blocs, later reframed as the Global South.

name: United Nations
summary: Universal international organisation founded in San Francisco in 1945, with 193 member states.

name: United Nations Security Council
summary: Fifteen-member body with five permanent vetoes, responsible for international peace and security.

name: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
summary: UN General Assembly declaration setting out a common standard of rights for all peoples.

name: Spread of Universal Suffrage
summary: Extension of the vote to women and excluded groups, from New Zealand in 1893 to South Africa in 1994.

name: World Health Organization
summary: UN agency for international health, which coordinated smallpox eradication and pandemic responses.

name: World Bank
summary: Development lender founded at Bretton Woods, originally for postwar reconstruction.

name: Modern Population Explosion
summary: Growth from about one billion people in 1800 to over eight billion, driven by falling mortality.

name: World Trade Organization
summary: Organisation governing world trade rules and disputes, founded in 1995 from GATT.

name: World Wide Web
summary: Berners-Lee's invention at CERN that made the internet a mass medium.

name: ANZAC Landing at Gallipoli
summary: Landing of 25 April 1915 that became the founding national legend of both countries.

name: Apology to the Stolen Generations
summary: Prime Minister Kevin Rudd's formal parliamentary apology to Indigenous Australians.

name: Convict Transportation to Australia
summary: About 162,000 convicts were transported to Australian colonies over eighty years.

name: Federation of Australia
summary: Six colonies united as the Commonwealth of Australia on 1 January 1901.

name: Australian Frontier Wars
summary: Sustained violent dispossession of Aboriginal peoples across the continent, with massacres and mass mortality.

name: Australian Gold Rushes
summary: Victorian and New South Wales gold discoveries that tripled the population and reshaped politics.

name: Australian Postwar Immigration Programme
summary: Mass European then global immigration that transformed Australia into a multicultural society.

name: Australian Referendum of 1967
summary: Over 90 percent voted to allow federal laws for Aboriginal people and their inclusion in the census.

name: Australian Republic Referendum
summary: Voters rejected replacing the monarchy with a parliamentary-appointed president.

name: Stolen Generations
summary: Policies of removing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children from their families.

name: Indigenous Voice Referendum
summary: Proposal for an Indigenous advisory body in the constitution, rejected by voters.

name: Bombing of Darwin
summary: Japanese air raids on northern Australia that shifted strategic reliance from Britain to the United States.

name: Colony of New South Wales
summary: First British colony in Australia, originally a penal settlement covering most of the continent.

name: Colony of Queensland
summary: Northern colony separated in 1859, built on pastoralism, sugar and Pacific Islander labour.

name: Colony of South Australia
summary: Free-settler colony founded on Wakefield's systematic colonisation principles.

name: Colony of Tasmania
summary: Van Diemen's Land separated from New South Wales, notorious for convict settlements and the Black War.

name: Colony of Victoria
summary: Separated from New South Wales in 1851 and transformed within a decade by the gold rush.

name: Colony of Western Australia
summary: Swan River settlement that later accepted convicts and boomed with 1890s goldfields.

name: Cook's Voyage to the East Coast of Australia
summary: James Cook charted the east coast and claimed it for Britain at Possession Island.

name: Dutch Exploration of New Holland
summary: Dutch navigators charted much of the Australian coast without settling, naming it New Holland.

name: Eureka Stockade
summary: Miners' revolt at Ballarat over licence fees, later mythologised as a birth of Australian democracy.

name: First Fleet
summary: Arrival of eleven ships at Sydney Cove on 26 January 1788 founded the penal colony of New South Wales.

name: Mabo Decision
summary: High Court ruling recognising native title and rejecting the doctrine of terra nullius.

name: Premiership of Robert Menzies
summary: Australia's longest-serving prime minister, presiding over postwar growth, ANZUS and the Cold War alignment.

name: White Australia Policy
summary: Immigration Restriction Act and successors that excluded non-European migrants for seven decades.

name: Dismissal of the Whitlam Government
summary: Governor-General Kerr dismissed Prime Minister Gough Whitlam, Australia's gravest constitutional crisis.

name: French Polynesia
summary: French overseas collectivity of 121 islands, site of nuclear testing at Mururoa.

name: Independent State of Samoa
summary: Polynesian state independent since 1962, with a fa'amatai chiefly political system.

name: Independence of Samoa
summary: First Pacific island state to gain independence, from New Zealand trusteeship.

name: Bougainville Conflict
summary: Secessionist war over the Panguna mine, ended by peace accords and a 2019 independence referendum.

name: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
summary: Independent from Australian administration in 1975, the most linguistically diverse country on earth.

name: Republic of Vanuatu
summary: Independent in 1980 from the Anglo-French New Hebrides condominium.

name: Federated States of Micronesia
summary: Four-state federation in free association with the United States since 1986.

name: Republic of Kiribati
summary: Micronesian atoll republic independent from Britain in 1979.

name: Republic of the Marshall Islands
summary: Freely associated state since 1986, site of US nuclear testing at Bikini and Enewetak.

name: Republic of Nauru
summary: Tiny phosphate island state independent in 1968, later dependent on offshore processing agreements.

name: Republic of Palau
summary: Last part of the Pacific trust territory to become independent, in free association with the US.

name: New Caledonia
summary: French territory with a large Kanak population and repeated independence referendums under the Noumea Accord.

name: Pacific Decolonisation
summary: Successive independences from Samoa in 1962 to Palau in 1994, leaving some territories under metropolitan rule.

name: Pacific Islands Forum
summary: Regional political grouping of Pacific states, prominent in climate diplomacy.

name: Nuclear Testing in the Pacific
summary: American, British and French tests at Bikini, Christmas Island, Maralinga and Mururoa with lasting contamination.

name: Colony of New Zealand
summary: British colony that gained self-government in 1852 and fought the New Zealand Wars over land.

name: Cook's Circumnavigation of New Zealand
summary: Cook charted both main islands, opening sustained European contact with Maori.

name: Dominion of New Zealand
summary: Self-governing dominion from 1907, fully sovereign under the 1947 adoption of the Statute of Westminster.

name: Musket Wars
summary: Inter-iwi wars transformed by trade muskets, causing large casualties and migrations before colonisation.

name: New Zealand Nuclear-Free Policy
summary: Ban on nuclear-armed and nuclear-powered ships that suspended New Zealand's ANZUS obligations.

name: New Zealand Wars
summary: Conflicts between the Crown, settlers and Maori over sovereignty and land, followed by large confiscations.

name: New Zealand Women's Suffrage
summary: First self-governing country to grant women the parliamentary vote.

name: Treaty of Waitangi
summary: Agreement between the Crown and Maori chiefs, with differing English and Maori texts, New Zealand's founding document.

name: Waitangi Tribunal
summary: Body established to investigate Crown breaches of the Treaty of Waitangi and recommend redress.

name: Republic of Fiji
summary: Independent in 1970 and a republic since 1987, with four coups over ethnic and political disputes.

name: Colony of Fiji
summary: British colony whose sugar plantations imported indentured Indian labour, reshaping its society.

name: Solomon Islands
summary: Melanesian state independent from Britain in 1978, with ethnic conflict and a regional intervention from 2003.

name: Tuvalu
summary: Polynesian atoll state independent in 1978, among the most exposed to sea-level rise.

name: Afghan Civil War of the 1990s
summary: Factional war after Najibullah's fall, won largely by the Taliban from 1996.

name: All-India Muslim League
summary: Party founded in Dhaka that under Jinnah demanded and won Pakistan.

name: Anglo-Afghan Wars
summary: Three British wars that failed to control Afghanistan, which won full independence in 1919.

name: Dominion of Ceylon and Sri Lanka
summary: Independent in 1948, renamed Sri Lanka as a republic in 1972 after decades of communal tension.

name: British Ceylon
summary: Crown colony after the fall of Kandy, with plantation tea and Tamil labour migration.

name: Durrani Empire
summary: Ahmad Shah Durrani's empire stretching from Mashhad to Delhi, the foundation of modern Afghanistan.

name: Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal
summary: Republic declared in 2008 after the Maoist war and the 2001 royal massacre.

name: Kingdom of Nepal
summary: Shah dynasty state unified by Prithvi Narayan Shah, long dominated by the Rana premiers.

name: Nepalese Civil War
summary: Maoist insurgency that killed some 17,000 and led to the monarchy's abolition.

name: Rana Regime
summary: Hereditary prime ministers who reduced the Shah kings to figureheads for a century.

name: First Kashmir War
summary: War over Kashmir after the maharaja's accession to India, ending with the ceasefire line.

name: Indian and Pakistani Nuclear Tests
summary: Pokhran-II and Chagai tests made both states declared nuclear powers.

name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1965
summary: Second war over Kashmir, ended by the Soviet-brokered Tashkent Declaration.

name: Islamic Republic of Afghanistan
summary: Western-backed republic under Karzai and Ghani that collapsed as US forces left.

name: Islamic Republic of Pakistan
summary: Republic since 1956, alternating between civilian and military rule, nuclear-armed since 1998.

name: Rule of Ayub Khan
summary: First military ruler: the Decade of Development, the 1965 war and Islamabad's construction.

name: Premierships of Benazir Bhutto
summary: First woman to lead a Muslim-majority state, twice prime minister; assassinated in 2007.

name: Dominion of Pakistan
summary: Independent Pakistan under the crown, founded by Jinnah as a homeland for South Asian Muslims.

name: Leadership of Muhammad Ali Jinnah
summary: Quaid-i-Azam and founder of Pakistan, its first governor-general.

name: Rule of Pervez Musharraf
summary: Coup leader who allied with the US after 9/11 and resigned amid the lawyers' movement.

name: Rule of Zia-ul-Haq
summary: Islamising military dictatorship that backed the Afghan mujahideen; died in an air crash.

name: Government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
summary: Populist leader who wrote the 1973 constitution and began the nuclear programme; overthrown and hanged.

name: Kargil War
summary: High-altitude conflict after Pakistani infiltration into Indian-held Kashmir.

name: Kingdom of Afghanistan
summary: Monarchy under Amanullah, Nadir Shah and Zahir Shah, ended by Daoud's republican coup.

name: Kingdom of Bhutan
summary: Himalayan Wangchuck monarchy, constitutional since 2008 and known for Gross National Happiness.

name: Reign of Aurangzeb
summary: Expanded the empire to its greatest extent while exhausting it in the Deccan wars.

name: Reign of Babur
summary: Founder of the Mughal Empire, victorious at Panipat over the Delhi Sultanate.

name: Reign of Jahangir
summary: Reign of court painting, Nur Jahan's influence and the first English embassy.

name: Reign of Shah Jahan
summary: Builder of the Taj Mahal and Shahjahanabad, deposed by his son Aurangzeb.

name: People's Republic of Bangladesh
summary: Independent since 1971, one of the world's most densely populated states and a garment-export power.

name: Bangladeshi Uprising of 2024
summary: Student-led protests over job quotas that toppled Sheikh Hasina's government.

name: Premierships of Sheikh Hasina
summary: Prime minister 1996-2001 and 2009-24, whose long rule ended in a student uprising and her flight in 2024.

name: Republic of India
summary: World's largest democracy, a federal republic under the 1950 constitution and the most populous country since 2023.

name: Anglo-Maratha Wars
summary: Three wars that destroyed Maratha power and made the Company paramount in India.

name: Anglo-Mysore Wars
summary: Four wars ending with the death of Tipu Sultan at Seringapatam.

name: Battle of Plassey
summary: Clive's victory in Bengal that began British territorial power in India.

name: Great Bengal Famine of 1770
summary: Famine under early Company rule that killed several million Bengalis.

name: Bengal Famine of 1943
summary: Wartime famine that killed some three million people in Bengal.

name: Partition of Bengal (1905)
summary: Curzon's division of Bengal, reversed after the swadeshi agitation it provoked.

name: Dominion of India
summary: Independent India under the crown until the republican constitution took effect.

name: East India Company Rule in India
summary: Company government from Plassey to the Crown takeover, extended by conquest, subsidiary alliances and revenue farming.

name: Indian Constitution
summary: Ambedkar-led constitution effective 26 January 1950, abolishing untouchability and creating a secular federal republic.

name: Indian Economic Liberalisation
summary: Balance-of-payments crisis reforms under Rao and Manmohan Singh that opened the economy.

name: The Emergency
summary: Twenty-one months of suspended civil liberties, press censorship and forced sterilisation under Indira Gandhi.

name: Integration of the Princely States
summary: Accession of over 500 princely states, including Hyderabad's forcible annexation.

name: Founding of the Indian National Congress
summary: First all-India nationalist organisation, later the vehicle of the independence movement.

name: Premiership of Indira Gandhi
summary: Prime minister 1966-77 and 1980-84: bank nationalisation, the 1971 war, the Emergency and her assassination.

name: Kingdom of Mysore
summary: South Indian state whose rulers Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan fought four wars against the British.

name: Premiership of Narendra Modi
summary: BJP prime minister: demonetisation, GST, abrogation of Article 370 and Hindu-nationalist consolidation.

name: Premiership of Jawaharlal Nehru
summary: Founding prime minister: planning, non-alignment, states reorganisation and the 1962 war with China.

name: Non-Cooperation Movement
summary: Gandhi's first mass satyagraha, boycotting British schools, courts and goods.

name: Operation Blue Star
summary: Army assault on the Golden Temple against Sikh militants, followed by Indira Gandhi's assassination and anti-Sikh pogroms.

name: Quit India Movement
summary: Congress demand for immediate independence, met by mass arrests and repression.

name: Salt March
summary: Gandhi's 385-kilometre march to Dandi against the salt tax, launching civil disobedience.

name: Sino-Indian War
summary: Chinese victory in the Himalayan border war that shattered Nehru's China policy.

name: Third Battle of Panipat
summary: Afghan victory over the Marathas that crippled the leading Indian power and eased British expansion.

name: Republic of Maldives
summary: Indian Ocean island state independent from Britain in 1965, a republic from 1968.

name: Saur Revolution
summary: Communist coup that installed the PDPA and triggered rural revolt and Soviet intervention.

name: Reign of Shivaji
summary: Founder-king who built a Maratha state through guerrilla war against the Mughals and Bijapur.

name: Soviet-Afghan War
summary: Nine-year Soviet occupation opposed by US- and Pakistan-backed mujahideen, ending in withdrawal.

name: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (first period)
summary: Taliban rule imposing strict shari'a and sheltering al-Qaeda, ended by US-led intervention.

name: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (restored)
summary: Taliban government since August 2021, unrecognised and enforcing severe restrictions on women.

name: United States War in Afghanistan
summary: Twenty-year NATO-led war after 9/11, ending in Taliban restoration and Western withdrawal.

name: Association of Southeast Asian Nations
summary: Regional organisation founded in Bangkok, now ten member states pursuing economic and security cooperation.

name: Bandung Conference
summary: First large Asian-African conference, a founding moment of Third World solidarity and non-alignment.

name: Brunei Darussalam
summary: Oil-rich Malay Islamic sultanate fully independent from Britain in 1984.

name: Premiership of Lee Kuan Yew
summary: Founding prime minister for 31 years who built a developmental, one-party-dominant state.

name: Republic of Singapore
summary: City-state that grew from an entrepot to a global financial hub under Lee Kuan Yew's People's Action Party.

name: Separation of Singapore from Malaysia
summary: Singapore was expelled from the federation and became an independent republic on 9 August 1965.

name: First Indochina War
summary: Viet Minh war against France that ended with Dien Bien Phu and the Geneva Accords.

name: Geneva Accords
summary: Agreements partitioning Vietnam at the 17th parallel and recognising Laotian and Cambodian independence.

name: Japanese Occupation of Indochina
summary: Japanese control alongside Vichy French administration, ending in the 1945 coup and Vietnamese famine.

name: Kingdom of Cambodia
summary: Restored constitutional monarchy, dominated politically by Hun Sen and his family since 1985.

name: Cambodian Genocide
summary: Mass killing, starvation and forced labour under the Khmer Rouge, about a quarter of the population.

name: Khmer Republic
summary: US-aligned republic under Lon Nol, defeated by the Khmer Rouge.

name: Democratic Kampuchea
summary: Khmer Rouge regime under Pol Pot that emptied the cities and killed some 1.7 to 2 million people.

name: Kingdom of Cambodia (1953-1970)
summary: Sihanouk's independent, neutralist kingdom, ended by Lon Nol's coup.

name: French Protectorate of Cambodia
summary: Norodom's kingdom under French protection within Indochina.

name: UN Transitional Authority in Cambodia
summary: UN administration that organised elections and restored the monarchy.

name: Vietnamese Intervention in Cambodia
summary: Vietnamese invasion that ousted the Khmer Rouge and installed the People's Republic of Kampuchea.

name: Kingdom of Thailand
summary: Constitutional monarchy renamed Thailand in 1939, with a modern history of frequent military coups.

name: Late Ayutthaya Kingdom
summary: Siamese kingdom of great wealth and cosmopolitan trade, destroyed by the Burmese in 1767.

name: Chakri Dynasty
summary: Bangkok dynasty that preserved Siamese independence through the colonial era and still reigns.

name: Reign of Bhumibol Adulyadej
summary: Rama IX reigned seventy years, becoming a unifying symbol through repeated coups.

name: Reign of Chulalongkorn
summary: Rama V abolished slavery, modernised administration and ceded border lands to keep Siam independent.

name: Reign of Mongkut
summary: Rama IV opened Siam to Western trade and diplomacy while preserving sovereignty.

name: Reign of Vajiralongkorn
summary: Rama X, king since 2016, whose reign has seen youth protests over royal reform.

name: Siamese Revolution of 1932
summary: Bloodless coup that ended absolute monarchy and created a constitutional system dominated by the military.

name: Lao People's Democratic Republic
summary: Communist state proclaimed after the Pathet Lao victory, the world's most heavily bombed country per capita.

name: Kingdom of Laos
summary: Independent kingdom torn by civil war and the Vietnam War's spillover bombing.

name: Laotian Civil War
summary: Pathet Lao and North Vietnamese struggle against royalists, with a massive covert US air campaign.

name: Vietnamese August Revolution
summary: Viet Minh seizure of power and Ho Chi Minh's declaration of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
summary: Viet Minh victory over the French garrison that ended French rule in Indochina.

name: Doi Moi
summary: Market-oriented reforms that transformed Vietnam into a fast-growing export economy.

name: Fall of Saigon
summary: North Vietnamese capture of Saigon on 30 April 1975 ended the war.

name: French Conquest of Vietnam
summary: Campaigns from Saigon to Tonkin that made Vietnam a French colony and protectorates.

name: Leadership of Ho Chi Minh
summary: Founder of Vietnamese communism and president of North Vietnam until his death.

name: Later Le Dynasty and Trinh-Nguyen Division
summary: Nominal Le kings with real power split between the Trinh lords in the north and the Nguyen in the south.

name: Democratic Republic of Vietnam
summary: Communist northern state under Ho Chi Minh, which won the war and unified the country in 1976.

name: Socialist Republic of Vietnam
summary: Unified communist state since 1976, market-reforming since doi moi in 1986.

name: Republic of Vietnam
summary: Anti-communist southern state under Diem then Thieu, which collapsed with the fall of Saigon.

name: Tet Offensive
summary: Coordinated communist attacks that failed militarily but broke American public support for the war.

name: Malaysia
summary: Federation formed in 1963 with Sabah, Sarawak and briefly Singapore; a rotating elective monarchy.

name: British Malaya
summary: Federated and unfederated Malay states under British protection, built on tin and rubber.

name: Federation of Malaya
summary: Independent Malaya from 31 August 1957 under Tunku Abdul Rahman.

name: Portuguese Conquest of Malacca
summary: Albuquerque's capture of Malacca gave Portugal control of a key Asian trade chokepoint.

name: Malayan Emergency
summary: British counterinsurgency against the Malayan Communist Party using resettlement and 'new villages'.

name: Straits Settlements
summary: British colony of Penang, Malacca and Singapore, the hub of colonial commerce in the region.

name: Aceh War
summary: Long Dutch war to subdue the Aceh sultanate, one of the colonial era's most costly campaigns.

name: Indonesian Mass Killings of 1965-66
summary: Army-led massacre of at least half a million alleged communists after a failed coup.

name: Indonesian National Awakening
summary: Rise of nationalist organisations from Budi Utomo to Sukarno's PNI and the 1928 Youth Pledge.

name: Indonesian National Revolution
summary: Four-year struggle after the 17 August 1945 proclamation that forced Dutch recognition of independence.

name: Reformasi
summary: Democratisation after Suharto's fall, with decentralisation and direct presidential elections.

name: Japanese Occupation of the Dutch East Indies
summary: Three years of Japanese rule that destroyed Dutch authority and armed Indonesian nationalists.

name: Java War
summary: Diponegoro's revolt against Dutch rule, ending in his exile and the cultivation system.

name: New Order
summary: Suharto's authoritarian developmental regime, ended by the Asian financial crisis and mass protest.

name: Presidency of Sukarno
summary: Founding president: Pancasila, Bandung Conference, Guided Democracy and confrontation with Malaysia.

name: Republic of the Philippines
summary: Southeast Asian republic independent since 1946, with the Marcos dictatorship and People Power in its history.

name: American Colonial Philippines
summary: US colonial rule with public schooling and English, moving to Commonwealth status in 1935.

name: Commonwealth of the Philippines
summary: Transitional self-government under Manuel Quezon, interrupted by Japanese occupation.

name: Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte
summary: Presidency defined by a lethal anti-drug campaign and pivot toward China.

name: First Philippine Republic
summary: Aguinaldo's Malolos republic, suppressed in the Philippine-American War.

name: Magellan's Arrival in the Philippines
summary: First European contact and Magellan's death at Mactan during the first circumnavigation.

name: Marcos Regime
summary: Ferdinand Marcos ruled 21 years, including 14 under martial law with plunder and repression.

name: People Power Revolution
summary: Four days of mass non-violent protest that ousted Marcos and installed Corazon Aquino.

name: Philippine-American War
summary: American conquest of the islands, with an estimated 200,000 or more Filipino civilian deaths.

name: Philippine Independence
summary: The United States granted independence on 4 July 1946.

name: Philippine Revolution
summary: Katipunan revolt under Bonifacio and Aguinaldo that ended Spanish rule.

name: Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste
summary: Independent in 2002 after a UN-run referendum and transitional administration.

name: Indonesian Occupation of East Timor
summary: Invasion and annexation after Portuguese withdrawal, with perhaps 100,000 to 200,000 deaths.

name: Union of Burma and Myanmar
summary: Independent from Britain in 1948, under military rule for most of its history and renamed Myanmar in 1989.

name: Anglo-Burmese Wars
summary: Three wars ending in the annexation of all Burma to British India.

name: Political Career of Aung San Suu Kyi
summary: Nobel laureate held under house arrest for 15 years, later state counsellor and detained again in 2021.

name: British Burma
summary: Province of British India until 1937 and then a separate colony, occupied by Japan in 1942-45.

name: Burmese Uprising of 1988
summary: Nationwide pro-democracy protests crushed by the army, which then formed the SLORC junta.

name: Myanmar Coup of 2021
summary: Military seizure of power that sparked nationwide armed resistance and civil war.

name: Rule of Ne Win
summary: Coup leader whose Burmese Way to Socialism isolated and impoverished the country.

name: Rohingya Crisis
summary: Military campaigns that drove over 700,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh, alleged as genocide.

name: Abraham Accords
summary: Normalisation agreements between Israel and the UAE, Bahrain, Morocco and Sudan.

name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
summary: War following Israel's declaration, ending in armistice lines and the displacement of most Palestinian Arabs.

name: Arab League
summary: Regional organisation of Arab states founded in Cairo in 1945.

name: Arab Revolt
summary: Hashemite rising against Ottoman rule, encouraged by Britain and aided by T. E. Lawrence.

name: Arab Spring
summary: Wave of uprisings from Tunisia to Bahrain that toppled four rulers and triggered wars in Libya, Syria and Yemen.

name: Gulf Cooperation Council
summary: Six-member Gulf political and economic union founded in 1981.

name: Battle of Lepanto
summary: Holy League naval victory over the Ottoman fleet that ended the myth of Ottoman invincibility at sea.

name: Camp David Accords
summary: Egyptian-Israeli peace brokered by Carter, returning Sinai to Egypt; Sadat was assassinated in 1981.

name: Kingdom of Bahrain
summary: Gulf island state independent in 1971 and a kingdom since 2002, host to the US Fifth Fleet.

name: State of Kuwait
summary: Oil-rich Gulf emirate independent from Britain in 1961, occupied by Iraq in 1990-91.

name: First Nagorno-Karabakh War
summary: War between Armenians and Azerbaijan over Karabakh that displaced about a million people.

name: Gulf War
summary: US-led coalition expelled Iraq from Kuwait after its August 1990 invasion.

name: Iran-Iraq War
summary: Eight-year war of attrition with chemical weapons and about a million casualties, ending in stalemate.

name: Anglo-Russian Convention
summary: Agreement dividing Persia into Russian and British spheres of influence.

name: Anglo-Soviet Invasion of Iran
summary: Allied occupation to secure oil and a supply corridor to the USSR, forcing Reza Shah's abdication.

name: Discovery of Oil in Persia
summary: Masjed Soleyman strike led to the Anglo-Persian Oil Company and a century of oil politics.

name: Iran Hostage Crisis
summary: 444-day seizure of the US embassy in Tehran that severed relations with Washington.

name: Iran Nuclear Deal
summary: JCPOA limiting Iran's nuclear programme for sanctions relief, abandoned by the United States in 2018.

name: Iranian Coup of 1953
summary: CIA and MI6 operation that removed Prime Minister Mosaddegh and restored the shah's power.

name: Iranian Green Movement
summary: Mass protests against a disputed presidential election, suppressed by security forces.

name: Iranian Oil Nationalisation
summary: Mosaddegh's nationalisation of the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company, met by boycott and covert action.

name: Iranian Revolution
summary: Mass movement that overthrew the shah and established an Islamic republic under Khomeini.

name: Leadership of Ali Khamenei
summary: Supreme leader since 1989, presiding over nuclear disputes, sanctions and protest movements.

name: Leadership of Ruhollah Khomeini
summary: Founder and first supreme leader, who institutionalised clerical rule and led the war with Iraq.

name: Mahsa Amini Protests
summary: Nationwide 'Woman, Life, Freedom' uprising after a young woman's death in morality police custody.

name: Reign of Mohammad Reza Pahlavi
summary: Last shah: oil nationalisation crisis, the 1953 coup, White Revolution, SAVAK repression and revolution.

name: Persian Constitutional Revolution
summary: Movement that won a constitution and the first Majlis, then was undermined by royal and foreign intervention.

name: Reign of Reza Shah Pahlavi
summary: Army officer turned shah who built railways, unveiled women and was deposed by the Allies in 1941.

name: Russo-Persian Wars
summary: Wars ending in the treaties of Gulistan and Turkmenchay, which ceded the Caucasus to Russia.

name: Reign of Shah Abbas I
summary: Reformed the army, retook lands from the Ottomans and Uzbeks, and rebuilt Isfahan.

name: Tobacco Protest
summary: Nationwide boycott led by clerics that forced cancellation of a British tobacco monopoly.

name: White Revolution
summary: Shah's programme of land reform, literacy and women's suffrage that also displaced rural populations.

name: Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
summary: Hashemite monarchy independent in 1946, host to large Palestinian refugee populations.

name: Emirate of Transjordan
summary: British-mandated Hashemite emirate under Abdullah I, independent as a kingdom in 1946.

name: Reign of King Hussein of Jordan
summary: Forty-six-year reign through the 1967 war, Black September and peace with Israel in 1994.

name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
summary: Absolute monarchy guarding Mecca and Medina, transformed by the world's largest conventional oil reserves.

name: Emirate of Diriyah
summary: First Saudi state, founded on the alliance of Muhammad ibn Saud and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, crushed by Egypt.

name: Seizure of the Grand Mosque
summary: Two-week takeover of the Kaaba compound by militants, after which the kingdom hardened religious policy.

name: Unification of Saudi Arabia
summary: Ibn Saud's campaigns from the recapture of Riyadh to the proclamation of the kingdom in 1932.

name: Rule of Mohammed bin Salman
summary: Crown prince driving Vision 2030 reforms, the Yemen war and a crackdown on dissent.

name: Reign of King Abdullah
summary: Cautious reformer who expanded education and faced the Arab Spring.

name: Reign of King Fahd
summary: King during the Gulf War, when US troops were stationed in the kingdom, and the Basic Law of 1992.

name: Reign of King Faisal
summary: Modernising king who led the 1973 oil embargo; assassinated by a nephew.

name: Discovery of Saudi Oil
summary: Dammam strike that made Saudi Arabia the centre of world oil and founded Aramco.

name: Emirate of Nejd
summary: Second Saudi state, based at Riyadh, overthrown by the Rashidis.

name: The Kurdish Question
summary: Statelessness of the Kurds after Sevres, with insurgencies and autonomy struggles in Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria.

name: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
summary: French League of Nations mandate that created the borders of modern Syria and Lebanon.

name: Ottoman Syria and the Levant
summary: Four centuries of Ottoman provincial rule over Syria, Lebanon, Palestine and Transjordan.

name: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
summary: Cartel founded in Baghdad that reshaped global energy politics, notably in the 1973 embargo.

name: Oslo Accords
summary: Israeli-Palestinian agreements creating the Palestinian Authority and mutual recognition.

name: Republic of Armenia
summary: Independent since 1991, shaped by the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict with Azerbaijan.

name: First Republic of Armenia
summary: Independent Armenia after Ottoman collapse, overwhelmed by Turkish and Soviet forces.

name: Republic of Azerbaijan
summary: Oil-rich Caspian republic independent in 1991, ruled by the Aliyev family since 1993.

name: Azerbaijan Democratic Republic
summary: First secular democratic republic in the Muslim world, sovietised in 1920.

name: Republic of Cyprus
summary: Independent from Britain in 1960, de facto divided since 1974 and an EU member since 2004.

name: Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus
summary: Self-declared state recognised only by Turkey.

name: Turkish Invasion of Cyprus
summary: Turkish intervention after a Greek-backed coup, dividing the island and creating a northern Turkish entity.

name: Georgia
summary: Independent since 1991; the Rose Revolution, the 2008 war with Russia and EU aspirations have defined it.

name: Democratic Republic of Georgia
summary: Independent Menshevik-led Georgia, invaded and sovietised by the Red Army in 1921.

name: Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti
summary: Unified eastern Georgian kingdom that sought Russian protection and was annexed by Russia in 1801.

name: Rose Revolution
summary: Peaceful protests that removed Eduard Shevardnadze and brought Mikheil Saakashvili to power.

name: Republic of Iraq
summary: Republic since 1958: Ba'athist rule, three wars, occupation and a federal constitution since 2005.

name: British Mandate for Mesopotamia
summary: British mandate over Iraq established after the Ottoman collapse, resisted in the 1920 revolt.

name: Iraq War
summary: US-led invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein, followed by insurgency, sectarian civil war and occupation.

name: Islamic State Caliphate
summary: Jihadist proto-state that seized Mosul and Raqqa before being destroyed by coalition and local forces.

name: Kingdom of Iraq
summary: Hashemite kingdom independent from 1932, overthrown in the bloody 1958 revolution.

name: Kurdistan Region of Iraq
summary: Autonomous Kurdish region established under no-fly-zone protection and constitutionally recognised in 2005.

name: Rule of Saddam Hussein
summary: Ba'athist dictator: war with Iran, gassing of Kurds, invasion of Kuwait and overthrow by US-led invasion.

name: Lebanese Republic
summary: Independent confessional republic, shaped by civil war, Syrian tutelage and economic collapse.

name: Israeli Invasion of Lebanon
summary: Invasion to expel the PLO, the siege of Beirut and the Sabra and Shatila massacre.

name: Lebanese Civil War
summary: Fifteen-year multi-sided war with Syrian and Israeli intervention, ending in the Taif Agreement.

name: Emirate of Mount Lebanon
summary: Autonomous Druze and Maronite emirate under Ottoman suzerainty, notably under Fakhr al-Din II.

name: Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate
summary: Autonomous Christian-governed Ottoman province created after the 1860 civil war under European pressure.

name: Republic of Turkey
summary: Secular republic founded by Ataturk on 29 October 1923, a NATO member since 1952.

name: Abolition of the Ottoman Sultanate and Caliphate
summary: The sultanate ended in 1922 and the caliphate in 1924, closing six centuries of Ottoman rule.

name: Presidency of Mustafa Kemal Ataturk
summary: Founding president who abolished the caliphate, latinised the alphabet, secularised law and enfranchised women.

name: Erdogan Era
summary: Prime minister then president since 2003: economic growth, Islamic conservatism, the 2016 coup attempt and executive presidency.

name: Presidency of Ismet Inonu
summary: Kept Turkey neutral in the Second World War and permitted the transition to multiparty democracy.

name: Treaty of Lausanne
summary: Settlement recognising the Turkish republic's borders and mandating population exchange with Greece.

name: Turkish Coup Attempt of 2016
summary: Failed military putsch followed by mass purges and a state of emergency.

name: Turkish Military Coups
summary: Interventions in 1960, 1971, 1980 and 1997 that repeatedly reset Turkish politics.

name: Turkish War of Independence
summary: Kemal's nationalist campaign against Greek, Armenian and French forces that saved Anatolian sovereignty.

name: Republic of Yemen
summary: Unified in 1990, since 2014 divided by civil war and Saudi-led intervention.

name: Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen
summary: Zaydi imamate in North Yemen, overthrown in the 1962 revolution.

name: People's Democratic Republic of Yemen
summary: Marxist state based at Aden after British withdrawal, merged with the north in 1990.

name: Yemeni Civil War
summary: Houthi takeover of Sanaa and Saudi-led intervention producing a severe humanitarian crisis.

name: Russo-Georgian War
summary: Five-day war over South Ossetia and Abkhazia that Russia won and followed by recognising both.

name: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
summary: Forty-four-day Azerbaijani victory that recovered most occupied territory; Karabakh fell entirely in 2023.

name: Six-Day War
summary: Israeli victory over Egypt, Jordan and Syria that took Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, Jerusalem and the Golan.

name: State of Israel
summary: Jewish state declared on 14 May 1948, which has fought repeated wars with its neighbours and Palestinians.

name: Premiership of David Ben-Gurion
summary: Founding prime minister who built state institutions, absorbed mass immigration and led the 1956 Sinai campaign.

name: Zionist Movement
summary: Political movement founded at Basel by Herzl to establish a Jewish state, realised in 1948.

name: State of Palestine
summary: Declared in 1988 and recognised by most UN members; a UN observer state since 2012.

name: Arab Revolt in Palestine
summary: Palestinian rebellion against British rule and Jewish immigration, suppressed with heavy casualties.

name: Balfour Declaration
summary: British pledge to favour a Jewish national home in Palestine while protecting non-Jewish rights.

name: First Intifada
summary: Palestinian mass uprising in the occupied territories, ended by the Oslo process.

name: Israeli Disengagement from Gaza
summary: Israel withdrew settlers and soldiers from Gaza, which Hamas took over in 2007.

name: Gaza War
summary: War following the Hamas attack of 7 October 2023, with devastating destruction and casualties in Gaza.

name: Mandatory Palestine
summary: British League of Nations mandate under the Balfour Declaration's terms, ending in war and partition.

name: Palestinian Authority
summary: Interim self-governing body in the West Bank and, until 2007, Gaza.

name: Palestine Liberation Organization
summary: Umbrella national movement led by Yasser Arafat from 1969, recognised as the Palestinian representative.

name: Second Intifada
summary: Violent uprising with suicide bombings and Israeli reoccupation, followed by the separation barrier.

name: United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine
summary: Resolution 181 recommended Jewish and Arab states with international status for Jerusalem.

name: State of Qatar
summary: Gas-rich emirate independent in 1971, home to Al Jazeera and host of the 2022 World Cup.

name: Sultanate of Oman
summary: Al Bu Said sultanate that once ruled Zanzibar, modernised after Sultan Qaboos took power in 1970.

name: Dhofar Rebellion
summary: Leftist insurgency in southern Oman defeated with British and Iranian help.

name: Sykes-Picot Agreement
summary: Secret Anglo-French plan to divide Ottoman Arab lands, the basis of later mandate borders.

name: Syrian Arab Republic
summary: Independent from France in 1946; Ba'athist from 1963, ruled by the Assads from 1970 to 2024.

name: Rule of Bashar al-Assad
summary: Presidency that met the 2011 uprising with war, chemical attacks and displacement, ending in his flight in December 2024.

name: Fall of the Assad Regime
summary: Rebel offensive that captured Damascus in December 2024 and ended 54 years of Assad family rule.

name: Rule of Hafez al-Assad
summary: Thirty years of Ba'athist Alawite-led authoritarian rule, including the 1982 Hama massacre.

name: Syrian Civil War
summary: Uprising turned multi-sided war with Russian, Iranian, Turkish and US involvement and over half a million dead.

name: United Arab Emirates
summary: Federation of seven emirates formed on British withdrawal, now a global trade and finance hub.

name: Yom Kippur War
summary: Egyptian and Syrian surprise attack on Israel that led to the oil embargo and eventually to peace talks.
